export function checksumRows(bytes) {
  assert.ok(Buffer.isBuffer(bytes) && bytes.length > 0 && bytes.length <= 1024 * 1024);
  const text = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {
    fatal: true
  }).decode(bytes);
  const rows = new Map();
  for (const line of text.trimEnd().split(/\r?\n/u)) {
    const match = /^([a-f0-9]{64})  ([A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*)$/u.exec(line);
    assert.ok(match, 'invalid checksum row');
    assert.ok(!rows.has(match[2]), 'duplicate checksum row');
    rows.set(match[2], match[1]);
  }
  return rows;
}

test('complete verification overlaps public streams with a fixed bound and stores only evidence', async t => {
  const { directory, bodies, selection } = transferFixture(t);
  let active = 0;
  let peak = 0;
  const responseOrder = [];
  t.mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async url => {
    const name = new URL(url).pathname.split('/').at(-1);
    active++;
    peak = Math.max(peak, active);
    await setImmediate();
    if (name === selection.assets[0].name) await setImmediate();
    active--;
    responseOrder.push(name);
    return new Response(bodies.get(name));
  });
  const evidence = await runVerification({ selection, outputDirectory: directory });
  assert.ok(peak > 1 && peak <= 3, 'expected bounded, overlapping public downloads');
  assert.notEqual(responseOrder[0], selection.assets[0].name);
  assert.deepEqual(evidence.downloads.map(item => item.name), [...bodies.keys()]);
  assert.equal(evidence.coverage.byteVerifiedAssets, bodies.size);
  assert.equal(evidence.publicationAuthority, false);
  assert.deepEqual(fs.readFileSync(join(directory, 'BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt')), bodies.get('BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt'));
  for (const name of expected) {
    if (/\\\\.(?:tgz|tar\\\\.gz|AppImage|dmg|zip|deb|exe)$/u.test(name)) {
      assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, name)), false, name);
    }
  }
});
test('failed public transfer identifies its asset and retains only verified progress', async t => {
  const { directory, bodies, selection } = transferFixture(t);
  const rejected = selection.assets[1].name;
  t.mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async url => {
    const name = new URL(url).pathname.split('/').at(-1);
    return new Response(name === rejected ? Buffer.alloc(bodies.get(name).length) : bodies.get(name));
  });
  await assert.rejects(runVerification({ selection, outputDirectory: directory }), error => {
    return error.message.includes(rejected) && /digest mismatch/u.test(error.message);
  });
  const progress = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(join(directory, 'download-observations.json')));
  assert.equal(progress.verificationComplete, false);
  assert.ok(progress.downloads.some(item => item.name === 'BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt'));
  assert.ok(!progress.downloads.some(item => item.name === rejected));
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, 'download-evidence.json')), false);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, rejected)), false);

import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { setImmediate } from 'node:timers/promises';""").replace("assessCoverage, macosAssetNames, MAX_ASSET_BYTES", "assessCoverage, macosAssetNames, runVerification, MAX_ASSET_BYTES")

s = s[:start] + """function transferFixture(t) {
  const directory = fs.mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), 'formal-ai-release-verification-'));
  t.after(() => fs.rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true }));
  const digest = bytes => createHash('sha256').update(bytes).digest('hex');
  const names = ['BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt', ...expected];
  const bodies = new Map(names.map(name => [name, Buffer.from(name)]));
  const checksums = expected.map(name => digest(bodies.get(name)) + '  ' + name).join('\\\\n');
  bodies.set('SHA256SUMS.txt', Buffer.from(checksums + '\\\\n'));
  const assets = Array.from(bodies, ([name, bytes], index) => ({
    ...asset(name, index + 1),
    size: bytes.length,
    digest: 'sha256:' + digest(bytes)
  }));
  return {
    directory,
    bodies,
    selection: { repository, tag, definition, assets, releaseId: 10 }
  };
}
test('complete verification overlaps public streams with a fixed bound and stores only evidence', async t => {
  const { directory, bodies, selection } = transferFixture(t);
  let active = 0;
  let peak = 0;
  const responseOrder = [];
  t.mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async url => {
    const name = new URL(url).pathname.split('/').at(-1);
    active++;
    peak = Math.max(peak, active);
    await setImmediate();
    if (name === selection.assets[0].name) await setImmediate();
    active--;
    responseOrder.push(name);
    return new Response(bodies.get(name));
  });
  const evidence = await runVerification({ selection, outputDirectory: directory });
  assert.ok(peak > 1 && peak <= 3, 'expected bounded, overlapping public downloads');
  assert.notEqual(responseOrder[0], selection.assets[0].name);
  assert.deepEqual(evidence.downloads.map(item => item.name), [...bodies.keys()]);
  assert.equal(evidence.coverage.byteVerifiedAssets, bodies.size);
  assert.equal(evidence.publicationAuthority, false);
  assert.deepEqual(fs.readFileSync(join(directory, 'BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt')), bodies.get('BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt'));
  for (const name of expected) {
    if (/\\\\.(?:tgz|tar\\\\.gz|AppImage|dmg|zip|deb|exe)$/u.test(name)) {
      assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, name)), false, name);
    }
  }
});
test('failed public transfer identifies its asset and retains only verified progress', async t => {
  const { directory, bodies, selection } = transferFixture(t);
  const rejected = selection.assets[1].name;
  t.mock.method(globalThis, 'fetch', async url => {
    const name = new URL(url).pathname.split('/').at(-1);
    return new Response(name === rejected ? Buffer.alloc(bodies.get(name).length) : bodies.get(name));
  });
  await assert.rejects(runVerification({ selection, outputDirectory: directory }), error => {
    return error.message.includes(rejected) && /digest mismatch/u.test(error.message);
  });
  const progress = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(join(directory, 'download-observations.json')));
  assert.equal(progress.verificationComplete, false);
  assert.ok(progress.downloads.some(item => item.name === 'BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt'));
  assert.ok(!progress.downloads.some(item => item.name === rejected));
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, 'download-evidence.json')), false);
  assert.equal(fs.existsSync(join(directory, rejected)), false);
});

## The single push gate (issue #1191)
Every push starts the whole pull-request matrix again. A push that fixes only
some of the previous run's failures pays that cost once per round trip.
Pull request #1188 needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of
them was green. Human and AI contributors therefore follow one push gate, which
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) restates for agents:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** They commit locally or hand back a diff.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** That agent first collects every
   actionable failure of the latest run on the current head
   (`gh run list --branch <branch>`, then `gh run view <id> --log-failed`). It
   fixes all of them in one batch and pushes once.

   `gh run list --branch <branch> --status in_progress` and `--status queued`

/** Reject unsupported encoding instead of replacing source characters.
 * @param {string} file @returns {string} */
export function readSourceText(file) {
  const status = fs.lstatSync(file);
  if (!status.isFile() || status.isSymbolicLink()) throw Error('RegularSourceFileRequired');
  if (status.size > 4 * 1024 * 1024) throw Error('SourceModelInputBudgetExceeded');
  return new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}).decode(fs.readFileSync(file));
}

+async function listCheckRunAnnotations(api, repo, checkRunId) {
+  const path = `repos/${repo}/check-runs/${checkRunId}/annotations`;
+  const pageSize = 100;
+  const annotations = [];
+  for (let page = 1; page <= 10; page++) {
+    const items = await api(`${path}?per_page=${pageSize}&page=${page}`);
+    if (!Array.isArray(items) || items.length > pageSize)
+      throw Error(
+        `Expected an array of annotations (up to ${pageSize}) for ${path}, page ${page}`,
+      );
+    annotations.push(...items);
+    if (items.length < pageSize) return annotations;
+  }
+  throw Error(`Annotation pagination limit reached for ${path} after 10 full pages`);
+}

pub fn with_retries<T>(
    attempts: u32,
    delay: Duration,
    mut operation: impl FnMut() -> Result<T, Failure>,
) -> Result<T, String> {
    if !(1..=10).contains(&attempts) {
        return Err("Registry attempts must be between 1 and 10".into());
    }
    for attempt in 1..=attempts {
        match operation() {
            Ok(value) => return Ok(value),
            Err(Failure::Permanent(error)) => return Err(error),
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) if attempt == attempts => {
                return Err(format!("{error} (after {attempts} attempts)"));
            }
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) => {
                eprintln!("Registry lookup retry {}/{attempts}: {error}", attempt + 1);
                std::thread::sleep(delay * 2_u32.pow(attempt - 1));
            }
        }
    }
    unreachable!()
}

use std::time::Duration;
// Keep rust-script from wrapping this shared module as an expression.
#[cfg(test)]
fn main() {}
#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Failure {
    Transient(String),
    Permanent(String),
}
pub fn with_retries<T>(
    attempts: u32,
    delay: Duration,
    mut operation: impl FnMut() -> Result<T, Failure>,
) -> Result<T, String> {
    if !(1..=10).contains(&attempts) {
        return Err("Registry attempts must be between 1 and 10".into());
    }
    for attempt in 1..=attempts {
        match operation() {
            Ok(value) => return Ok(value),
            Err(Failure::Permanent(error)) => return Err(error),
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) if attempt == attempts => {
                return Err(format!("{error} (after {attempts} attempts)"));
            }
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) => {
                eprintln!("Registry lookup retry {}/{attempts}: {error}", attempt + 1);
                std::thread::sleep(delay * 2_u32.pow(attempt - 1));
            }
        }
    }
    unreachable!()
}

use std::time::Duration;
// Keep rust-script from wrapping this shared module as an expression.

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum Failure {
    Transient(String),
    Permanent(String),
}
pub fn with_retries<T>(
    attempts: u32,
    delay: Duration,
    mut operation: impl FnMut() -> Result<T, Failure>,
) -> Result<T, String> {
    if !(1..=10).contains(&attempts) {
        return Err("Registry attempts must be between 1 and 10".into());
    }
    for attempt in 1..=attempts {
        match operation() {
            Ok(value) => return Ok(value),
            Err(Failure::Permanent(error)) => return Err(error),
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) if attempt == attempts => {
                return Err(format!("{error} (after {attempts} attempts)"));
            }
            Err(Failure::Transient(error)) => {
                eprintln!("Registry lookup retry {}/{attempts}: {error}", attempt + 1);
                std::thread::sleep(delay * 2_u32.pow(attempt - 1));
            }
        }
    }
    unreachable!()
}

/// Measure the files under `cwd`, or only those in `listed` when it is given.
/// A file git ignores can never be committed (a local session transcript, a
/// sandbox), so inside a work tree the gate measures what a commit can carry,
/// the same files CI's checkout holds.
fn check_listed_files(cwd: &Path, listed: Option<&BTreeSet<String>>) -> CheckResult {
    let mut result = CheckResult {
        warnings: Vec::new(),
        violations: Vec::new(),
        embedded_data_violations: Vec::new(),
        errors: Vec::new(),
    };

    for entry in WalkDir::new(cwd).into_iter().filter_entry(|entry| {
        entry.depth() == 0
            || !entry.file_type().is_dir()

                && listed_directories.as_ref().is_none_or(|directories| {
                    directories.contains(&relative_path(entry.path(), cwd))
                }))
    }) {
        let entry = match entry {
            Ok(entry) => entry,
            Err(error) => {
                let message = format!("Error: {error}");
                eprintln!("{}", safe_log_text(&message));
                result.errors.push(message);
                continue;
            }
        };
        if !entry.file_type().is_file() {
            continue;

fn warnings_for_growing_paths<'a>(
    warnings: &'a [Finding],
    growing_paths: &[String],
) -> Vec<&'a Finding> {
    warnings
        .iter()
        .filter(|finding| growing_paths.contains(&finding.file))
        .collect()
}
/// Parse git diff --numstat -z, retaining literal names and rename destinations.
/// An incomplete inventory falls back to reporting every size warning.
fn growing_paths_from_numstat(numstat: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    if numstat.is_empty() {
        return Some(Vec::new());
    }
    let mut records = numstat.strip_suffix('\0')?.split('\0');
    let mut growing = Vec::new();
    while let Some(header) = records.next() {
        let mut fields = header.splitn(3, '\t');
        let added = fields.next()?;
        let removed = fields.next()?;
        let mut path = fields.next()?;
        if path.is_empty() {
            let previous = records.next()?;
            path = records.next()?;
            if previous.is_empty() || path.is_empty() {
                return None;
            }
        }
        if added == "-" && removed == "-" {
            continue;
        }
        let added = added.parse::<u64>().ok()?;
        let removed = removed.parse::<u64>().ok()?;
        // Match the JavaScript twin's exact integer domain.
        if added > 9_007_199_254_740_991 || removed > 9_007_199_254_740_991 {
            return None;
        }
        if added > removed {
            growing.push(path.to_string());
        }
    }
    Some(growing)
}

//! Rust package path detection utility
//!
//! Automatically detects the Rust package root for both:
//! - Single-language repositories (Cargo.toml in root)
//! - Multi-language repositories (Cargo.toml in rust/ subfolder)

//! Usage (as library - import functions from this module):

//!   1. Explicit parameter passed to functions
//!   2. CLI argument: --rust-root <path>

//! ```cargo

//! Release-note selection shared by the publishing CLI and native contracts.
//! Fence scanning follows the Unlicense Rust pipeline template,
//! 5f1e7a96acbf7a93b567195443cf6e5158fbbf1f, scripts/release-content.rs.
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
#[cfg(test)]
#[allow(dead_code)]
fn main() {}
fn markdown_line(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let trimmed = line.trim_start_matches(' ');
    (line.len() - trimmed.len() <= 3).then_some(trimmed)
}
fn release_heading(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let (version, suffix) = line.strip_prefix("## [")?.split_once(']')?;
    if version.is_empty()
        || !suffix
            .as_bytes()
            .first()
            .is_none_or(|b| matches!(b, b' ' | b'\t'))
    {
        return None;
    }
    Some(version)
}
/// Byte offsets of actual release headings, ignoring fenced examples.
fn headings(content: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = (usize, usize, &str)> {

mod github_output;
use github_output::set_output;
#[path = "rust-paths.rs"]
mod rust_paths;
fn main() {
    let rust_root = match rust_paths::get_rust_root(None, true) {
        Ok(root) => root,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("Error: {}", e);
            exit(1);
        }
    };
    let cargo_toml = rust_paths::get_cargo_toml_path(&rust_root);
    let package_manifest = match rust_paths::get_package_manifest_path(&cargo_toml) {
        Ok(path) => path,
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("Error: {}", e);
            exit(1);
        }
    };
    match rust_paths::read_package_info(&package_manifest) {
        Ok(info) => {
            println!("Current version: {}", info.version);
            set_output("version", &info.version);
        }
        Err(e) => {
            eprintln!("Error: {}", e);
            exit(1);
        }
    }

    language, repository, old, new = details_line.split('\\t')
    previous = next(t for t in prior_summary['templates'] if t['language'] == language)
    former = prior[language]
    assert previous['head'] == old and len(former) == previous['blobs']
    if old == new:
        current = former
        changed = []
    else:
        tree = json.loads((source / f'{language}-tree.json').read_text())
        assert tree['truncated'] is False
        current = {row['path']: row['sha'] for row in tree['tree'] if row['type'] == 'blob'}
        delta, = json.loads((source / f'{language}-compare.json').read_text())
        assert delta['base_commit']['sha'] == delta['merge_base_commit']['sha'] == old

        actual = {path for path in former.keys() | current.keys() if former.get(path) != current.get(path)}
        assert actual == {row['filename'] for row in delta['files']} == details[language].keys()

                'newGitBlob': current[path],
                'patchSha256': hashlib.sha256(patch).hexdigest(),

            })

                'path': path,
                'patch': row['patch'],

    reports.append({

        'priorHead': old,

        'unchangedBlobs': len(current) - len(changed),
        'changed': changed,
    })
assert len(reports) == len(prior) == 8
assert sum(len(record['changed']) for record in reports) == len(patches) == 19

## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

+# Template source changes on 24 November 2026
+
+The latest comparison covers 3,030 blob paths across all eight templates. JavaScript, Python, PHP, Java and Go stayed at their previously compared commits. The Rust, C# and C++ trees changed 11, three and five paths respectively, with two added files and no removed files. The receipt matches all 19 paths against GitHub's complete recursive trees and compare responses, records their Git blob IDs and retains the complete changed-file patches. [Comparison receipt](current-tree-delta-20261124.json) · [Source patches](current-tree-delta-20261124-patches.jsonl.gz)
+
+The C# and C++ templates adopted check-run annotation pagination. The Formal AI production recovery helper already follows both job and annotation pages, verifies the check-run identity and blocks retries when a real test started. [C# template PR #115](https://github.com/link-foundation/csharp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/115) · [C++ template PR #43](https://github.com/link-foundation/cpp-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/43) · [Formal AI recovery regression](../../../../experiments/issue-1580/runner-acquisition-recovery.test.mjs)
+
+The Rust template changed five production paths. Formal AI already reports incomplete file-size scans, drains the GitHub CLI's output while writing its request, and allows only spaces and tabs after a Markdown closing fence. Its manifest selector already propagates errors reading existing workspace members. The native version CLI fixture now checks a missing first member followed by a valid one, then places invalid UTF-8 in the first manifest and expects a fatal read error with no output. [Rust template PR #267](https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/pull/267) · [File-size controls](../../../../scripts/check-file-size/tests.rs) · [Release-pipe control](../../../../experiments/issue-1580/release-registry/release_process_regressions.py) · [Markdown controls](../../../../scripts/release-changelog/tests.rs) · [Manifest CLI control](../../../../experiments/issue-1580/release-registry/cli_regressions.py)
+
+Formal AI's crate waiter could previously report that a release was absent when one registry endpoint returned invalid data with HTTP 200 and the other returned HTTP 404. It also accepted a matching version with the wrong API crate name, and an index row with invalid SemVer could pass beside an exact match. The repair decodes the full response as UTF-8, validates every sparse row and checks the API crate name when present. A valid exact match can settle availability after a failed observation. A malformed success leaves availability uncertain when the peer supplies only evidence of absence.
+
+To reproduce, the native CLI test runs the waiter with two bounded attempts against a loopback registry. It builds the archived pre-fix registry module from commit `02b4076e7` and the revised source against the same inputs. The six failing cases cover invalid JSON and UTF-8 on both endpoints, a malformed indexed version after an exact match, and a matching API version for the wrong crate. The revised waiter is expected to produce an uncertainty diagnostic and leave `GITHUB_OUTPUT` absent. The positive controls exercise case-insensitive crate identity, a valid beta version with build metadata, and ordinary absence when the peer returns a transient HTTP error. GitHub Actions runs these binaries through the existing release-registry job. [Native CLI controls](../../../../experiments/issue-1580/release-registry/sparse_registry_regressions.py)
+
+The local JavaScript admission suite passed all 68 checks after a new assertion failed against the pre-fix source. Rust formatting, Python parsing and the isolated Cargo lock update passed. The lock added only SemVer 1.0.28. Native compilation and runtime verification of these controls require the hosted release-registry job. The source refresh leaves wider practice acceptance open and adds zero independent Formal AI authorship or reasoning credit.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-secrets.sh
#
# Scans the files a change touches for committed credentials, using secretlint
# with the recommended preset (CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 11 / issue #808).
#
# Usage:
#   BASE_REF=main bash scripts/check-secrets.sh     # scan the diff vs BASE_REF
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh --all             # scan every tracked file
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh path/to/file ...  # scan specific files
#
# Exit code 0 = no secrets found; non-zero = a finding or scanner failure.
#
# Why the diff and not the whole tree
# -----------------------------------
# The js template runs `secretlint "**/*"`. Measured on this repository that
# does not finish in a usable time: the glob walks the working tree (including
# `target/` and ~150 MB of committed case-study logs) and the scan was still
# running after 25 minutes locally. A gate that cannot be relied on to finish is
# a new CI failure mode, which is the opposite of what issue #808 asks for.
#
# Scanning what the change touches keeps the gate fast and catches the case that
# matters: a credential being *introduced*. Pre-existing files are not re-scanned
# on every pull request; run `--all` (no timeout) to audit the whole tree.
#
# FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG=[REDACTED] prints the resolved file list before scanning.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
debug() {
  if [ "${FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG:[REDACTED]}" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[check-secrets] %s\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}
# Captured third-party CI/agent logs kept verbatim as evidence. They are
# reviewed when added and consist of redacted GitHub Actions output.
exclude() {
  local status=0
  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Externally supplied commands receive zero autonomous-authorship credit.
import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';
import {mkdirSync,writeFileSync} from 'node:fs';
import {resolve} from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL} from 'node:url';
// Tool result lines are indented by drive.mjs; only its top-level boundary
// ends the transcript. Source bytes may contain the same marker or exit text.
export function reviewCommandResult(result, shellCommand) {
  const stdout = result.stdout ?? '';
  const boundary = /^== answer ==\r?$/mu.exec(stdout);
  const trace = boundary ? stdout.slice(0, boundary.index) : stdout;
  const headers = [...trace.matchAll(/^>> (\S+) ([^\r\n]*)\r?$/gmu)];
  let arguments_, receipt;
  if (headers.length === 1 && trace.slice(0, headers[0].index) === '') {
    try { arguments_ = JSON.parse(headers[0][2]); } catch { /* Invalid arguments earn no execution credit. */ }
    const body = trace.slice(headers[0].index + headers[0][0].length);
    // shell-capture.mjs appends the actual status after all stdout/stderr.
    // A preview, signal or JSON error capture has no such complete footer.
    if (body.startsWith('\n   Output: ')) receipt = /\n   Exit Code: (\d{1,3})\r?\n?$/u.exec(body);
  }
  const exact = headers.length === 1 && headers[0][1] === 'bash'
    && arguments_ !== null && typeof arguments_ === 'object' && !Array.isArray(arguments_)
    && Object.keys(arguments_).length === 1 && arguments_.command === shellCommand;
  const code = receipt ? Number(receipt[1]) : null;
  const driverSucceeded = result.status === 0 && !result.signal && !result.error;
  const qualified = boundary !== null && exact && code !== null && code <= 255;
  const exitCode = !driverSucceeded
    ? (Number.isInteger(result.status) && result.status > 0 ? result.status : 1)
    : qualified ? code : 1;
  return {trace, exact, exitCode};
}

A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.\n\n**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:\n\n```\n ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)\n```\n\nThe bullets above without this one convert \"two writers collide\" into \"the second writer reliably fails\" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.\n\n**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.\n\n**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — \"Changes must be made through a pull request\") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.\n\n```js\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {\n  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);\n  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };\n  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.\n  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });\n  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.\n  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);\n  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);\n}\n```\n\n- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.\n- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.\n- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.\n- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.\n\n#### Preserve a full check when a commit arrives\n\nGroup commit checks by workflow and PR and cancel only superseded `synchronize` runs. Keep the shared non-cancelling group for publishing and deployment jobs. Workflow-level cancellation is safe only when every event eligible for cancellation runs checks without publishing or deploying. Secrets Detection\n\nPrevent accidental credential leaks in CI:\n\n- Include a secrets scan step using tools like `secretlint` or `truffleHog`\n- Fail CI immediately if secrets are detected\n- Never log environment variables or token values\n\n### 12. Documentation Validation\n\n**Validate documentation files in CI just like code:**\n\n- Check file size limits (e.g., max 2500 lines for docs)\n- Verify required sections exist in key documents\n- Check for broken links using tools like `lychee`\n\n```yaml\nvalidate-docs:\n  needs: [detect-changes]\n  if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.docs-changed == 'true'\n  steps:\n    - run: node tests/docs-validation.mjs\n```\n\n### 13. Container Images: Native Runners per Architecture\n\n**Build each architecture on its own native runner.** GitHub provides free arm64 Linux runners for public repositories (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Emulating arm64 with QEMU on an x86 runner is much slower for compiled languages, and building two architectures inside one job makes them sequential instead of parallel.\n\n```yaml\nbuild-image:\n  strategy:\n    matrix:\n      include:\n        - platform: linux/amd64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04\n        - platform: linux/arm64\n          runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm\n  runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}\n  steps:\n    - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7\n      with:\n        platforms: ${{ matrix.platform }}\n        cache-from: type=gha\n        cache-to: type=gha,mode=max\n        outputs: type=image,push-by-digest=true,name-canonical=true,push=true\n\nmerge-manifest:\n  needs: [build-image]\n  steps:\n    - run: docker buildx imagetools create -t $IMAGE:$VERSION $DIGESTS\n```\n\n- **No `setup-qemu-action`.** Its presence means an architecture is being emulated; use a native runner instead.\n- **Publish images for every architecture your users run.** A single-architecture image silently excludes Apple Silicon, Graviton, and arm CI runners.\n- **Always cache.** Set `cache-from: type=gha` and `cache-to: type=gha,mode=max` on every build step; otherwise every architecture rebuilds the full dependency tree for every release.\n- **Never gate the release on the image push.** Publish the GitHub Release and language-registry package first, then attach images as they finish. Release notes contain no data derived from image bytes, so a slow or failed registry push must not hide an otherwise completed release.\n- **Assert what you shipped.** Verify that the published manifest lists every intended platform and that each default-branch tag has a corresponding GitHub Release; a missing release is otherwise easy to overlook.\n\nReference implementations: [`link-foundation/box`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box) and [`link-assistant/hive-mind`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind).\n\n### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves\n\n**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.\n\nTwo complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:\n\n- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.\n- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.\n\n```yaml\n- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12\n  with:\n    args: -color\n```\n\n- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.\n- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.\n- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.\n- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.\n\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 \"Dependabot is rebasing this PR\" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).\n- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).\n- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. The `fix` command automates the whole flow:\n\n```bash\nfix https://github.com/owner/repo --ci-cd\n```\n\nThis command:\n\n1. **Detects the repository's languages** using the GitHub Linguist API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/languages`), ordered by the number of bytes per language.\n2. **Selects the matching CI/CD templates** from the table above, sorted so the template for the most-used language comes first.\n3. **Inspects the latest default-branch run of every active workflow** by enumerating the workflow inventory, reading each workflow's time-ordered runs, and validating `head_branch` locally (GitHub's workflow-specific branch index can lag). This catches a failed required workflow on an earlier commit even when a busy workflow fills GitHub's 1,000-result combined-history window or the latest commit has unrelated passing runs, without permanently reporting a deleted workflow's last failure. If an inventory or per-workflow query fails, it falls back to paginated combined branch history; the exact latest-commit query is used only when branch history has no active runs.\n4. **Creates a remediation issue** that lists the failing runs, the detected languages, the recommended templates, and a link back to this document. The issue is created as a **Bug** (with a `bug` label) and its title and text are taken from the [standard remediation template](https://github.com/link-assistant/web-capture/issues/139).\n5. **Hands the issue off to `/solve --development-log --deep-analysis --auto-merge`**, which iterates until the fixes are merged. Every option `fix` does not consume itself (for example `--tool`, `--model`, `--think`) is forwarded to `/solve`.\n\n### Why the issue is a Bug, and what it leaves out\n\n`--development-log` replaces the template's retired case-study-folder instruction and collects artifacts under `./dev/log/issues/{issue-id}/pulls/{pull-id}`. `/fix` never emits the retired paragraph, including with `--no-solve` or partial option sets. `--deep-analysis` supplies the timeline, root-cause, debug-output, and upstream-reporting guidance, so `fix` conditionally omits the matching paragraphs instead of delivering them twice.\n\nThat omission is only lossless because `/solve` emits the root-cause wording **only for bug-typed issues** — which is why `fix` creates the issue as a Bug. Issue types are configured per organization and labels per repository, so if the target repository accepts neither, the issue is still created without them.\n\nThe retired paragraph cannot be restored by an option combination; `--development-log` is the only supported collection workflow. The remaining conditional omissions are controlled by `--deep-analysis`.\n\n### Language → Template Mapping\n\nThe command maps detected languages to templates as follows (JavaScript and TypeScript share a single template, and so do C, C++ and CMake):\n\n| Detected Language(s)  | Template                                                         |\n| --------------------- | # CI/CD Best Practices for AI-Driven Development (languages: en • [zh](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.zh.md) • [hi](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.hi.md) • [ru](CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.ru.md))
This document describes CI/CD best practices that significantly improve the quality and reliability of AI-driven development workflows. When properly configured, Hive Mind AI solvers are forced to iterate with CI/CD checks until all tests pass, ensuring code quality meets the highest standards.
## Why CI/CD Matters for AI Development
Hive Mind's AI issue solver is instructed to pay attention to CI/CD checks in each pull request. This creates a powerful feedback loop:
1. **AI creates a solution** - The solver generates code based on issue requirements
2. **CI/CD validates the solution** - Automated checks verify code quality
3. **AI iterates until passing** - The solver fixes issues until all checks pass
4. **Quality is guaranteed** - No code merges without passing all gates
This approach ensures consistent quality regardless of whether the team consists of humans, AIs, or both.

Use `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.
**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:
```
 ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)
```
The bullets above without this one convert "two writers collide" into "the second writer reliably fails" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.
**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.
**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — "Changes must be made through a pull request") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). ## Quality Enforcement Strategy
The templates implement a defense-in-depth approach:
```
Developer Machine    →    CI/CD Pipeline    →    Release
├── Pre-commit hooks      ├── detect-changes      ├── All checks pass
├── Local tests           ├── version-check       ├── Version bump
└── IDE integration       ├── changeset-check     ├── Changelog update
                          ├── test-compilation    └── Publish package
                          ├── lint (format+ESLint)
                          ├── check-file-line-limits
                          ├── test-suites
                          ├── test-execution
                          ├── validate-docs
                          └── docker-pr-check
```
Each layer catches different issues, ensuring no problematic code reaches production.
## Getting Started
1. **Choose a template** from the table above matching your language
2. **Use it as a GitHub template** to create your new repository
3. **Configure secrets** if needed for publishing (OIDC preferred)
4. **Start developing** with the template workflows
The AI solvers will automatically respect and iterate with all configured checks, producing higher quality output than repositories without CI/CD enforcement.

Preserve full checks for ready PRs and each `main` revision. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.\n- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.\n- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.\n- **Workflow scope:** Allow workflow-level cancellation only for events that cannot publish, deploy, or change repository state. An active writer would also be interrupted if its workflow were cancelled.\n\nBy default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.\n\nUse `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.\n\n**Serialisation orders writers; it does not rebase them.** The concurrency group decides _when_ each writer runs, not _what_ it has checked out. `actions/checkout` checks out `github.sha` — the commit that triggered the run — so the second writer in the queue starts one or more commits behind the branch the instant the first one lands, and its push is rejected:\n\n```\n ! [rejected]        main -> main (non-fast-forward)\n```\n\nThe bullets above without this one convert \"two writers collide\" into \"the second writer reliably fails\" — better, because it is deterministic and loud, but still a broken release. `link-foundation/browser-commander` implemented the group to the letter (three language releases in three workflow files, zero overlap in their timings) and two of its three releases still ended on that line. Each run looked like ordinary flaky CI, so the damage accumulated unnoticed: the Rust crate reached 0.10.11 on crates.io while `Cargo.toml` on `main` still said 0.9.0, and the Python package was never published at all, because the job dies at a changelog push that sits before the publish step.\n\n**Do not fix it with `ref: main` on the checkout.** That silences the rejection by building, testing and publishing a tree that is not the tree CI validated, with nothing in the log to say so. The rejection is the honest outcome; what is missing is the recovery.\n\n**Give every write job a push that classifies the rejection, then rebases and retries.** A repository-ruleset rejection (GH006, GH013 — \"Changes must be made through a pull request\") also prints `[rejected]`, and no number of rebases can ever satisfy a rule; fail with the rule's output instead, so the rule gets fixed (see principle 9). Retrying it burns the queue slot and reports the wrong cause.\n\n```js\nfor (let attempt = 1; attempt <= maxAttempts; attempt++) {\n  const result = await run('git', ['push', remote, branch]);\n  if (result.code === 0) return { pushed: true, attempt };\n  // A rule can never be satisfied by a rebase: fail with the rule's output.\n  if (isBlockedByRepositoryRule(result)) throw repositoryRuleError({ branch, version, cause: result });\n  // Auth, network, a missing remote: rebasing would hide the real error.\n  if (!isNonFastForward(result) || attempt === maxAttempts) throw new CommandFailedError('git', ['push', remote, branch], result);\n  await run('git', ['pull', '--rebase', remote, branch]);\n}\n```\n\n- **Never `--force`, and never `--force-with-lease`, on a shared branch.** Both turn a lost race into a silent deletion of whatever the writer ahead of you landed. Rebasing is the point: the later commit has to end up on top of the earlier one.\n- **Recompute after the rebase whatever was derived before it.** A version number, a changelog entry or a tag chosen against the stale tip may already be taken by the writer that won the queue. Re-read the state instead of replaying the plan.\n- **Report success only after the push landed.** A step that sets `version_committed=true` before the push is confirmed leaves the downstream publish job working from a commit that exists only on that runner.\n- **Bound the retries and name the reason in the log.** A handful of attempts with a short delay covers a queue; an unbounded loop against a branch that is genuinely protected turns a fast failure into a long one.\n\n#### Preserve a full check when a commit arrives\n\nGroup commit checks by workflow and PR and cancel only superseded `synchronize` runs. Keep the shared non-cancelling group for publishing and deployment jobs. Workflow-level cancellation is safe only when every event eligible for cancellation runs checks without publishing or deploying. Container Images: Native Runners per Architecture\n\n**Build each architecture on its own native runner.** GitHub provides free arm64 Linux runners for public repositories (`ubuntu-24.04-arm`). Lint the Workflows Themselves\n\n**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.\n\nTwo complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:\n\n- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.\n- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.\n\n```yaml\n- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12\n  with:\n    args: -color\n```\n\n- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. - **Read-only jobs:** Cancel superseded commit-tier checks to reduce runner load. Preserve full checks for ready PRs and each `main` revision. Give each job a distinct suffix; include relevant matrix values so different matrix entries can still run in parallel.
- **Dependent writers:** Use `needs` and require successful prerequisites. A cancelled prerequisite must make its write job not start.
- **Active writers:** Give every release, deploy, tag, generated-content push, and other write job the same repository-scoped group with `cancel-in-progress: false`. An already started writer finishes while the next writer waits in the queue, including writers from another workflow file.
- **Workflow scope:** Allow workflow-level cancellation only for events that cannot publish, deploy, or change repository state. An active writer would also be interrupted if its workflow were cancelled.
By default, a concurrency group keeps at most one running and one pending job; a newer pending writer replaces the older pending writer. If every queued write must run, add `queue: max` to the writer's concurrency block (up to 100 jobs can wait). `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, and execution order follows when jobs start waiting rather than workflow dispatch order, so write jobs should remain idempotent. See [GitHub's concurrency documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-when-workflows-run/control-workflow-concurrency) for the current queue limits and semantics.
Use `!cancelled()` instead of `always()` in job conditions so cancellation propagates correctly through the job graph. A bare `always()` can keep downstream work running after cancellation.

forwarded its selected token to Cargo with two process arguments. It also warned

## Trusted Publishing Enhancements
In our July 2025 update, we announced Trusted Publishing support for GitHub Actions. Since then, we have made several enhancements to this feature.
### GitLab CI/CD Support
Trusted Publishing now supports GitLab CI/CD in addition to GitHub Actions. This allows GitLab users to publish crates without managing API tokens, using the same OIDC-based authentication flow.
Note that this currently only works with GitLab.com. Self-hosted GitLab instances are not supported yet. The crates.io implementation has been refactored to support multiple CI providers, so adding support for other platforms like Codeberg/Forgejo in the future should be straightforward. Contributions are welcome!
### Trusted Publishing Only Mode
Crate owners can now enforce Trusted Publishing for their crates. When enabled in the crate settings, traditional API token-based publishing is disabled, and only Trusted Publishing can be used to publish new versions. This reduces the risk of unauthorized publishes from leaked API tokens.

## Crates.io Publishing Fails
> **The release preflight cannot verify a crates.io token read-only.**
> `GET /api/v1/me` is `AuthCheck::only_cookie()` in crates.io
> (`rust/src/controllers/user/me.rs`): it answers HTTP 403 to every API token,
> valid or not, and endpoint-scoped tokens are rejected on every route that
> does not require their scope. A probe that reads that 403 as "revoked or
> expired" is a false positive (run 34149311523 blocked a release with the
> token that had published v0.347.0 two days earlier; issue #1085).
> `scripts/preflight-credentials.sh` therefore reports the crates.io token as
> `unknown` with that reason and never sends it anywhere; `cargo publish`
> itself is the only step that proves it.
### Symptom
The "Publish to Crates.io" step fails with an error.
### Common Errors
#### "please provide a non-empty token"
**Cause:** The `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` environment variable is empty or not set.
**Solution:**
1. Ensure you have a secret configured (either `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` or `CARGO_TOKEN`)
2. Map the secret correctly in your workflow:
```yaml
- name: Publish to Crates.io
  env:

A revoked crates.io token or an expired Docker Hub access\n# token therefore cost a full build before anyone learned the release could not\n# happen -- and on a pull request the same absence means nothing at all, because\n# forks have no secrets. This script separates those two readings: `--mode\n# release` fails the run, `--mode report` states what a release would find.\n#\n# Every probe follows the same three rules from that principle:\n#\n#   Probe with a write, not with a login. A registry token endpoint answers 200\n#   for scopes it will not honour -- ghcr.io issues a token for any scope, and\n#   docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with a pull-only `access`\n#   claim -- so the push then fails 403. Opening a blob upload session\n#   (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancelling it (`DELETE <Location>`)\n#   is one round trip, stores nothing, and is the only form of the check that\n#   is not a guess.\n#\n#   Report every failure, not the first. One report naming all three missing\n#   credentials is worth three runs each naming one, so no probe aborts the\n#   script; each records its own verdict and the exit status is decided once.\n#\n#   Report `unknown`, never a guess. A registry that times out or answers 429\n#   has not said the credential is broken. \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is\n#   actionable; \"no failures\" is not.\n#\n# INPUT (environment)\n#   PREFLIGHT_MODE            \"release\" | \"report\" (--mode wins). Default report.\n#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN\n#   CARGO_TOKEN               crates.io token; the first one set is used.\n#   CRATE_NAME                crate whose public record is looked up. Default: formal-ai.\n#   GHCR_IMAGE                e.g. ghcr.io/owner/name. Empty disables the probe.\n#   GITHUB_ACTOR/GITHUB_TOKEN credential for the GHCR probe.\n#   DOCKERHUB_IMAGE           e.g. owner/name. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove the release can publish before the pipeline spends an hour building it.
#
# Issue #1081, principle 16 of docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md ("Prove You Can
# Publish Before You Build"): every credential this repository releases with was
# only ever exercised by the step that used it, at the end of a 90-minute
# `auto-release` job. A revoked crates.io token or an expired Docker Hub access
# token therefore cost a full build before anyone learned the release could not
# happen -- and on a pull request the same absence means nothing at all, because
# forks have no secrets. This script separates those two readings: `--mode
# release` fails the run, `--mode report` states what a release would find.
#
# Every probe follows the same three rules from that principle:
#
#   Probe with a write, not with a login. A registry token endpoint answers 200
#   for scopes it will not honour -- ghcr.io issues a token for any scope, and
#   docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with a pull-only `access`
#   claim -- so the push then fails 403. Opening a blob upload session
#   (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancelling it (`DELETE <Location>`)
#   is one round trip, stores nothing, and is the only form of the check that
#   is not a guess.
#
#   Report every failure, not the first. One report naming all three missing
#   credentials is worth three runs each naming one, so no probe aborts the
#   script; each records its own verdict and the exit status is decided once.
#
#   Report `unknown`, never a guess. A registry that times out or answers 429
#   has not said the credential is broken. "0 verified, 3 unknown" is
#   actionable; "no failures" is not.
#
# INPUT (environment)
#   PREFLIGHT_MODE            "release" | "report" (--mode wins). Default report.
#   CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
#   CARGO_TOKEN               crates.io token; the first one set is used.

import test from 'node:test';

import YAML from 'yaml';

const evidence='experiments/formal_ai_subagent/evidence/specification-delivery-1188/dormant-staged-release/';

function validatePreflight(workflow){
 const job=workflow.jobs['release-preflight'],checkout=job.steps[0],probe=job.steps[1];
 assert.equal(job['timeout-minutes'],5);assert.equal(checkout['timeout-minutes'],2);
 assert.equal(checkout.uses,'actions/checkout@v7');

  'sparse-checkout':'/scripts/preflight-credentials.sh','[REDACTED]':false});

 assert.deepEqual(job.permissions,{contents:'read',packages:'write'});
 return job;
}

// Externally supplied commands receive zero autonomous-authorship credit.
import {spawnSync} from 'node:child_process';

// Tool result lines are indented by drive.mjs; only its top-level boundary
// ends the transcript. Source bytes may contain the same marker or exit text.
export function reviewCommandResult(result, shellCommand) {
  const stdout = result.stdout ?? '';
  const boundary = /^== answer ==\r?$/mu.exec(stdout);
  const trace = boundary ? stdout.slice(0, boundary.index) : stdout;
  const headers = [...trace.matchAll(/^>> (\S+) ([^\r\n]*)\r?$/gmu)];
  let arguments_, receipt;
  if (headers.length === 1 && trace.slice(0, headers[0].index) === '') {
    try { arguments_ = JSON.parse(headers[0][2]); } catch { /* Invalid arguments earn no execution credit. */ }
    const body = trace.slice(headers[0].index + headers[0][0].length);
    // shell-capture.mjs appends the actual status after all stdout/stderr.
    // A preview, signal or JSON error capture has no such complete footer.
    if (body.startsWith('\n   Output: ')) receipt = /\n   Exit Code: (\d{1,3})\r?\n?$/u.exec(body);
  }
  const exact = headers.length === 1 && headers[0][1] === 'bash'
    && arguments_ !== null && typeof arguments_ === 'object' && !Array.isArray(arguments_)
    && Object.keys(arguments_).length === 1 && arguments_.command === shellCommand;
  const code = receipt ? Number(receipt[1]) : null;
  const driverSucceeded = result.status === 0 && !result.signal && !result.error;
  const qualified = boundary !== null && exact && code !== null && code <= 255;
  const exitCode = !driverSucceeded
    ? (Number.isInteger(result.status) && result.status > 0 ? result.status : 1)
    : qualified ? code : 1;
  return {trace, exact, exitCode};
}

 * @param {string} value
 */
export function setOutput(key, value) {
  const outputFile = process.env.GITHUB_OUTPUT;
  if (outputFile) {
    appendFileSync(outputFile, `${key}=${value}\n`);
  }
  console.log(`Output: ${key}=${value}`);
}

  # === RELEASE PREFLIGHT ===
  # Attempt OIDC and check readable repository identity and package visibility
  # before expensive builds/tests. GitHub write capability and exact package
  # push authorization remain unverified until actual writes. Release mode
  # (main push/dispatch) rejects known failures before the matrix; pull requests
  # report without blocking because forks legitimately lack release secrets.
  release-preflight:
    concurrency:
      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-release-preflight
      cancel-in-progress: true
    name: Release Preflight
    runs-on: ubuntu-26.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: [REDACTED]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Detect C# layout
        id: csharp_layout
        uses: $/.github/actions/csharp-layout
      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version: '1.4.4'
      - name: NuGet login (preflight OIDC)
        id: nuget-login
        if: vars.NUGET_USER != '' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: NuGet/login@8d196754b4036150537f80ac539e15c2f1028841 # v1.2.0
        with:
          user: ${{ vars.NUGET_USER }}
      - name: Probe every release precondition
        working-directory: ${{ steps.csharp_layout.outputs.root }}
        env:
          PREFLIGHT_MODE: >-
            ${{
              (
                (github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') ||
                (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main')
              ) && 'release' || 'report'
            }}
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: [REDACTED]

+
+## Bound the release credential probes
+
+The five-minute release preflight job sets aside up to two minutes for checkout.
+Its credential script retried transient HTTP results, but an unresponsive
+server could use the remaining job time in one curl call. The other credential
+probes and the aggregate verdict would then be lost to cancellation.
+
+Each curl attempt now allows three seconds to connect and five seconds total.
+With the existing three attempts and two five-second delays, seven exchanges
+can consume at most 175 seconds of request time and backoff. The checkout bound
+and credential verdicts are preserved. The Bash script still works from the
+existing one-file checkout. Crates.io token authority remains unknown without
+an authenticated publication or a crate-owner-configured trusted publisher.
+
+Run `node --test --test-concurrency=1 rust/tests/web/release-preflight-checkout.test.mjs`.
+The loopback fixture stalls the first public crate lookup for seven seconds and
+returns HTTP 503 on retry. The old script waits for the late HTTP 200, skips the
+retry and fails the assertion. The repaired script retries, reports the crate
+as unknown, verifies and cancels a GHCR upload session, reports Docker Hub's
+HTTP 403 and blocks publication. All three tests pass. Bash syntax and
+ShellCheck 0.11.0 also pass. The request fixture uses only synthetic credentials.

#!/usr/bin/env node
// One pinned scanner/configuration, sequential inputs, no extracted files.
import {accessSync,constants,readFileSync,realpathSync,statSync,existsSync} from 'node:fs';
import {delimiter,dirname,join,resolve} from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL,fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
import {createRequire} from 'node:module';
import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';
import {MAX_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES,scanCompressed} from './lib/compressed-secrets.mjs';
function packageVersion(file,name) {
  for(let directory=dirname(file);;) {
    const manifest=join(directory,'package.json');
    if(existsSync(manifest)) {
      const value=JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifest,'utf8'));
      if(value.name===name)return value.version;
    }
    const parent=dirname(directory);if(parent===directory)throw Error('Scanner package identity unavailable');
    directory=parent;
  }
}
export function scannerModule(version,searchPath=process.env.PATH??'') {
  let binary;
  for(const directory of searchPath.split(delimiter)) {
    if(!directory)continue;
    const candidate=join(directory,process.platform==='win32'?'secretlint.cmd':'[REDACTED]');
    try {accessSync(candidate,constants.X_OK);binary=realpathSync(candidate);break;}catch{}
  }
  if(!binary)throw Error('Pinned secretlint executable unavailable');
  const require=createRequire(pathToFileURL(binary));
  const engine=require.resolve('@secretlint/node');
  const builtin=require.resolve('@secretlint/core/builtin');
  for(const [file,name] of [[binary,'secretlint'],[engine,'@secretlint/node'],[builtin,'@secretlint/core']]) {
    if(packageVersion(file,name)!==version)throw Error('Pinned scanner package version mismatch: '+name);
  }
  return pathToFileURL(engine).href;
}

// Resolve only after a complete Git observation; pass paths directly as argv/cwd.

import path from 'node:path';
import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
import {dependencyManifests, trackedDependencyFiles} from './dependency-manifest-inventory.mjs';
export function resolveDependencyLockfiles(repository, kind, run = spawnSync) {
  let resolutions;
  if (kind === '--cargo') {
    resolutions = dependencyManifests(repository).activeCargo.map(manifest => ({
      tool: 'cargo', args: ['update', '--workspace', '--manifest-path', manifest], cwd: repository,
    }));
  } else if (kind === '--javascript') {
    resolutions = trackedDependencyFiles(repository).flatMap(name => {
      const basename = path.posix.basename(name);
      const cwd = path.join(repository, path.posix.dirname(name));
      if (basename === 'bun.lock') return [{tool: 'bun', args: ['install', '--lockfile-only'], cwd}];
      if (basename === 'package-lock.json') return [{
        tool: 'npm', args: ['install', '--package-lock-only', '--ignore-scripts', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], cwd,
      }];
      return [];
    });
  } else {
    throw new Error('Usage: resolve-dependency-lockfiles.mjs --cargo|--javascript');
  }
  for (const resolution of resolutions) {
    if (process.env.FORMAL_AI_DEPENDENCY_DEBUG === '1') {
      console.error('dependency lock resolution: ' + JSON.stringify(resolution));
    }
    const result = run(resolution.tool, resolution.args, {cwd: resolution.cwd, stdio: 'inherit'});
    if (result.error || result.signal || result.status !== 0) {
      const error = new Error('Dependency resolver failed: ' + JSON.stringify(resolution) + ': ' +
        (result.error?.message ?? result.signal ?? result.status));
      error.exitCode = Number.isInteger(result.status) && result.status > 0 && result.status <= 255 ? result.status : 1;
      throw error;
    }

#[test]
fn runtime_coreference_searches_nearest_relevant_ancestor_turn() {
    let solver = UniversalSolver::default();
    let history = [
        ConversationTurn::user("I love Rust."),
        ConversationTurn::assistant("Rust is a systems programming language."),
        ConversationTurn::user("The weather is pleasant."),
        ConversationTurn::assistant("It is."),
    ];
    let response = solver.solve_with_history("Why is it safer than C?", &history);
    assert_eq!(response.intent, "coreference_rust");
    assert!(
        response
            .evidence_links
            .iter()
            .any(|link| link.starts_with("context_resolution:")),
        "runtime use must expose the inherited-scope decision: {:?}",
        response.evidence_links
    );
}

//! The internet as formal knowledge (issue #1163, E128).
//!
//! Web search exists, but its results stay "observations": strings the
//! solver shows and forgets. This module is the generic page formalizer that
//! turns any fetched resource -- HTML, Markdown, plain text, JSON, or
//! PDF-extracted text -- into a [`LinkNetwork`] the solver can reason over:
//! headings become section links, paragraphs become statement links, lists
//! and tables become list and row links, and every code block becomes a code
//! node tagged with its language.
//!
//! All behavior that could differ between deployments lives in
//! `data/seed/page-formalization-rules.lino` (mime hints, sniffing order,
//! language-tag resolution, shebang and extension heuristics, command
//! verbs) and `data/seed/source-trust-weights.lino` (the trust features and
//! their weights). The Rust here only interprets those rules.
//!
//! The six bespoke extractors in `concept_lookup.rs` stay as faster paths;
//! [`covers_statements`] proves the generic formalizer yields every
//! statement they yield on the same bytes, so each is a cache, not a
//! dependency.
//!
//! Nothing here fetches anything: bytes arrive through the existing
//! `source_fetch` capture boundary, and [`annotate_capture`] records the
//! rediscovery procedure (query, rank, URL, hash, timestamp) so a cached
//! network can be dropped under storage pressure and re-fetched
//! deterministically.

//! Structural code generation for numeric-list programs.
//!
//! Issue #395 explicitly asks the coding path to manipulate CST/AST-like
//! structures instead of memorizing final code snippets. This module therefore
//! lowers a resolved numeric-list meaning into a small, language-independent
//! [`NumericProgram`] tree first:
//!
//! * `literal_list` — the user-provided numbers, preserved in order.
//! * `sort_list` / `reverse_list` / `reduce_list` — the semantic operation.
//! * `print_joined` / `print_scalar` — the requested result projection.
//!
//! The projection from that tree into source code is *discovered at execution
//! time* from the `data/seed/coding-idioms.lino` knowledge base rather than
//! owned by per-language renderer functions. Each language section there
//! declares scaffolds (one per operation family) and idioms (named code
//! fragments whose cases are selected by the requested operation and the value
//! class of the list items). [`NumericProgram::render`] walks the language's
//! inheritance chain, picks the scaffold for the operation's ontology family,
//! and recursively expands every `{slot}` placeholder — so adding a language or
//! an operation idiom is seed data, not Rust code. The tree itself is logged in
//! Links Notation so the solver's reasoning can be inspected independently from
//! the printed code.
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use std::fmt::Write as _;
use std::sync::OnceLock;
use crate::coding::catalog::ProgramLanguage;
use crate::seed::parser::{LinoNode, parse_lino};

/// Value of `name="..."` in a tag's attribute text, if present.
pub(super) fn tag_attr(inner_tag: &str, name: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let lower = inner_tag.to_ascii_lowercase();
    let needle = format!("{name}=");
    let at = lower.find(&needle)?;
    let rest = &inner_tag[at + needle.len()..];
    let quote = rest.chars().next()?;
    if quote == '"' || quote == '\'' {
        let end = rest[1..].find(quote)? + 1;
        Some(rest[1..end].to_owned())
    } else {
        Some(
            rest.split_whitespace()
                .next()
                .unwrap_or_default()
                .to_owned(),
        )
    }
}
/// The text of an HTML fragment with every tag removed, whitespace kept.
fn remove_tags(fragment: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut depth = 0usize;
    for character in fragment.chars() {
        match character {
            '<' => depth += 1,
            '>' => depth = depth.saturating_sub(1),
            _ if depth == 0 => out.push(character),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    out
}
/// Strip every tag from an HTML fragment and collapse its whitespace.
pub(super) fn strip_tags(fragment: &str) -> String {
    remove_tags(fragment)
        .split_whitespace()
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(" ")
}
