/// This matches the behaviour of the legacy JavaScript `normalizePrompt(prompt)`
/// helper in the browser worker — keeping a single implementation in Rust
/// eliminates the drift that produced different traces in #133.
///
/// The rules:
///   * Unicode letters and digits are kept (preserving every script — Cyrillic,
///     Devanagari, CJK, Latin).
///   * Every other Unicode codepoint becomes a single space.
///   * Adjacent spaces collapse, leading and trailing spaces are stripped.
///   * ASCII uppercase letters fold to lowercase. Non-ASCII case folding is
///     applied through `char::to_lowercase` so the result is locale-agnostic.
#[must_use]
pub fn normalize_prompt(prompt: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(prompt.len());
    let mut last_was_space = true;
    for ch in prompt.chars() {
        if is_unicode_letter_or_digit(ch) {
            for lower in ch.to_lowercase() {
                out.push(lower);
            }
            last_was_space = false;
        } else if !last_was_space {
            out.push(' ');
            last_was_space = true;
        }
    }
    if out.ends_with(' ') {

/// Build the page network from parsed blocks: a `page` root with one child
/// object per block, each carrying its text (and language/level/command
/// fields where they apply). Block node ids come back in document order.
fn blocks_to_network(
    blocks: &[PageBlock],
    url_hint: Option<&str>,
) -> (LinkNetwork, Vec<(LinkId, PageBlock)>) {
    let mut network = LinkNetwork::new();
    let page = network.insert_object("page");
    if let Some(url) = url_hint {
        let domain = network.insert_point(&url_domain(url));
        network.insert_field(page, "domain", domain);
    }
    let mut nodes = Vec::new();
    for block in blocks {
        let (kind, text) = match block {
            PageBlock::Heading { text, .. } => ("heading", text.as_str()),
            PageBlock::Paragraph { text, .. } => ("paragraph", text.as_str()),
            PageBlock::ListItem { text } => ("list_item", text.as_str()),
            PageBlock::TableRow { cells } => ("table_row", cells.as_str()),
            PageBlock::CodeBlock { text, .. } => ("code_block", text.as_str()),
        };
        // `insert_object` interns by term, so every block of one kind would
        // share a single link; each block is its own instance of its kind
        // (the JS twin's per-block `id`), so a page query's link names
        // exactly one block.
        let kind_id = network.insert_object(kind);
        let node = network.insert_object_instance(kind_id);
        let text_id = network.insert_point(text);
        network.insert_field(node, "text", text_id);
        match block {
            PageBlock::Heading { level, .. } => {
                let level_id = network.insert_point(&level.to_string());
                network.insert_field(node, "level", level_id);
            }
            PageBlock::CodeBlock { language, .. } => {
                let language_id = network.insert_point(language);

pub fn client() -> CachedSourceClient<DocumentationReplay> {
    let thread = std::thread::current();
    let name = thread.name().expect("test name").replace("::", "-");
    let cache = std::env::temp_dir()
        .join(format!("formal-ai-doc-replay-{}", std::process::id()))
        .join(name);
    CachedSourceClient::new(cache, DocumentationReplay).with_online(true)
}

/// One registered list file and how it is kept canonical.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct ListFile {
    path: String,
    list_kind: String,
    /// Directory whose modules this list must declare, when the list is an
    /// exact mirror of a directory's contents.
    declares_directory: Option<String>,
    /// Module stems present in `declares_directory` that the list deliberately
    /// does not declare yet: a plan drafted as tests before its leaf lands
    /// (issue #1138's draft-first discipline). The mirror stays exact for
    /// everything else, so registering a red test early can never be forced by
    /// this gate.
    inert: Vec<String>,
}
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Links Notation registry
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// Strip one level of surrounding quotes from a registry value.
fn unquote(value: &str) -> String {
    let trimmed = value.trim();
    trimmed
        .strip_prefix('"')
        .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_suffix('"'))
        .unwrap_or(trimmed)
        .to_string()
}
fn indent_of(line: &str) -> usize {
    line.len() - line.trim_start().len()
}

#[test]
fn runtime_coreference_searches_nearest_relevant_ancestor_turn() {
    let solver = UniversalSolver::default();
    let history = [
        ConversationTurn::user("I love Rust."),
        ConversationTurn::assistant("Rust is a systems programming language."),
        ConversationTurn::user("The weather is pleasant."),
        ConversationTurn::assistant("It is."),
    ];
    let response = solver.solve_with_history("Why is it safer than C?", &history);
    assert_eq!(response.intent, "coreference_rust");
    assert!(
        response
            .evidence_links
            .iter()
            .any(|link| link.starts_with("context_resolution:")),
        "runtime use must expose the inherited-scope decision: {:?}",
        response.evidence_links
    );
}

//! Keep every union-merged list in its canonical order.
//!
//! Issue #991 review feedback: "find a way to reduce possibility of conflicts

//! of conflicts in the future reduced to zero."
//!
//! `scripts/analyze-merge-conflicts.py` shows that the single largest class of
//! manual conflict resolutions in this repository is the *append-only list*:
//! `src/lib.rs`, `tests/unit/mod.rs` and their siblings are nothing but a
//! canonically ordered list of declarations, and two branches that each add one
//! unrelated entry collide on the same region.
//!
//! `.gitattributes` marks those files `merge=union`, so git keeps both sides
//! instead of reporting a conflict. A union is a *superset* of two correct
//! files: it can be out of order and it can repeat an entry, but it never loses
//! one. This script is the second half of that mechanism — it restores the
//! canonical order and removes the repeats, and in `--check` mode it fails CI
//! whenever a committed list is not already canonical.
//!

fn js_modules_in(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::new();
    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) else {
        return names;
    };
    for entry in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
        let path = entry.path();
        if !path.is_file() {
            continue;
        }
        let Some(name) = path.file_name().and_then(|name| name.to_str()) else {
            continue;
        };
        // `formal_ai_worker.js` is the entry point that loads this list, not
        // a module in it: listing it would make the entry import itself.
        if name.ends_with(".js") && name != "formal_ai_worker.js" {
            names.push(name.to_string());
        }
    }
    names.sort();
    names
}

pub(super) fn registered_paths(root: &Path, directory: &Path) -> Result<BTreeSet<PathBuf>, String> {
    let Some(crate_root) = directory
        .ancestors()
        .find(|base| base.join("src/lib.rs").is_file() || base.join("src/main.rs").is_file())

// Directory-mirroring lists
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
/// The module sources a Rust directory offers: `name.rs` files and `name/`
/// directories that carry their own `mod.rs`.
fn module_sources(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names = Vec::new();
    let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) else {
        return names;
    };
    for entry in entries.filter_map(std::result::Result::ok) {
        let path = entry.path();
        let Some(stem) = path.file_stem().and_then(|stem| stem.to_str()) else {
            continue;
        };
        if path.is_dir() {
            if path.join("mod.rs").is_file() {
                names.push(stem.to_string());
            }
            continue;
        }
        if path.extension().and_then(|extension| extension.to_str()) == Some("rs") && stem != "mod"
        {
            names.push(stem.to_string());
        }
    }
    names.sort();
    names.dedup();
    names
}

/// punctuation and Links Notation structure do not.
fn tokenize(line: &str) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
    line.split(|character: char| !(character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || character == '-'))
        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())
}

fn function_body<'a>(text: &'a str, signature: &str) -> &'a str {
    let Some(start) = text.find(signature) else {
        return "";
    };
    let tail = &text[start..];
    let Some(open) = tail.find('{') else {
        return "";
    };
    let body = &tail[open + 1..];
    let mut depth = 1_i64;
    for (index, character) in body.char_indices() {
        match character {
            '{' => depth += 1,
            '}' => {
                depth -= 1;
                if depth == 0 {
                    return &body[..index];
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    ""
}
/// Top-level conditional route arms in the two planner dispatch functions.
/// This counts the general source-order cascade, not names of individual
/// handlers, and therefore remains meaningful while handlers are migrated.
fn planner_route_arms(text: &str) -> u64 {
    [
        "fn plan_chat_step_routes(",
        "pub(super) fn plan_settled_routes(",
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|signature| {
        function_body(text, signature)
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.starts_with("    if "))
            .count() as u64
    })
    .sum()
}

/// Formalize the page a request names through `client` (R1188-U18).
///
/// The cache answers first, and the network only when the client is
/// online. Returns `None` when the request names no URL or does not ask for
/// a formalization. The browser twin is `tryPageFormalization` in
/// `js/worker/formal_ai_worker_page_formalization.js`.
pub fn try_page_formalization_with_client<T: SourceTransport>(
    prompt: &str,
    log: &mut EventLog,
    client: &CachedSourceClient<T>,
) -> Option<SymbolicAnswer> {
    let normalized = normalize_prompt(prompt);
    let url = extract_http_fetch_url(prompt, &normalized)?;
    is_page_formalization_prompt(prompt, &normalized)
        .then(|| answer_page_formalization(prompt, &url, log, client))
}

fn phrase_rows(text: &str) -> u64 {
    text.lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|line| line.starts_with("phrase ") || line.starts_with("keyword "))
        .count() as u64
}
fn function_body<'a>(text: &'a str, signature: &str) -> &'a str {
    let Some(start) = text.find(signature) else {
        return "";
    };
    let tail = &text[start..];
    let Some(open) = tail.find('{') else {
        return "";
    };
    let body = &tail[open + 1..];
    let mut depth = 1_i64;
    for (index, character) in body.char_indices() {
        match character {
            '{' => depth += 1,
            '}' => {
                depth -= 1;
                if depth == 0 {
                    return &body[..index];
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    ""
}
/// Top-level conditional route arms in the two planner dispatch functions.
/// This counts the general source-order cascade, not names of individual
/// handlers, and therefore remains meaningful while handlers are migrated.
fn planner_route_arms(text: &str) -> u64 {
    [
        "fn plan_chat_step_routes(",
        "pub(super) fn plan_settled_routes(",
    ]
    .into_iter()
    .map(|signature| {
        function_body(text, signature)
            .lines()
            .filter(|line| line.starts_with("    if "))
            .count() as u64
    })
    .sum()
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Canonical total-closure audit for the formal-ai seed (issue #398, PR #399).
PR #399 review (comment 4668929105) requires *total* closure, not just the
meaning-graph backbone: **every semantic reference** used as a value anywhere
in ``data/seed/**.lino`` must resolve to one of
  * a defined meaning slug (either the ``slug:`` colon-head form or the
    nested-under-``meanings`` indent form),
  * a declared role in ``data/seed/roles.lino`` (a reserved predicate name),
  * an external grounded id (``Q…``/``L…``/``P…``) with a checked-in Wikidata
    cache record,
  * a lexical cache record (``data/cache/wiktionary/en/<lemma>.json`` or
    ``data/cache/wordnet/en/<lemma>.json``), optionally via an override, or
  * a structural language code (``en``/``ru``/``hi``/``zh``).
Anything else is *undefined* and must be grounded, defined, or overridden — the
build fails the instant a value token resolves to nothing.
This module is the single source of truth shared by
  * the grounding scripts (``--candidates`` emits the work-list), and
  * the Rust CI gate ``tests/unit/total_closure.rs`` (which shells out to
    ``--json`` so the resolver logic lives in exactly one place).
Usage::
    python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py [ROOT]           # human report
    python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py --json [ROOT]     # machine report
    python3 scripts/audit-total-closure.py --candidates en   # English lemmas

fn run() -> Result<(), String> {
    let options = options()?;
    let ledger = fs::read_to_string(options.root.join(LEDGER))
        .map_err(|error| format!("{LEDGER}: {error}"))?;
    let ratchet = parse_ratchet(&ledger)?;
    let mut measured = static_measures(&options.root)?;
    let runtime = if let Some(path) = options.measurement_output {
        let output =
            fs::read_to_string(&path).map_err(|error| format!("{}: {error}", path.display()))?;
        parse_runtime_measures(&output)?
    } else {
        runtime_measures(&options.root)?
    };
    measured.extend(runtime);
    println!("capability-routing ratchet ({LEDGER}):");
    for (name, value) in &measured {
        println!("  {name}: measured {value}");
    }
    let mut failures = check_exact(&ratchet, &measured);
    match ratchet_at(&options.root, &options.base) {
        Ok(Some(previous)) => failures.extend(check_previous(&previous, &ratchet)),
        Ok(None) => println!(
            "  ({} has no {LEDGER}; no earlier ratchet to compare)",
            options.base
        ),
        Err(error) => return Err(format!("could not compare {}: {error}", options.base)),
    }
    if failures.is_empty() {
        println!("capability-routing ratchet holds");
        return Ok(());
    }
    for failure in &failures {
        println!("::error file={LEDGER}::{failure}");
    }
    Err(format!("{} capability-routing failure(s)", failures.len()))
}
fn main() {
    if let Err(error) = run() {
        eprintln!("check-capability-routing: {error}");
        std::process::exit(1);
    }
}

  function visit(oldNode, newNode, location) {
    if (Object.is(oldNode, newNode)) return;
    if (!oldNode || !newNode || typeof oldNode !== 'object' || typeof newNode !== 'object') {
      difference(location, oldNode, newNode); return;
    }
    let visited = pairs.get(oldNode);
    if (!visited) { visited = new WeakSet(); pairs.set(oldNode, visited); }
    if (visited.has(newNode)) return;
    visited.add(newNode);
    if (++visitedPairs > 200000) throw Error('ScalarDifferenceObjectBoundExceeded');
    if (Array.isArray(oldNode) !== Array.isArray(newNode)) {
      difference(location, oldNode, newNode); return;
    }
    for (const key of [...new Set([...Object.keys(oldNode), ...Object.keys(newNode)])].sort())
      visit(oldNode[key], newNode[key], [...location, key]);
  }
  visit(before, after, []);
  return {scope: 'complete paired physical object graph; bounded small-value details',
    differences, visitedPairs, allDifferencesSha256: digest.digest('hex'),
    detailsTruncated: differences > details.length, details};

+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+import {readFileSync} from 'node:fs';
+import {test} from 'node:test';
+
+const before = '33bac27018f08e171424321344b930cdbfe29bfb';
+const planner = 'rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs';
+const requestRoutes = 'rust/src/agentic_coding/planner/request_routes.rs';
+const [requestSignature, settledSignature] = ['fn plan_chat_step_routes(', 'fn plan_settled_routes('];
+const oldSource = path => execFileSync('git', ['show', `${before}:${path}`], {encoding: 'utf8'});
+const currentSource = path => readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
+
+// Mirror the Rust gate's brace scan for the two source functions, without compiling Rust.
+function functionBody(source, signature) {
+  const start = source.indexOf(signature);
+  assert.ok(start >= 0, signature);
+  const open = source.indexOf('{', start);
+  assert.ok(open >= 0, signature);
+  let depth = 1;
+  for (let index = open + 1; index < source.length; index += 1) {
+    if (source[index] === '{') depth += 1;
+    if (source[index] === '}' && --depth === 0) return source.slice(open + 1, index);
+  }
+  assert.fail(`Incomplete body for ${signature}`);
+}
+
+const count = (source, signature) => functionBody(source, signature).split('\n')
+  .filter(line => line === '    if' || line.startsWith('    if ')).length;
+
+test('measure both planner functions and enforce the reviewed ceiling', () => {
+  const beforeCount = count(oldSource(requestRoutes), requestSignature)
+    + count(oldSource(planner), settledSignature);
+  const afterCount = count(currentSource(requestRoutes), requestSignature)
+    + count(currentSource(planner), settledSignature);
+  const ledger = currentSource('data/meta/capability-routing-ratchet.lino');
+  const ceiling = Number(ledger.match(/measure planner-route-arms\n    value (\d+)/u)?.[1]);
+  assert.equal(beforeCount, 68);
+  assert.equal(afterCount, 57);
+  assert.equal(afterCount, ceiling);
+});
+
+test('all twelve existing recipe predicates and steps retain their order', () => {
+  const oldPlanner = functionBody(oldSource(planner), settledSignature);
+  const oldRecipes = [...oldPlanner.matchAll(/if (\w+::is_\w+_task)\(task\) \{\n        return Some\((plan_\w+_step)\(/gu)]
+    .filter(([, predicate]) => !predicate.startsWith('diagram::'))
+    .map(([, predicate, step]) => [predicate, step]);
+  const recipes = currentSource('rust/src/agentic_coding/document_recipe.rs')
+    .split('const SELF_REFERENTIAL_RECIPES:')[1].split('];')[0];
+  const table = [...recipes.matchAll(/(\w+::is_\w+_task),[\s\S]*?(plan_\w+_step)/gu)]
+    .map(([, predicate, step]) => [predicate, step]);
+  assert.equal(table.length, 12);
+  const first = oldRecipes.findIndex(([predicate]) => predicate === table[0][0]);
+  assert.ok(first >= 0);
+  assert.deepEqual(table, oldRecipes.slice(first, first + table.length));
+});

#
# A gate can only say "this drifted"; something has to move the manifests
# forward the day a release lands. This job is that something: once a day it
# refreshes the registry snapshot, lets the gate rewrite every manifest that
# is behind (blocked pins are annotated in-tree and stay put), re-resolves
# the lockfiles from the rewritten manifests, re-runs the CI gates against
# the result, and opens one pull request carrying whatever moved. An empty
# day produces no PR at all.
# If only the default token is available and workflows changed, retain the
# complete validated patch for review instead of pushing an unauthorized
# workflow edit or publishing a partial update.

    - cron: "23 5 * * *"

      create-pull-request:
        description: Open the dependency update PR after validation (scheduled runs always do)

*** Add File: /tmp/gh-issue-solver-resume-01a1e869-4e22-7e51-94df-498e8b918581-1795495060544/experiments/issue-1580/cache-reference-inventory.py
+"""Measure the cache gate's references and identify surviving test/view consumers."""
+
+from pathlib import Path
+import json
+import re
+
+BUCKETS = (
+    Path("data/cache/wikidata/entity"),
+    Path("data/cache/wordnet/en"),
+    Path("data/cache/wiktionary/en"),
+)
+REFERENCE_ROOTS = ("data/seed", "data/cache", "data/overrides", "rust/src", "js/source-cache")
+REFERENCE_EXTENSIONS = {".lino", ".rs", ".json", ".rq"}
+TOKENS = re.…(rb"[A-Za-z0-9-]+")
+
+
+def main():
+    records = {
+        bucket: {path.stem.encode() for path in bucket.iterdir()
+                 if path.is_file() and not path.stem.startswith(".") and path.name != "README.md"}
+        for bucket in BUCKETS
+    }
+    unreferenced = set().union(*records.values())
+    for root in REFERENCE_ROOTS:
+        for path in Path(root).rglob("*"):
+            if path.suffix in REFERENCE_EXTENSIONS and path.is_file():
+                own_stem = path.stem.encode()
+                for token in TOKENS.finditer(path.read_bytes()):
+                    if token[0] != own_stem:
+                        unreferenced.discard(token[0])
+
+    report = []
+    for bucket, stems in records.items():
+        for stem in sorted(stems & unreferenced):
+            name = stem.decode()
+            source = [str(path) for path in sorted(bucket.glob(name + ".*"))]
+            view = Path(f"data/view/en/{name}.lino")
+            report.append({"record": str(bucket / name), "source": source,
+                           "committedView": str(view) if view.is_file() else None})
+    print(json.dumps(report, indent=2))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
*** End Patch output=Exit code: 0

#: Prefix of the files ``scripts/close-total.py`` writes.
#:
#: Issue #1138 B9, plan 09 leaf 6. Counting these as definitions made the metric
#: self-satisfying: the generator wrote a gloss for every unresolved token and
#: the audit then read its own output back as grounding, so the reported gap was
#: zero by construction while thousands of English-only glosses no runtime loads
#: stood in for it. The honest measurement excludes them; the generator may
#: propose work, never satisfy the gate.
GENERATED_PREFIX = "closure-generated-"
def defined_meaning_slugs(root: str, *, include_generated: bool = True) -> set[str]:
    """Slugs defined by either syntax across every ``data/seed/*.lino`` file.
    With ``include_generated=False`` the files ``scripts/close-total.py`` writes
    are skipped, which is the honest definition set (see ``GENERATED_PREFIX``).
    """
    defined: set[str] = set()
    for path in sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(root, "data/seed/*.lino"))):
        if not include_generated and os.path.basename(path).startswith(GENERATED_PREFIX):
            continue
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            lines = handle.read().split("\n")
        stack: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
        for raw in lines:
            if not raw.strip():
                continue
            ind = _indent(raw)
            stripped = raw.strip()
            while stack and stack[-1][0] >= ind:
                stack.pop()
            head = stripped.split(" ", 1)[0]
            if head.endswith(":"):
                head = head[:-1]
            if stack and stack[-1][1] == "meanings":
                defined.add(head)
            stack.append((ind, head))
    return defined

Enforce the cached-record budget for `data/cache/**`.\n//!\n//! Issue #960 (R222-1, <https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/pull/222#issuecomment-4513844358>):\n//! \"we should cache not more than 128 the most frequently used words ... our\n//! system should be lightweight by default\". That number lives in code as\n//! [`MAX_SEED_RECORDS_PER_BUCKET`] (`src/translation/cache.rs`), but nothing\n//! failed when a bucket grew past it: `data/cache/wikidata/entity` holds 406\n//! records, over 3x the cap, with CI green throughout.\n//!\n//! ## What a bucket is\n//!\n//! A bucket is a leaf directory under `data/cache/` (for example\n//! `data/cache/wikidata/entity`, `data/cache/wordnet/en`). A *record* is a\n//! distinct file stem inside it: `Q1860.json` + `Q1860.lino` are one record,\n//! not two.\n//!\n//! ## Why two rules instead of one\n//!\n//! A flat 128-record cap collides head-on with a later, equally binding\n//! requirement: the total reference-closure gate\n//! (`scripts/audit-total-closure.py`) demands that *every* bare token in\n//! `data/seed/*.lino` resolve to a cached record. Three buckets are already\n//! above 128 purely because the seed references that many ids and lemmas —\n//! deleting records to satisfy the cap would fail closure, and closure is what\n//! keeps natural language out of the engine. Sharding the directory would keep\n//! both numbers happy while changing nothing about the repository's weight,\n//! which is the thing the cap actually protects.\n//!\n//! So the budget is enforced as the requirement's *intent*:\n//!\n//!   * **Capped buckets** (everything not listed in [`CLOSURE_DRIVEN_BUCKETS`])\n//!     fail the build above [`MAX_RECORDS_PER_BUCKET`]. Speculative offline\n//!     bulk-caching is blocked outright.\n//!   * **Closure-driven buckets** are exempt from the count, and pay for the\n//!     exemption with a stricter rule: every record must be *referenced* from\n//!     `data/seed/**`, `src/**`, or another cache record (the recursive\n//!     grounding closure `tests/unit/seed/semantic_grounding.rs` walks). An\n//!     unreferenced record is speculative caching by another name and fails.\n//!     Their overflow above the cap is reported as a warning on every run, so\n//!     the debt stays visible and attributable.\n//!\n//! Usage:\n//!   rust-script scripts/check-cache-budget.rs          # check (CI/local)\n//!   rust-script --test scripts/check-cache-budget.rs   # inline unit tests\n//!\n//! ```cargo\n//! def json_cache_file(root_id: str, value) -> str:
    """`json_cache_file`: the canonical Links Notation of a cached document."""
    value = strip_empty(value)
    if value is None:
        value = {}
    out: list = []
    entities = value.get(ENTITIES_KEY) if isinstance(value, dict) else None
    entity = entities.get(root_id) if isinstance(entities, dict) else None
    if isinstance(entity, dict):
        _write_line(out, 0, root_id)
        _write_entity_fields(out, 2, entity)
        for key, field in _sorted_items(value):
            if key != ENTITIES_KEY:
                _write_named_value(out, 0, key, field)
    else:
        _write_document(out, value)
    return "".join(out)
def _verify(cache_dir: Path) -> int:
    checked = mismatched = 0
    for lino_path in sorted(cache_dir.rglob("*.lino")):
        json_path = lino_path.with_suffix(".json")
        if not json_path.is_file():
            continue
        document = json.loads(json_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        encoded = json_cache_file(lino_path.stem, document)
        checked += 1
        if encoded != lino_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"):
            mismatched += 1
            print(f"mismatch: {lino_path}")
    print(f"codec port: {checked} cache files re-encoded, {mismatched} differ")
    return 1 if mismatched else 0

"""Ground English lemmas against Open English WordNet 2024 (issue #398, PR #399).
PR #399 review (comment 4668929105) requires a working multi-source ``view``
whose first new source is WordNet: "archived OEWN 2024 mirrored in-repo (raw +
``.lino``), reachable by meanings." This script is that importer.
Unlike the live Wikidata/Wiktionary APIs, WordNet ships as a single downloadable
lexicon, so one download grounds the whole English content vocabulary offline —
no per-word network round-trips. The pipeline:
  1. **Discover** the work-list: by default, every still-undefined English lemma
     reported by ``scripts/audit-total-closure.py --candidates`` (so the list is
     derived from the data, never hardcoded). Pass words explicitly to ground a
     specific batch: ``python3 scripts/ground-wordnet.py algorithm ability``.
  2. **Look up** each lemma in OEWN 2024 via the ``wn`` library, downloading the
     lexicon into ``WN_DATA_DIR`` (default ``~/.formal-ai-wndata``) the first
     time. Only the compact per-lemma projection is mirrored in-repo; the multi-
     megabyte source database stays out of git, matching R398-09 (small repo,
     on-demand expansion).
  3. **Cache** each grounded lemma as pretty JSON
     (``data/cache/wordnet/en/<lemma>.json``) plus the lossless Links-Notation
     projection beside it (``<lemma>.lino``), regenerated with the same
     ``wikidata_json_to_lino`` codec the Wiktionary/Wikidata caches use, so the
     round-trip CI gate covers i

# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai
This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the
hive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates
only the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI
time ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).
## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

"""Verify that the complete historical timeline can be replayed offline."""
import importlib.util
import json
from pathlib import Path
import sys
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import unittest
from unittest.mock import patch
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
from wikidata_lino_codec import json_cache_file
SPEC = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
    "ground_release_timelines", Path("scripts/ground-release-timelines.py")
)
replay = importlib.util.module_from_spec(SPEC)
SPEC.loader.exec_module(replay)
class ReleaseTimelineCaptures(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_replay_entity_and_canonical_twin_is_beside_the_query(self):
        query = replay.FIXTURE.parent / "historical/spider-man-title-role-films.json"
        entity_dir = query.with_name("wikidata-entities")
        rows = replay.query_rows(query)
        self.assertEqual(len(rows), 12)
        self.assertEqual({path.stem for path in entity_dir.glob("*.json")}, {qid for qid, _ in rows})
        documents = [query] + [entity_dir / f"{qid}.json" for qid, _ in rows]
        for path in documents:
            with self.subTest(capture=path):
                payload = json.loads(path.read_bytes())
                self.assertEqual(
                    path.with_suffix(".lino").read_text(encoding="utf-8"),
                    json_cache_file(path.stem, payload),
                )
        with patch.object(replay, "get", side_effect=AssertionError("capture must be offline")):
            self.assertEqual(replay.main(["ground-release-timelines.py", "--check"]), 0)
    def test_missing_offline_capture_fails_before_network_use(self):
        with TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
            entity_dir = Path(folder)
            with patch.object(replay, "get", side_effect=AssertionError("capture must be offline")):
                with self.assertRaises(FileNotFoundError) as failure:
                    replay.fetch_entity("Q182212", entity_dir, offline=True)
        self.assertEqual(Path(failure.exception.filename).name, "Q182212.json")
if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def wordnet_senses(lemma: str) -> list[dict]:
    path = WORDNET_DIR / f"{lemma}.json"
    if not path.is_file():
        return []
    record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    out = []
    for sense in record.get("senses", []):
        gloss = _gloss_clean(sense.get("definition", ""))
        if not gloss:
            continue
        out.append({
            "pos": _norm_pos(sense.get("partOfSpeech", "")),
            "gloss": gloss,
            "sources": ["wordnet"],
        })
    return out

function evaluate(expression, context) {
  const source = expression.trim().replace(/^\$\{\{\s*/u, '').replace(/\s*\}\}$/u, '')
    .replace(/\.([a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_-]*)/gu, (_, key) => '[' + JSON.stringify(key) + ']');
  return new Script(source).runInNewContext({cancelled: () => false, vars: {}, inputs: {}, ...context}, {timeout: 100});
}

/// Gate commands the lint job still runs inline, bypassing the registry.
///
/// This is the check that keeps the append point closed: without it the list
/// would grow back one convenient step at a time.
fn inline_gate_steps(workflow: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    job_body(workflow, "lint")
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|line| {
            let Some(command) = line.strip_prefix("run: ") else {
                return false;
            };
            command.starts_with("rust-script scripts/check-")
                || command.starts_with("rust-script --test scripts/check-")
                || command.starts_with("npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:")
        })
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect()
}
/// Stages the workflow actually invokes.
fn invoked_stages(workflow: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut stages = BTreeSet::new();
    for line in workflow.lines() {
        if let Some(rest) = line.trim().split_once("run-ci-gates.rs --stage ") {
            stages.insert(rest.1.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_string());
        }
    }
    stages
}

    let end = rest
        .match_indices("\n  ")
        .find(|(index, _)| {
            let after = &rest[index + 3..];
            after
                .chars()
                .next()
                .is_some_and(|character| character.is_ascii_alphabetic())
                && after
                    .lines()
                    .next()
                    .is_some_and(|line| line.trim_end().ends_with(':'))
        })
        .map_or(rest.len(), |(index, _)| index);
    &rest[..end]
}
/// Gate commands the lint job still runs inline, bypassing the registry.
///
/// This is the check that keeps the append point closed: without it the list
/// would grow back one convenient step at a time.
fn inline_gate_steps(workflow: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    job_body(workflow, "lint")
        .lines()
        .map(str::trim)
        .filter(|line| {
            let Some(command) = line.strip_prefix("run: ") else {
                return false;
            };
            command.starts_with("rust-script scripts/check-")
                || command.starts_with("rust-script --test scripts/check-")
                || command.starts_with("npm run --prefix tests/e2e check:")
        })
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect()
}
/// Stages the workflow actually invokes.
fn invoked_stages(workflow: &str) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    let mut stages = BTreeSet::new();
    for line in workflow.lines() {
        if let Some(rest) = line.trim().split_once("run-ci-gates.rs --stage ") {
            stages.insert(rest.1.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_string());
        }
    }
    stages
}

# v1.7.12 - 2026-03-30
  * Support the `timezone` configuration in `on.schedule` with checks for IANA timezone string. See the documentation for more details. Note that actionlint starts to embed the timezone database in the executables from this version so the binary sizes slightly increase. (#641, thanks @martincostello)
# v1.7.11 - 2026-02-14
  * Support the `case()` function in `${{ }}` expressions which was recently added to GitHub Actions. (#612, #614, thanks @heppu)
    env:
      # ERROR: case() requires an odd number of arguments
      ENVIRONMENT: |-
        ${{ case(
          github.ref == 'refs/heads/main', 'production',
          github.ref == 'refs/heads/staging', 'staging'
        ) }}
  * Support new `macos-26-large` and `windows-2025-vs2026` runner labels. # v1.7.10 - 2025-12-30
  * Support YAML anchors and aliases (`&anchor` and `*anchor`) in workflow files. In addition to parsing YAML anchors correctly, actionlint checks unused and undefined anchors. See the document for more details. (#133, thanks @srz-zumix for the initial implementation at #568 and @alexaandru for trying another approach at #557)

+test('dependency qualification restores its exact source patch and rejects stale or corrupt transfers', t => {
+  const {jobs} = read('.github/workflows/dependencies-latest.yml');
+  const seal = jobs['prepare-qualification'].steps.find(step => step.id === 'seal').run;
+  const restore = jobs['qualify-rust'].steps.find(step => step.name === 'Apply the patch to its exact source').run;
+  const directory = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'dependency-qualification-'));
+  t.after(() => fs.rmSync(directory, {recursive: true, force: true}));
+  const cwd = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(directory, 'checkout-'));
+  const git = (...args) => execFileSync('git', args, {cwd, encoding: 'utf8'}).trim();
+  const manifest = path.join(cwd, 'Cargo.toml');
+  const update = '[dependencies]\nexample = "2"\n';
+  git('init', '--quiet');
+  fs.writeFileSync(manifest, '[dependencies]\nexample = "1"\n');
+  git('add', 'Cargo.toml');
+  git('-c', 'user.name=Test', '-c', 'user.email=test@example.invalid', 'commit', '--quiet', '-m', 'fixture');
+  const sha = git('rev-parse', 'HEAD');
+  const env = {...process.env, RUNNER_TEMP: directory, GITHUB_SHA: sha, GITHUB_OUTPUT: path.join(directory, 'outputs')};
+  const bash = (run, environment = env) => spawnSync('bash', ['-c', run], {cwd, env: environment, encoding: 'utf8'});
+  fs.writeFileSync(manifest, update);
+  const captured = bash('rustc() { printf "rustc 1.100.0\\n"; }\n' + seal);
+  assert.equal(captured.status, 0, captured.stderr);
+  assert.equal(fs.readFileSync(env.GITHUB_OUTPUT, 'utf8'), 'rust-version=1.100.0\n');
+  git('restore', 'Cargo.toml');
+  assert.equal(bash(restore, {...env, GITHUB_SHA: 'bad'}).status, 1);
+  assert.equal(git('diff'), '');
+  const restored = bash(restore);
+  assert.equal(restored.status, 0, restored.stderr);
+  assert.equal(fs.readFileSync(manifest, 'utf8'), update);
+  assert.equal(git('diff', '--cached'), '');
+  git('restore', 'Cargo.toml');
+  fs.appendFileSync(path.join(directory, 'dependency-qualification', 'update.patch'), 'corrupt\n');
+  assert.equal(bash(restore).status, 1);
+  assert.equal(git('diff'), '');
+});

// The scope a learned standing requirement belongs to (issue #1559):
// rust/src/standing_scope.rs.
//
// Every recorded exchange carries the scope it was made in as evidence entries
// `scope:user=<id>`, `scope:repository=<host/owner/repo>` and
// `scope:session=<id>`:
//
// - `user` is the client-declared end user (OpenAI `user`, Anthropic
//   `metadata.user_id`) — a requirement that user states follows that user into
//   every later conversation;
// - `session` is recorded for an agent session (a request that carries tools):
//   the client's first message configures one task, so what is learned there
//   stays in that session unless sharing is requested with
//   `FORMAL_AI_SHARE_STANDING_REQUIREMENTS=1`;
// - `repository` names the repository an agent session works on, so a trace
//   shows which task a requirement came from.
//
// An exchange with neither a user nor a session scope belongs to the owner of
// the memory store, and what it teaches applies everywhere in that store, as
// before. An amendment applies to a request only when every scope pair it
// carries equals the request's own.

Validate the Actual Merge Result\n\n**CI must test what will actually be merged, not a stale PR snapshot.**\n\nWhen a PR is opened against a base branch that later receives new commits, the GitHub merge preview can become stale. Simulate a fresh merge before running checks:\n\n```yaml\n- name: Simulate fresh merge with base branch (PR only)\n  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n  env:\n    BASE_REF: ${{ github.base_ref }}\n  run: |\n    git config user.email \"github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com\"\n    git config user.name \"github-actions[bot]\"\n    git fetch origin \"$BASE_REF\"\n    BEHIND_COUNT=$(git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/$BASE_REF)\n    if [ \"$BEHIND_COUNT\" -gt 0 ]; then\n      git merge origin/$BASE_REF --no-edit || \\\n        (echo \"::error::Merge conflict! PR must be rebased before merging.\" && exit 1)\n    fi\n```\n\nThis ensures lint, file-size, and other checks validate the final merged state.\n\n### 8. Pre-commit Hooks\n\nLocal quality gates prevent broken commits from reaching CI:\n\n1. Format check and auto-fix\n2. Lint and static analysis\n3. Type checking (where applicable)\n4. File size validation\n5. Secrets detection\n\nThis \"shift left\" approach catches issues immediately rather than waiting for CI.\n\n### 9. Release Automation\n\nAutomated release workflows ensure:\n\n- **No manual version management** - Versions update automatically\n- **OIDC trusted publishing** - No API tokens needed in CI (npm, PyPI, crates.io)\n- **Validated releases only** - All checks must pass before publishing\n- **Dual trigger modes** - Both automatic (on merge) and manual (workflow dispatch)\n- **Commit the version bump directly to the default branch** - The release job pushes its generated version commit (package metadata, lockfile, changelog, consumed changesets) straight to `main` as `github-actions[bot]`, and fails closed if that commit changes anything other than release metadata. Do not route it through an auto-merged release pull request: every release then adds one more pull request and one more branch (a no-deletion ruleset keeps it forever), and a failed run leaves an open release pull request behind for someone to close\n- **A rule-blocked push is fixed in the rule, not in the workflow** - When a repository rule rejects the version push, fail the release with the rule's output and fix the rule (remove it, or add `github-actions` as a bypass actor). The rebase-and-retry path for a lost race is a different recovery for a rejection that prints the same word (see principle 10)\n- **Wait for the registry as long as it really takes, and never republish to find out** - `npm publish` can succeed minutes before `npm view` sees the version. Hive Mind's lag went from 2–9 s to 99–377 s in September 2026, and 2.35.1 took 874 s (issue #2923). A 330 s window turned a good release into a red run with no GitHub release, Docker image or Helm chart. Size the window from measured data with a wide margin (`experiments/npm-publish-lag-2923.mjs` measures it from the Sigstore attestations), log how long each wait took, and treat `E409 Cannot publish over previously staged version` as \"already landed\", not as a failure\n- **Decide \"is there anything to release?\" from every artifact, not just the registry** - If the job dies after the publish, the next push sees the version on npm and skips the release for good. Check the GitHub release too and re-run the release without a bump when it is missing; a lookup that fails is \"unknown\", which never releases\n\n**Prohibit manual version changes** in PRs — all version bumps should be managed by the CI release workflow:\n\n```yaml\nversion-check:\n  if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'\n  steps:\n    - name: Check for version changes in package.json\n      run: node scripts/check-version.mjs\n```\n\n### 14. Lint the Workflows Themselves\n\n**The pipeline is code, and nothing lints it by default.** Workflow files accumulate shell quoting bugs, over-broad `permissions`, unpinned actions and template-injection sinks that no job in the pipeline is looking for, because every job is busy checking the application.\n\nTwo complementary tools, in their own workflow, triggered on changes to `.github/`:\n\n- [`actionlint`](https://github.com/rhysd/actionlint) — syntax, expressions, and (crucially) the shell inside every `run:` block.\n- [`zizmor`](https://docs.zizmor.sh/) — security audits: `excessive-permissions`, `unpinned-uses`, `template-injection`, `artipacked`.\n\n```yaml\n- uses: docker://rhysd/actionlint:1.7.12\n  with:\n    args: -color\n```\n\n- **Run actionlint as the Docker image, not a bare binary.** The image bundles `shellcheck` and `pyflakes`. A binary without `shellcheck` on `PATH` silently skips every shell check and exits 0 — so a green local run means nothing. This one detail is the difference between finding fourteen shell bugs and finding none.\n- **Prefer annotations to SARIF** for zizmor unless code scanning is enabled everywhere the workflow runs. SARIF upload fails silently on forks; annotations fail loudly in both.\n- **Set a confidence floor, not a severity floor.** `--min-confidence medium` filters by how sure the tool is, not by how bad the finding is. Review what falls below the floor once and record the decision, rather than discovering later that the floor was hiding a real finding.\n- **Scope suppressions to a file, and write down when they can be removed.** A blanket `ignore` is indistinguishable from no gate at all.\n\n### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 \"Dependabot is rebasing this PR\" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).\n- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).\n- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. Strip versions, ids, hashes and paths before comparing (issue #4055).\n- **Wait for asynchronous release with a bound.** An async database pool closes its connections on a worker thread after `close()` returns. A step that needs \"no open handles\" right afterwards must poll with backoff and a deadline and name the holder it waited for, instead of failing on the first look (issue #4055).\n\nissue-preflight-comments-live.json\nissue-presubmit-comments.json\nissues-1580-comments.json\nissues-1581-comments.json\npr-preflight-comments-live.json\npr-presubmit-comments.json\npulls-1581-comments.json\nupdater-current-inline-comments.jsonl\nupdater-current-issue-comments.jsonl\nupdater-current-pr-comments.jsonl\norigin\thttps://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai.git (fetch)\norigin\thttps://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai.git (push)\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';

/** Run npm without a shell, returning JSON for a registry lookup. */
export function runNpm(argumentsList, directory) {
  return execFileSync('npm', argumentsList, {
    cwd: directory, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 120000, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  });
}
/** Determine whether immutable registry bytes match the prepared tarball. */
export function publicationDecision(specification, integrity, lookup) {
  let existing;
  try {
    existing = JSON.parse(lookup(['view', specification, 'dist.integrity', '--json']));
  } catch (error) {
    let registryError;
    try { registryError = JSON.parse(String(error.stdout ?? '')).error; } catch { /* transport failure */ }
    if (registryError?.code === 'E404') return { publish: true };
    throw error;
  }
  if (existing === integrity) return { publish: false };
  throw new Error('Published package integrity differs from this release tarball');
}
/** Upload the packed artifact or verify that a previous attempt uploaded it. */

  const specification = manifest.name + '@' + manifest.version;

This file restates\nonly the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI\ntime ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).\n\n## The single push gate\n\nA push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It keeps only\n   the latest build's artifacts, and by default it caps the tree at 4 GB\n   locally (`CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB`).\n\n## Where things live\n\n- Production-only failures are recorded in\n  [`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino).\n  These are failures that main recorded after a green pull request. #!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-secrets.sh
#
# Scans the files a change touches for committed credentials, using secretlint
# with the recommended preset (CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 11 / issue #808).
#
# Usage:
#   BASE_REF=main bash scripts/check-secrets.sh     # scan the diff vs BASE_REF
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh --all             # scan every tracked file
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh path/to/file ...  # scan specific files
#
# Exit code 0 = no secrets found; non-zero = a finding or scanner failure.
#
# Why the diff and not the whole tree
# -----------------------------------
# The js template runs `secretlint "**/*"`. Measured on this repository that
# does not finish in a usable time: the glob walks the working tree (including
# `target/` and ~150 MB of committed case-study logs) and the scan was still
# running after 25 minutes locally. A gate that cannot be relied on to finish is
# a new CI failure mode, which is the opposite of what issue #808 asks for.
#
# Scanning what the change touches keeps the gate fast and catches the case that
# matters: a credential being *introduced*. Pre-existing files are not re-scanned
# on every pull request; run `--all` (no timeout) to audit the whole tree.
#
# FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG=[REDACTED] prints the resolved file list before scanning.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
debug() {
  if [ "${FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG:[REDACTED]}" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[check-secrets] %s\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}
# Captured third-party CI/agent logs kept verbatim as evidence. They are
# reviewed when added and consist of redacted GitHub Actions output.
exclude() {
  local status=0
  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}

  local check="crates.io publish token"
  local token="${C…-}}"
  if [ -z "$token" ]; then
    record failed "$check" "neither CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN nor CARGO_TOKEN is set; \`cargo publish\` cannot run"
    return

  # is declared `AuthCheck::only_cookie()` in crates.io's `src/controllers/
  # user/me.rs`, so every API token -- valid, revoked or expired -- is answered
  # 403 there; the probe that shipped with issue #1081 read that 403 as "the
  # token is revoked, expired or misscoped" and blocked the release of run
  # 34149311523 with a token that had published v0.347.0 two days earlier

  # does not require their scope, and the only route that requires the
  # publish scope is the publish itself. So the token is never sent anywhere
  # from here: the one honest read-only verdict is `unknown`, stated with the
  # reason, and `cargo publish` remains the step that proves it.
  local body status
  body="$(mktemp)"
  curl_headers=()

// once: `str::lines`, Unicode `trim`, `split_whitespace`, byte-wise `String`
// ordering, `{:?}` string escaping, `io::Error` and `ParseIntError` messages,
// `Path::extension`, and the order `walkdir` visits a tree in.
//
// Node built-ins only.
import { lstatSync, opendirSync, readFileSync, statSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';
// `char::is_whitespace`: the Unicode White_Space property. JavaScript's `\s`
// adds U+FEFF and drops U+0085, so it is spelled out.
const WHITESPACE = '\t\n\v\f\r \u0085         '
  + '        　';
/** `char::is_whitespace`. */
export function isWhitespace(ch) {
  return ch.length > 0 && WHITESPACE.includes(ch);
}
/** `str::trim_start`. */
export function trimStart(text) {
  let start = 0;
  while (start < text.length && WHITESPACE.includes(text[start])) start += 1;
  return text.slice(start);
}
/** `str::trim_end`. */
export function trimEnd(text) {
  let end = text.length;
  while (end > 0 && WHITESPACE.includes(text[end - 1])) end -= 1;
  return text.slice(0, end);
}
/** `str::trim`. */
export function trim(text) {
  return trimEnd(trimStart(text));
}
/** `str::split_whitespace`. */
export function splitWhitespace(text) {
  const words = [];
  let word = '';
  for (const ch of text) {
    if (WHITESPACE.includes(ch)) {
      if (word) words.push(word);
      word = '';
    } else {
      word += ch;
    }
  }
  if (word) words.push(word);
  return words;
}
/** `str::lines`: split on `\n`, drop one trailing `\r`, no final empty line. */
export function lines(text) {
  if (text === '') return [];
  const parts = text.

Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 \"Dependabot is rebasing this PR\" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).\n- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).\n- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. Strip versions, ids, hashes and paths before comparing (issue #4055).\n- **Wait for asynchronous release with a bound.** An async database pool closes its connections on a worker thread after `close()` returns. A step that needs \"no open handles\" right afterwards must poll with backoff and a deadline and name the holder it waited for, instead of failing on the first look (issue #4055).\n\n## Quality Enforcement Strategy\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build
**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.
Put a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.
```yaml
release-preflight:
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  permissions:
    contents: read
    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - env:
        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}
      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode "$PREFLIGHT_MODE"
release:
  needs: [release-preflight]
  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}
```
- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.
- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.
- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more version

#!/usr/bin/env node
// One pinned scanner/configuration, sequential inputs, no extracted files.
import {accessSync,constants,readFileSync,realpathSync,statSync,existsSync} from 'node:fs';
import {delimiter,dirname,join,resolve} from 'node:path';
import {pathToFileURL,fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
import {createRequire} from 'node:module';
import {randomUUID} from 'node:crypto';
import {MAX_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES,scanCompressed} from './lib/compressed-secrets.mjs';
function packageVersion(file,name) {
  for(let directory=dirname(file);;) {
    const manifest=join(directory,'package.json');
    if(existsSync(manifest)) {
      const value=JSON.parse(readFileSync(manifest,'utf8'));
      if(value.name===name)return value.version;
    }
    const parent=dirname(directory);if(parent===directory)throw Error('Scanner package identity unavailable');
    directory=parent;
  }
}
export function scannerModule(version,searchPath=process.env.PATH??'') {
  let binary;
  for(const directory of searchPath.split(delimiter)) {
    if(!directory)continue;
    const candidate=join(directory,process.platform==='win32'?'secretlint.cmd':'[REDACTED]');
    try {accessSync(candidate,constants.X_OK);binary=realpathSync(candidate);break;}catch{}
  }
  if(!binary)throw Error('Pinned secretlint executable unavailable');
  const require=createRequire(pathToFileURL(binary));
  const engine=require.resolve('@secretlint/node');
  const builtin=require.resolve('@secretlint/core/builtin');
  for(const [file,name] of [[binary,'secretlint'],[engine,'@secretlint/node'],[builtin,'@secretlint/core']]) {
    if(packageVersion(file,name)!==version)throw Error('Pinned scanner package version mismatch: '+name);
  }
  return pathToFileURL(engine).href;
}

#[test]
fn learning_frontier_takes_precedence_when_the_request_also_names_the_catalog() {
    let request = "Map the Google Trends learning frontier for unresolved catalog prompts.";
    assert!(is_google_trends_learning_task(request));
    assert!(is_google_trends_catalog_task(request));
    with_trends_replay(|| {
        let call = expect_single_call(&[ChatMessage::user(request)], &["write_file"]);
        assert_eq!(call.tool, "write_file");
        let arguments: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&call.arguments).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(arguments["path"], GOOGLE_TRENDS_LEARNING_PATH);
    });
}

use crate::issue_498_google_trends::{captured_feed, with_trends_replay};
use formal_ai::agentic_coding::{
    AgenticPlan, DRIVER_TOOLS, GOOGLE_TRENDS_LEARNING_PATH, GOOGLE_TRENDS_LEARNING_TASK,
    PlannedToolCall, google_trends_learning as recipe, is_google_trends_catalog_task,
    is_google_trends_learning_task, plan_chat_step, run_agentic_task,
};
use formal_ai::{ChatMessage, ToolCall, parse_frontier_record, trending_learning_report_from_feed};
use lino_objects_codec::format::parse_indented;
fn expect_single_call(messages: &[ChatMessage], tools: &[&str]) -> PlannedToolCall {
    match plan_chat_step(messages, tools) {
        Some(AgenticPlan::ToolCalls(mut calls)) => {
            assert_eq!(calls.len(), 1, "the planner emits one call per step");
            calls.remove(0)
        }
        other => panic!("expected a single tool call, got {other:?}"),
    }
}
fn answer_tool_call(messages: &mut Vec<ChatMessage>, call: &PlannedToolCall, result: &str) {
    let id = format!("call_{}", messages.len());
    messages.push(ChatMessage::assistant_tool_calls(vec![ToolCall::function(
        id.clone(),
        call.tool.clone(),
        call.arguments.clone(),
    )]));
    messages.push(ChatMessage::tool_result(id, &call.tool, result));
}

// Mirror the Rust gate's brace scan for the two source functions, without compiling Rust.
function functionBody(source, signature) {
  const start = source.indexOf(signature);
  assert.ok(start >= 0, signature);
  const open = source.indexOf('{', start);
  assert.ok(open >= 0, signature);
  let depth = 1;
  for (let index = open + 1; index < source.length; index += 1) {
    if (source[index] === '{') depth += 1;
    if (source[index] === '}' && --depth === 0) return source.slice(open + 1, index);
  }

}
