Audit the Dependency Tree\n\n**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.\n\n```yaml\n- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high\n```\n\n- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.\n- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.\n- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.\n\n### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build\n\n**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.\n\nPut a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.\n\n```yaml\nrelease-preflight:\n  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n  permissions:\n    contents: read\n    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it\n  steps:\n    - uses: actions/checkout@v7\n    - env:\n        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'release' || 'report' }}\n      run: node scripts/preflight-credentials.mjs --mode \"$PREFLIGHT_MODE\"\n\nrelease:\n  needs: [release-preflight]\n  if: ${{ !cancelled() && needs.release-preflight.result == 'success' }}\n```\n\n- **Probe with a write, not with a login.** ghcr.io's token endpoint returns 200 for any scope and verifies nothing — the push then fails 403. docker.io answers an anonymous push-scope request with 200 and a pull-only `access` claim. Open a blob upload session (`POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/`) and cancel it with `DELETE <Location>`: one round trip, nothing stored, and the only form of the check that is not a guess.\n- **Report every failure, not the first.** The preflight's value is one report naming all missing credentials. A login step that aborts the job hides the rest, so make it `continue-on-error: true` and let the preflight script decide.\n- **Check reachability, not just writability.** A GHCR package is private on first push and stays private until someone clicks; publishing more versions of a package nobody can pull is exactly the compute this job exists to skip. GitHub exposes no API for package visibility (the packages REST API is GET/DELETE/restore only), so this is a manual step that the pipeline can only detect and name.\n- **Prefer trusted publishing.** A credential that expires is a release outage waiting for a calendar date. npm (`id-token: [REDACTED] + `--provenance`) and Docker Hub (`DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`, no `password:[REDACTED] both support OIDC. Check `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` before trying — the runner injects it only when `id-token: [REDACTED] is granted, so a half-wired setup fails with a message about the permission rather than about the token request.\n- **Verify the published result anonymously, and separately.** Never gate the release on the push (a failed mirror must not delete a good release), but do check afterwards, with no credentials, that what you published can be pulled. A check that authenticates measures the publisher's view; a reader gets neither the login nor the benefit of the doubt.\n- **Report `unknown`, never a guess.** A registry that times out or answers HTTP 429 has not said the credential is broken, and a run in which nothing could be verified is not a pass. Say which of the two happened: \"0 verified, 3 unknown\" is actionable, \"no failures\" is not.\n- **Measure the tarball before you upload it.** npm refused `@link-assistant/hive-mind` 2.40.0 and 2.40.1 with `E413 Payload Too Large` after every build had passed (2.40.1's tarball was 249,862,346 bytes); the largest tarball it is known to have accepted here is 165,142,849 bytes. Gate the actual archive below that (`npm pack --dry-run --json | node scripts/check-npm-tarball-size.mjs --stdin`) and name its largest files. An E413 is deterministic, so fail on the first one instead of retrying. Ship platform-specific binaries as per-platform packages pinned by `optionalDependencies`, as `@openai/codex` does (#4050, `src/native-codex/PACKAGES.md`).\n\n### 17. Tell a Broken Pipeline from a Changed World\n\n**A job that fails for a reason no commit can fix is a false negative, and it trains everyone to ignore red.** Issue #2625 found four of them on `main` at once: a dependency gate that failed every push because a new upstream major had appeared, a cleanup that failed every day because a ruleset forbids deleting branches, a dispatch that GitHub refused before it started, and a log upload that retried a refusal three times. Each one hid the real failures next to it.\n\n```yaml\non:\n  workflow_dispatch:\n    inputs:\n      bump_type:\n        required: true\n        default: patch # the dispatch API answers HTTP 422 without it\n```\n\n- **Gate external state on pull requests; on push, warn.** \"A newer version was published\" is a fact about the world, not about the commit. Failing the push skips lint, tests and the release for a change that broke nothing; the pull request is where someone can act on it.\n- **A policy refusal is a decision, not a transient error.** `Resource not accessible by integration` (a workflow `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot create gists) and a ruleset's `Repository rule violations found` answer the same way on every attempt. Retry `HTTP 429` and `5xx`; report a refusal once, name what would allow it, and move on.\n- **Every input a workflow is dispatched with by API needs a default.** `gh workflow run` cannot fill a form: a `required: true` input without `default:` makes GitHub answer `HTTP 422: Required input '<name>' not provided`, and the run never exists. Test that each dispatched workflow accepts exactly the inputs its caller passes.\n- **Create what you depend on, or tolerate its absence.** `gh pr edit --add-label` fails with `'<label>' not found` in a repository that never had the label. Create it on first use (`gh label create`) instead of failing a run that already did its work.\n- **Write logs where the upload step looks.** An artifact step that finds nothing warns `No files were found with the provided path` and passes; the run that failed early, the one the artifact exists for, leaves no evidence. Make a missing log fail loudly in the test suite, not silently in production.\n- **Say why a job skipped.** A downstream workflow that skips because its upstream failed is correct, but a green run that silently did nothing reads as \"tested\". Print the reason as a `::notice::` annotation so it shows on the run summary (issue #2923).\n- **One outcome, one message.** A log that says \"recovered and completed successfully\" and then \"❌ Agent reported error\" for the same error sends readers down the wrong path. Compute the verdict first, then log only what is true.\n- **A green bot run can still be stuck.** Dependabot logs `Deferring creation of a new pull request` and exits green while an open group pull request exists, even after a newer major superseded it (dependabot/dependabot-core#16791). Pull request #2285 stayed open 52 days and collected 37 \"Dependabot is rebasing this PR\" banners while every daily run passed. Check the outcome, not the exit status: the Dependabot Health workflow fails when a bot pull request is older than 14 days or carries more than 2 rebase banners (issue #4055).\n- **Configure only what exists.** A Dependabot `docker-compose` entry for compose files that build every image locally matches no dependency and warns `groups where no dependencies match` on every run. Derive the ecosystem list from the repository and test it (issue #4055).\n- **Group repeated failures by meaning, not by text.** A health check that keys failures by their exact message counts `Could not pull …:2.40.0` and `…:2.40.1` as two faults, so twelve identical failures never reach a threshold of five. Strip versions, ids, hashes and paths before comparing (issue #4055).\n- **Wait for asynchronous release with a bound.** An async database pool closes its connections on a worker thread after `close()` returns. A step that needs \"no open handles\" right afterwards must poll with backoff and a deadline and name the holder it waited for, instead of failing on the first look (issue #4055).\n\n## Quality ### 15. Audit the Dependency Tree
**Code scanning does not audit your dependencies, and PR-scoped dependency review does not audit the ones you already have.** These two jobs look like coverage together and leave a hole between them: CodeQL analyses your source, while `dependency-review-action` runs only on `pull_request` and only inspects the dependencies a PR _changes_. An advisory published against a package that has been pinned for a year is invisible to both, forever, because no PR touches that line.
```yaml
- run: npm audit --package-lock-only --audit-level=high
```
- **Audit the lockfile as committed** (`--package-lock-only`). It reports what a consumer would get, and cannot be turned green by a resolution that only happens on this runner.
- **Put the job on the schedule**, not only on push. A scheduled run is the only thing that can notice an advisory published after the code stopped changing.
- **Set the level explicitly.** The default is `low`, which trains everyone to ignore the job; no flag at all is a different failure from a deliberate `--audit-level=high`.
### 16. Prove You Can Publish Before You Build
**A pull request exists to test the code; a push to the default branch exists to produce a release.** Those are different jobs, and a missing credential means different things to each. On a pull request it is a warning — forks have no secrets, and the code can still be tested. On the default branch it is the answer: if any credential needed for any planned release is unusable, nothing the run does afterwards can produce a release, and every minute spent building is waste.
Put a `preflight` job first and make every publishing job `needs:` it.
```yaml
release-preflight:
  runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
  permissions:
    contents: read
    id-token: [REDACTED] # so the probe can confirm OIDC works before `npm publish` needs it
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    - env:
        PREFLIGHT_MODE: ${

#
# GitHub's rule: a `pull_request` workflow run whose PR was opened/pushed by
# the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` waits for a maintainer's approval. That is what
# happened to every check on bot PR #1124 -- they ran only after a person
# acted. When the credential resolver (actions/automation-token) reports
# layer `default`, the workflow that opened the push calls THIS action for
# every `pull_request` workflow, so the checks start at once on the head
# commit through `workflow_dispatch` -- dispatch runs need no approval.
#

Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. // Publish a built browser-engine tarball once; unknown registry errors fail.
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, appendFileSync, lstatSync } from 'node:fs';
import { resolve } from 'node:path';
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url';
import { BROWSER_ENGINE_ARCHIVE_MAX_BYTES } from './release-publication-observation.mjs';
/** Run npm without a shell, returning JSON for a registry lookup. */
export function runNpm(argumentsList, directory) {
  return execFileSync('npm', argumentsList, {
    cwd: directory, encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 120000, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'],
  });
}
/** Determine whether immutable registry bytes match the prepared tarball. */
export function publicationDecision(specification, integrity, lookup) {
  let existing;
  try {
    existing = JSON.parse(lookup(['view', specification, 'dist.integrity', '--json']));
  } catch (error) {
    let registryError;
    try { registryError = JSON.parse(String(error.stdout ?? '')).error; } catch { /* transport failure */ }
    if (registryError?.code === 'E404') return { publish: true };
    throw error;
  }
  if (existing === integrity) return { publish: false };
  throw new Error('Published package integrity differs from this release tarball');
}
function checkPackedArchive(directory) {
  const tarballs = readdirSync(directory).filter((file) => file.endsWith('.tgz'));
  if (tarballs.length !== 1) throw new Error('Exactly one packed engine tarball is required');
  const [filename] = tarballs;
  const path = resolve(directory, filename);
  const stat = lstatSync(path);
  if (!stat.isFile()) throw new Error(`Packed engine archive ${JSON.stringify(filename)} must be a regular file`);

# Issue #1085 (D4): the ladder runs on pull requests that touch it or the
# agentic coding modules (leaf level), weekly over every level, and on
# dispatch. The deepest level whose nodes all pass is compared with
# data/meta/ladder-ratchet.lino and may only move deeper.
#
# PR #1188: the depth-five run measured its 32 leaves one after another in one
# job, 72-82 minutes (runs 37652295748, 37663996930; ~250s per passing leaf).
# Leaves are independent -- each starts from a reset worktree and only a
# depth-4 composite reads its children's effects -- so the default run is now
#   plan     consults the green ledger (lookup only), warms the binary cache

#            success, not the plan's, records the inputs green.

Issue #1017 is that exact regression: `macOS core slice 10/12`\n# spent 133s on checkout/toolchain/artifact setup and was killed 467s into a\n# test step whose 480s budget could therefore never expire first, so the whole\n# `CI/CD Pipeline` run reported `cancelled` and no release was published.\n#\n# This wrapper owns the deadline instead of the runner: it warns while the\n# command can still be acted on and -- unless enforcement is explicitly\n# disabled -- terminates the command at the budget and exits 124, so the job\n# reports `failure` with an ::error annotation naming the budget it blew.\n#\n# Usage: run-with-budget-warning.sh <budget-seconds> <label> <command> [args...]\n#\n# Environment:\n#   TEST_WARN_RATIO_PERCENT    warn once this share of the budget is spent (70)\n#   TEST_BUDGET_ENFORCE        `false` warns only and never terminates (true)\n#   TEST_BUDGET_GRACE_SECONDS  SIGTERM -> SIGKILL grace period (15)\n#   TEST_BUDGET_POLL_SECONDS   deadline polling interval (1)\n#   FORMAL_AI_CI_VERBOSE       `true` prints periodic progress lines (false)\n#\n# After the command finishes -- whatever its outcome -- the compiler cache's\n# write-rejection rate is checked once (issue #1081, D9). That check is silent\n# unless the rate crosses its threshold, so a healthy step stays exactly as\n# quiet as it was before.\nset -euo pipefail\n\nscript_dir=\"$(cd -- \"$(dirname -- \"${BASH_SOURCE[0]}\")\" && pwd)\"\n\nbudget_seconds=\"${1:?budget seconds are required}\"\nlabel=\"${2:?a warning label is required}\"\nshift 2\n[ \"$#\" -gt 0 ] || {\n  echo \"a command is required\" >&2\n  exit 2\n}\n\nwarn_ratio=\"${TEST_WARN_RATIO_PERCENT:-70}\"\nenforce=\"${TEST_BUDGET_ENFORCE:-true}\"\ngrace_seconds=\"${TEST_BUDGET_GRACE_SECONDS:-15}\"\npoll_seconds=\"${TEST_BUDGET_POLL_SECONDS:-1}\"\nverbose=\"${FORMAL_AI_CI_VERBOSE:-false}\"\nheartbeat_seconds=\"${TEST_BUDGET_HEARTBEAT_SECONDS:-60}\"\n\nthreshold=$((budget_seconds * warn_ratio / 100))\n[ \"$threshold\" -gt 0 ] || threshold=1\nstarted=$SECONDS\n\n# Job control gives the command its own process group, so the whole process\n# tree can be signalled at the deadline instead of only its root.\nset -m\n\"$@\" &\ncommand_pid=$!\nset +m\n\n# A budgeted Rust step that runs long has two causes with the same shape in the\n# log -- work that grew, and a compiler cache that stopped answering -- and\n# nothing printed so far tells them apart. Issue #1021 hit exactly that:\n# `Test (macos-15-intel / specification)` blew its 1200s budget still compiling\n# dependencies, and deciding whether the runner was slow or the cache was cold\n# took reconstructing per-crate rustc timestamps out of a megabyte of log\n# (`experiments/issue_1021_compile_rate_compare.py`). sccache already counts\n# the answer. It is printed when the budget is in trouble and never otherwise,\n# so a healthy run stays quiet and a red one arrives with its own diagnosis.\nreport_compiler_cache() {\n  case \"${RUSTC_WRAPPER:-}\" in\n    *sccache*) ;;\n    *) return 0 ;;\n  esac\n  local sccache=\"${SCCACHE_PATH:-}\"\n  [ -n \"$sccache\" ] || sccache=\"$(command -v sccache 2> /dev/null || true)\"\n  [ -n \"$sccache\" ] || return 0\n  echo \"[budget] compiler cache counters for ${label}:\" >&2\n  # Never fatal: this is a diagnostic, and `set -e` is in force. A wrapper that\n  # died reporting why a step was slow would replace the finding with a worse\n  # one.\n  \"$sccache\" --show-stats 2>&1 | sed 's/^/[budget] /' >&2 || true\n}\n\n# Issue #1081 (D9): the counter that says how much of the compilation this step\n# just did will actually be there for the next one. `Cache write errors` is\n# printed by --show-stats above, but only when the budget is already in trouble,\n# and nothing has ever compared it to a threshold -- so a run whose cache\n# accepted half of what it was offered looked identical to a healthy one. fn default_locale() -> Option<String> {
    crate::seed::source_record(SOURCE_IDENTIFIER)?
        .api_language
        .into_iter()
        .next()
}
/// Read the ranked topics for one region through the caller's capture client.
pub fn fetch_google_trends_feed<T: SourceTransport>(
    client: &CachedSourceClient<T>,
    geo: &str,
    locale: &str,
) -> Option<GoogleTrendsCatalog> {
    let url = feed_url(geo)?;
    let capture = client.fetch(&url).ok()?;
    let rss = std::str::from_utf8(capture.bytes()).ok()?;
    let mut snapshot = parse_google_trends_rss(rss, geo, locale).ok()?;
    snapshot.source_url = capture.source_url().into();
    snapshot.collected_at = capture.fetched_at().into();
    snapshot.source_sha256 = Some(capture.sha256().into());
    Some(snapshot)
}
/// Open the configured regional feed, respecting the runtime's network policy.
pub fn runtime_google_trends_feed(
    geo: &str,
    locale: &str,
    online: bool,
) -> Option<GoogleTrendsCatalog> {
    let client = CachedSourceClient::new(
        crate::coding::synthesis_runtime::source_cache_root(),
        CurlSourceTransport,
    )
    .with_ttl_seconds(FEED_TTL_SECONDS)
    .with_online(online && crate::solver_config::read_network_allowed());
    fetch_google_trends_feed(&client, geo, locale)
}

/// Build the learning report for a supplied feed using normal solver responses.
#[must_use]
pub fn trending_learning_report_from_feed(catalog: &GoogleTrendsCatalog) -> TrendingLearningReport {
    let engine = FormalAiEngine;
    let mut total_prompts = 0usize;
    let mut handled_by_engine = 0usize;
    let mut frontier = Vec::new();
    let mut traces = Vec::new();
    for topic in &catalog.topics {
        for prompt in prompt_variants_for_topic(&topic.query) {
            total_prompts += 1;
            let answer = engine.answer(&prompt.prompt);
            // The frontier is the prompts the engine left *unrouted* (intent
            // `unknown`). A prompt the solver ultimately routed to a real capability
            // (e.g. `web_search`) is handled, even though its internal trace touched
            // the unknown path — so classify on the final intent, not on whether a
            // trace can be recovered.
            if answer.intent == "unknown" {
                if let Some(trace) = UnknownTrace::from_symbolic_answer(&prompt.prompt, &answer) {
                    traces.push(trace);
                }
                frontier.push(TrendingFrontierEntry {
                    rank: topic.rank,
                    query: topic.query.clone(),
                    language: prompt.language.clone(),
                    variation_key: prompt.variation_key.clone(),
                    prompt: prompt.prompt.clone(),
                    engine_intent: answer.intent.clone(),
                });
            } else {
                handled_by_engine +=

# shellcheck disable=SC2329  # invoked indirectly by the trap below
forward_cancellation() {
  signal_command_tree TERM
}
trap forward_cancellation INT TERM
warned=false
terminated=false
last_heartbeat=0
while command_is_running; do
  elapsed=$((SECONDS - started))

  #
  # A full HumanEval slice spends about 55 seconds per case in the solver
  # (run 37594798452: 89 cases in 81 minutes, one case taking 164 seconds), so
  # 164 cases cannot finish inside one job cap -- and grading happens after the
  # last case, so a cancelled run reports nothing at all. Each shard here runs
  # `--offset`/`--slice` windows of the same suite, grades its own window, and
  # the total job adds the windows up. Shards read only; their combined count
  # is recorded in the ledger by a reviewed commit, never by one shard.
  shard-plan:
    name: Plan upstream shards
    concurrency:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-secrets.sh
#
# Scans the files a change touches for committed credentials, using secretlint
# with the recommended preset (CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 11 / issue #808).
#
# Usage:
#   BASE_REF=main bash scripts/check-secrets.sh     # scan the diff vs BASE_REF
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh --all             # scan every tracked file
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh path/to/file ...  # scan specific files
#
# Exit code 0 = no secrets found; non-zero = a finding or scanner failure.
#
# Why the diff and not the whole tree
# -----------------------------------
# The js template runs `secretlint "**/*"`. Measured on this repository that
# does not finish in a usable time: the glob walks the working tree (including
# `target/` and ~150 MB of committed case-study logs) and the scan was still
# running after 25 minutes locally. A gate that cannot be relied on to finish is
# a new CI failure mode, which is the opposite of what issue #808 asks for.
#
# Scanning what the change touches keeps the gate fast and catches the case that
# matters: a credential being *introduced*. Pre-existing files are not re-scanned
# on every pull request; run `--all` (no timeout) to audit the whole tree.
#
# FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG=[REDACTED] prints the resolved file list before scanning.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
debug() {
  if [ "${FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG:[REDACTED]}" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[check-secrets] %s\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}
# Captured third-party CI/agent logs kept verbatim as evidence. They are
# reviewed when added and consist of redacted GitHub Actions output.
exclude() {
  local status=0
  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}

# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai
This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the
hive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates
only the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI
time ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).
## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

/// Why a payload cannot be decoded in this environment, if anything.
#[must_use]
pub fn unavailable_reason(manifest: &SuiteManifest) -> Option<String> {
    if matches!(manifest.source, SuiteSource::ParquetRows { .. })
        && !python_module_available("pyarrow.parquet")
    {
        return Some(vocabulary::text(
            "external_benchmark_parquet_module_unavailable",
        ));
    }
    None
}
fn python_module_available(module: &str) -> bool {
    let import = vocabulary::render("external_benchmark_python_import", &[("module", module)]);
    crate::bounded_process::command_output(
        {
            let mut bounded_child_command = Command::new("python3");
            bounded_child_command.args(["-c", &import]);
            bounded_child_command
        },
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
        64 * 1024 * 1024,
        16 * 1024 * 1024,
    )
    .map_err(|failure| std::io::Error::new(failure.kind(), failure))
    .is_ok_and(|output| output.status.success())
}

 * The ledger as flat entries: `main-run <id>` holds kind groups, a kind holds
 * `regression <id>` blocks, and each field of a block appears at most once.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# External verifier for one Agent CLI ladder node (issues #1028, #1066, #1085).
#
# The verdict never trusts the agent's own words: a leaf must have changed the
# one tracked file its task names, the file must still format, compile and pass
# the unit tests of its module; a depth-4 composite must compose both verified
# child effects and both children's diffs must apply to one tree and compile;
# a node at depth 3 or above is requirement-shaped, so every leaf marker under
# it must be present, only those files modified, and the tree must compile and
# pass the tests of every touched module (issue #1085 D4).
#
# Environment (all optional):
#   LADDER_CARGO_CHECK=0       skip `cargo check --lib`
#   LADDER_CARGO_TEST=0        skip `cargo test --test unit <module>`
#   LADDER_CARGO_TARGET_DIR    shared target directory (run.sh sets one per run)
#   LADDER_LEAVES              leaves.tsv (requirement-shaped nodes)
#   LADDER_LEAF_SPAN=start-end leaf numbers under a requirement-shaped node
#   LADDER_CHILD_DIFFS         two diff files a depth-4 composite must merge

/** Reject unsupported encoding instead of replacing source characters.
 * @param {string} file @returns {string} */
export function readSourceText(file) {
  const status = fs.lstatSync(file);
  if (!status.isFile() || status.isSymbolicLink()) throw Error('RegularSourceFileRequired');
  if (status.size > 4 * 1024 * 1024) throw Error('SourceModelInputBudgetExceeded');
  return new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true, ignoreBOM: true}).decode(fs.readFileSync(file));
}

debug "secretlint ${SECRETLINT_VERSION}"
# Feed the exact existing selection through stdin rather than interpolating paths
# into npm's shell command. The pinned API is loaded once for all archive members.
export SECRETLINT_VERSION
scan_files() {
  if [ "$SECRETLINT_VERSION" = 14.0.0 ]; then
    # npm exec pins the root package, but resolves its semver transitives again.
    # Install the committed closure separately from application dependencies.
    scanner_directory="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/formal-ai-secretlint.XXXXXX")"
    trap 'rm -rf -- "$scanner_directory"' EXIT
    cp .github/secretlint/package.json .github/secretlint/package-lock.json "$scanner_directory/"
    # Installation must not consume the NUL filename stream intended for the scanner.
    npm ci --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund --engine-strict --prefix "$scanner_directory" </dev/null >&2
    PATH="$scanner_directory/node_modules/.bin:$PATH" node scripts/check-secrets-files.mjs
  else
    # Preserve the explicit custom-version override; only the default is lock-qualified.
    npx --yes -p "secretlint@${SECRETLINT_VERSION}" node scripts/check-secrets-files.mjs
  fi
}
printf '%s\0' "${files[@]}" | scan_files

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
BIN="${BIN:-$ROOT/rust/target/release/formal-ai}"
AGENT="${AGENT:-agent}"
OUT="${OUT:-$ROOT/docs/case-studies/issue-1028/agent-tree-run}"
TREE_DEPTH="${TREE_DEPTH:-5}"
NODE_FILTER="${NODE_FILTER:-}"
BASE_PORT="${BASE_PORT:-8870}"
VERIFY_NODE="$ROOT/experiments/issue_1028_agent_cli_ladder/verify-node.sh"
AUTHORED_RULES="${AUTHORED_RULES:-enabled}"
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --no-authored-rules) AUTHORED_RULES=disabled; shift ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
case "$AUTHORED_RULES" in
  enabled|disabled) ;;
  *) echo "AUTHORED_RULES must be enabled or disabled" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
[[ -x "$BIN" ]] || { echo "build first: cargo build --release --bin formal-ai --manifest-path rust/Cargo.toml" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v "$AGENT" >/dev/null || { echo "Agent CLI not installed" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v git >/dev/null || { echo "git is required" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v curl >/dev/null || { echo "curl is required" >&2; exit 2; }
command -v python3 >/dev/null || { echo "python3 is required" >&2; exit 2; }
case "$TREE_DEPTH" in
  0|1|2|3|4|5|all) ;;
  *) echo "TREE_DEPTH must be 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or all" >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
if [[ -n "$NODE_FILTER" && ! "$NODE_FILTER" =~ ^(R|[12](\.[12]){0,4})$ ]]; then
  echo "NODE_FILTER must be R or a binary path such as 2.1.2.2.1" >&2
  exit 2
fi
mkdir -p "$OUT"
# A full depth-five run is over half an hour of real Agent CLI turns, and it
# shares `target/` with whatever else is building on the machine. A rebuild or a
# cache prune inside that window swaps -- or removes -- the binary under
# measurement, and a node that fails because its server never started is
# indistinguishable in the log from a node that failed on its merits. Copy the
# binary out once, and every node is measured against the same bytes.
STAGE="$(mktemp -d)"
WORK="$STAGE/work"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Run a command under an execution budget that expires before the job clock.
#
# GitHub reports a job killed by `timeout-minutes` as **cancelled**, not
# **failed** (issue #977), so a step that is allowed to run until the runner
# kills it converts a real, actionable timeout into a benign-looking
# cancellation. Issue #1017 is that exact regression: `macOS core slice 10/12`
# spent 133s on checkout/toolchain/artifact setup and was killed 467s into a
# test step whose 480s budget could therefore never expire first, so the whole
# `CI/CD Pipeline` run reported `cancelled` and no release was published.
#
# This wrapper owns the deadline instead of the runner: it warns while the
# command can still be acted on and -- unless enforcement is explicitly
# disabled -- terminates the command at the budget and exits 124, so the job
# reports `failure` with an ::error annotation naming the budget it blew.
#
# Usage: run-with-budget-warning.sh <budget-seconds> <label> <command> [args...]
#
# Environment:
#   TEST_WARN_RATIO_PERCENT    warn once this share of the budget is spent (70)
#   TEST_BUDGET_ENFORCE        `false` warns only and never terminates (true)
#   TEST_BUDGET_GRACE_SECONDS  SIGTERM -> SIGKILL grace period (15)
#   TEST_BUDGET_POLL_SECONDS   deadline polling interval (1)
#   FORMAL_AI_CI_VERBOSE       `true` prints periodic progress lines (false)
#
# After the command finishes -- whatever its outcome -- the compiler cache's
# write-rejection rate is checked once (issue #1081, D9). That check is silent
# unless the rate crosses its threshold, so a healthy step stays exactly as
# quiet as it was before.

  echo "a command is required" >&2
  exit 2
}

This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the

## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

# mapfile alone loses the exit status of a process substitution. Wait for the
# producer before accepting either an empty or a partially emitted inventory.
read_inventory() {
  local descriptor producer
  exec {descriptor}< <("$@" | exclude)
  producer=$!
  mapfile -d '' files <&"$descriptor"
  exec {descriptor}<&-
  if ! wait "$producer"; then
    echo 'Unable to collect complete scanner inventory; no scan performed.' >&2
    return 1
  fi
}

  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}
# mapfile alone loses the exit status of a process substitution. Wait for the
# producer before accepting either an empty or a partially emitted inventory.
read_inventory() {
  local descriptor producer
  exec {descriptor}< <("$@" | exclude)
  producer=$!
  mapfile -d '' files <&"$descriptor"
  exec {descriptor}<&-
  if ! wait "$producer"; then
    echo 'Unable to collect complete scanner inventory; no scan performed.' >&2
    return 1
  fi
}
uncommitted_files() {
  git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRT -z HEAD &&
    git ls-files -z --others --exclude-standard
}

L35: A module item is a module, surrounded in braces, named, and prefixed with the keyword `mod`. A module item introduces a new, named module into the tree of modules making up a crate.
L36: 【11†[items.mod.nesting]】

L41:

L54:         fn tan(f: f64) -> f64 {
L55:             /* ... */
L56:           unimplemented!();
L57:         }
L58:     }
L59:     }`

ok\n//! Regression gates for issue #1081: the audit of every remaining CI/CD false\n//! positive, false negative, warning and error.\n//!\n//! Issue #977 established that a job killed by `timeout-minutes` is reported as\n//! **cancelled**, not **failed**, and issue #1017 answered it for long steps by\n//! putting them under `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh`, whose budget expires\n//! first and exits 124 with an `::error`. Both left the same blind spot open:\n//!\n//! * Every gate compared a budget **upward**, against the cap it sits under.\n//!   Nothing compared one **downward**, against the work it bounds. `Run\n//!   specification tests` grew from 424s to 1181s against a fixed 1400s budget,\n//!   crossed it in runs 32688997247 and 34095902681, and the only signal either\n//!   time was the pipeline going red -- after the fact, with no warning before.\n//! * The upward comparison was made one budget at a time. A job may declare\n//!   several, and several budgets that all run add up against one cap; the\n//!   js pipeline template's `tests/ci-timeouts.test.js` already sums them and\n//!   this repository only had half of that rule.\n//! * A step running `cargo test` with no deadline of its own is bounded only by\n//!   the job cap, which is the grey conclusion issue #977 exists to remove.\n//!\n//! Each budget may pass \\\n                 `issue_1017`'s per-step check and still leave the job clock as the thing \\\n                 that expires first, which reports the overrun as `cancelled` instead of \\\n                 `failure`. Raise the cap or lower the budgets so the sum stays at or below \\\n                 {MAX_BUDGET_SHARE_PERCENT}% of it.\"\n            );\n        }\n    }\n\n    assert!(\n        checked >= 5,\n        \"expected the macOS archive build and slice, coverage, the release test matrix and \\\n         the agent CLI E2E job to be summed, summed {checked}\"\n    );\n}\n\n/// A step that runs the test suite and owns no deadline is bounded only by the\n/// job cap, and a job cap kill is grey. Equivalent to the JS implementation in `worker/formal_ai_worker.js` and\\\\\\\\n/// the offline trace in `web_requests.rs`.\\\\\\\\n#[must_use]\\\\\\\\npub fn reciprocal_rank_fusion(entries: &[ProviderRanking], k: u32) -> Vec<FusedEntry> {\\\\\\\\n    let mut fused: Vec<FusedEntry> = Vec::new();\\\\\\\\n    for entry in entries {\\\\\\\\n        if entry.url.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n             .providers\\\\\\\\n                .push((entry.provider_id.clone(), entry.rank));\\\\\\\\n            if existing.title.is_empty() && !entry.title.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n                existing.title.clone_from(&entry.title);\\\\\\\\n            }\\\\\\\\n            if existing.excerpt.is_empty() && !entry.excerpt.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n                existing.excerpt.clone_from(&entry.excerpt);\\\\\\\\n            }\\\\\\\\n        } else {\\\\\\\\n            let providers: Vec<(String, u32)> = vec![(entry.provider_id.clone(), entry.rank)];\\\\\\\\n            fused.push(FusedEntry {\\\\\\\\n                url: entry.url.clone(),\\\\\\\\n                title: if entry.title.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n                    entry.url.clone()\\\\\\\\n                } else {\\\\\\\\n                    entry.title.clone()\\\\\\\\n                },\\\\\\\\n                excerpt: entry.excerpt.clone(),\\\\\\\\n                score,\\\\\\\\n                providers,\\\\\\\\n            });\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    fused.sort_by(|left, right| match right.score.partial_cmp(&left.score) {\\\\\\\\n        Some(Ordering::Equal) | None => right.providers.len().cmp(&left.providers.len()),\\\\\\\\n        Some(order) => order,\\\\\\\\n    });\\\\\\\\n    fused\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/// Parse the Empty lines are\\\\\\\\n/// skipped; malformed lines are dropped silently so the JS fallback can\\\\\\\\n/// recover even when one provider returns junk.\\\\\\\\n#[must_use]\\\\\\\\npub fn parse_rrf_input(input: &str) -> Vec<ProviderRanking> {\\\\\\\\n    let mut entries: Vec<ProviderRanking> = Vec::new();\\\\\\\\n    for line in input.split('\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n') {\\\\\\\\n        if line.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        let mut parts = line.split('\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\t');\\\\\\\\n        let Some(provider_id) = parts.next() else {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        };\\\\\\\\n        let Some(rank_text) = parts.next() else {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        };\\\\\\\\n        let Some(url) = parts.next() else {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        };\\\\\\\\n        let title = parts.next().unwrap_or(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\");\\\\\\\\n        let excerpt = parts.next().unwrap_or(\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\"\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\");\\\\\\\\n        let Ok(rank) = rank_text.parse::<u32>() else {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        };\\\\\\\\n        if url.is_empty() {\\\\\\\\n            continue;\\\\\\\\n        }\\\\\\\\n        entries.push(ProviderRanking {\\\\\\\\n            provider_id: provider_id.to_string(),\\\\\\\\n            rank,\\\\\\\\n            url: url.to_string(),\\\\\\\\n            title: title.to_string(),\\\\\\\\n            excerpt: excerpt.to_string(),\\\\\\\\n        });\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    entries\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\n/// Serialize the fused result list back to the JS side. The `no_std` WASM target does not link the `round`\\\\\\\\n/// intrinsic, so we do the round-half-away-from-zero conversion by hand.\\\\\\\\nfn format_score(score: f64) -> String {\\\\\\\\n    let scaled_f = score * 1_000_000.0;\\\\\\\\n    let scaled = if scaled_f >= 0.0 {\\\\\\\\n        (scaled_f + 0.5) as i64\\\\\\\\n    } else {\\\\\\\\n        (scaled_f - 0.5) as i64\\\\\\\\n    };\\\\\\\\n    let whole = scaled / 1_000_000;\\\\\\\\n    let fraction = (scaled % 1_000_000).abs();\\\\\\\\n    let mut text = String::new();\\\\\\\\n    if scaled < 0 && whole == 0 {\\\\\\\\n        text.push('-');\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    text.push_str(&whole.to_string());\\\\\\\\n    text.push('.');\\\\\\\\n    let fraction_str = fraction.to_string();\\\\\\\\n    for _ in 0..(6 - fraction_str.len()) {\\\\\\\\n        text.push('0');\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    text.push_str(&fraction_str);\\\\\\\\n    text\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\",\\\\\\\"filePath\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"/tmp/tmp.onAeTqs6u4/work/rust/src/web_search_core.rs\\\\\\\"}\\\"\\n              }\\n            }\\n          ]\\n        },\\n        {\\n          \\\"role\\\": \\\"tool\\\",\\n          \\\"tool_call_id\\\": \\\"call_74b51b590189860b\\\",\\n          \\\"content\\\": \\\"\\\"\\n        },\\n        {\\n          \\\"role\\\": \\\"assistant\\\",\\n          \\\"content\\\": \\\"Let me run the requested command to get that for you.\\\",\\n          \\\"tool_calls\\\": [\\n            {\\n              \\\"id\\\": \\\"call_4dee984aea9cb076\\\",\\n              \\\"type\\\": \\\"function\\\",\\n              \\\"function\\\": {\\n                \\\"name\\\": \\\"bash\\\",\\n                \\\"arguments\\\": \\\"{\\\\\\\"command\\\\\\\":\\\\\\\"cat rust/src/web_search_core.rs\\\\\\\"}\\\"\\n              }\\n            }\\n          ]\\n        },\\n        {\\n          \\\"role\\\": \\\"tool\\\",\\n          \\\"tool_call_id\\\": \\\"call_4dee984aea9cb076\\\",\\n          \\\"content\\\": \\\"//! '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n    if (!text.includes(args.oldString)) return '\\\\\\\\''Error: oldString not found in content'\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n    if (text.indexOf(args.oldString) !== text.lastIndexOf(args.oldString)) return '\\\\\\\\''Error: Found multiple matches for oldString.'\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n    files.set(path, text.replace(args.oldString, () => args.newString));\\\\\\\\n    return '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  if (tool === '\\\\\\\\''bash'\\\\\\\\'') {\\\\\\\\n    const event = runPlanEvent(files, args.command);\\\\\\\\n    if (event !== null) return event;\\\\\\\\n    const presence = args.command.match(/^test (! )?-e (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\S+)$/u);\\\\\\\\n    if (presence) return files.has(presence[2]) !== Boolean(presence[1]) ? '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'' : ['\\\\\\\\''Output: '\\\\\\\\'', '\\\\\\\\''Error: '\\\\\\\\'', '\\\\\\\\''Exit Code: 1'\\\\\\\\''].join(String.fromCharCode(10));\\\\\\\\n    if (args.command.startsWith('\\\\\\\\''mkdir -p -- '\\\\\\\\'')) return '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n    const transfer = args.command.match(/^(cp|mv) (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\S+) (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\S+)$/u);\\\\\\\\n    if (transfer && files.has(transfer[2])) {\\\\\\\\n      files.set(transfer[3], files.get(transfer[2]));\\\\\\\\n      if (transfer[1] === '\\\\\\\\''mv'\\\\\\\\'') files.delete(transfer[2]);\\\\\\\\n      return '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'';\\\\\\\\n    }\\\\\\\\n    const digest = /^sha256sum -- (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\S+)$/u.exec(args.command);\\\\\\\\n    if (digest) return `${createHash('\\\\\\\\''sha256'\\\\\\\\'').update(files.get(digest[1]) ?? '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'').digest('\\\\\\\\''hex'\\\\\\\\'')}  ${digest[1]}\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\n`;\\\\\\\\n    const cat = /^cat (\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\S+)$/u.exec(args.command);\\\\\\\\n    if (cat) return files.get(cat[1]) ?? `Output: \\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nError: cat: ${cat[1]}: No such file or directory\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\nExit Code: 1`;\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  return `Error: ${tool} is not simulated`;\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\nasync function drive(prompt, workspace, maxSteps = 12) {\\\\\\\\n  const files = new Map(Object.entries(workspace));\\\\\\\\n  const messages = [{ role: '\\\\\\\\''user'\\\\\\\\'', content: prompt }];\\\\\\\\n  const calls = [];\\\\\\\\n  for (let step = 0; step < maxSteps; step += 1) {\\\\\\\\n    const plan = await planChatStep(messages, TOOLS);\\\\\\\\n    if (!plan || plan.kind === '\\\\\\\\''final'\\\\\\\\'') return { calls, files, answer: plan ? plan.answer : null };\\\\\\\\n    const [call] = plan.calls;\\\\\\\\n    const args = JSON.parse(call.arguments);\\\\\\\\n    const id = `call_${step}`;\\\\\\\\n    calls.push(call.tool);\\\\\\\\n    messages.push({ role: '\\\\\\\\''assistant'\\\\\\\\'', content: '\\\\\\\\'''\\\\\\\\'', tool_calls: [{ id, type: '\\\\\\\\''function'\\\\\\\\'', function: { name: call.tool, arguments: call.arguments } }] });\\\\\\\\n    messages.push({ role: '\\\\\\\\''tool'\\\\\\\\'', tool_call_id: id, content: execute(files, call.tool, args) });\\\\\\\\n  }\\\\\\\\n  return { calls, files, answer: null };\\\\\\\\n}\\\\\\\\n\\\\\\\\ntest('\\\\\\\\''an '';\\\\n    if (!text.includes(args.oldString)) return 'Error: oldString not found in content';\\\\n    if (text.indexOf(args.oldString) !== text.lastIndexOf(args.oldString)) return 'Error: Found multiple matches for oldString.';\\\\n    files.set(path, text.replace(args.oldString, () => args.newString));\\\\n    return '';\\\\n  }\\\\n  if (tool === 'bash') {\\\\n    const event = runPlanEvent(files, args.command);\\\\n    if (event !== null) return event;\\\\n    const presence = args.command.match(/^test (! )?-e (\\\\\\\\S+)$/u);\\\\n    if (presence) return files.has(presence[2]) !== Boolean(presence[1]) ? '' : ['Output: ', 'Error: ', 'Exit Code: 1'].join(String.fromCharCode(10));\\\\n    if (args.command.startsWith('mkdir -p -- ')) return '';\\\\n    const transfer = args.command.match(/^(cp|mv) (\\\\\\\\S+) (\\\\\\\\S+)$/u);\\\\n    if (transfer && files.has(transfer[2])) {\\\\n      files.set(transfer[3], files.get(transfer[2]));\\\\n      if (transfer[1] === 'mv') files.delete(transfer[2]);\\\\n      return '';\\\\n    }\\\\n    const digest = /^sha256sum -- (\\\\\\\\S+)$/u.exec(args.command);\\\\n    if (digest) return `${createHash('sha256').update(files.get(digest[1]) ?? '').digest('hex')}  ${digest[1]}\\\\\\\\n`;\\\\n    const cat = /^cat (\\\\\\\\S+)$/u.exec(args.command);\\\\n    if (cat) return files.get(cat[1]) ?? `Output: \\\\\\\\nError: cat: ${cat[1]}: No such file or directory\\\\\\\\nExit Code: 1`;\\\\n  }\\\\n  return `Error: ${tool} is not simulated`;\\\\n}\\\\n\\\\nasync function drive(prompt, workspace, maxSteps = 12) {\\\\n  const files = new Map(Object.entries(workspace));\\\\n  const messages = [{ role: 'user', content: prompt }];\\\\n  const calls = [];\\\\n  for (let step = 0; step < maxSteps; step += 1) {\\\\n    const plan = await planChatStep(messages, TOOLS);\\\\n    if (!plan || plan.kind === 'final') return { calls, files, answer: plan ? /// One edit request changes one file, so such a request is declined with the
/// files named rather than applied to the first alone (mirrors
/// `severalEditTargets`).
pub(super) fn several_edit_targets(request: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>> {
    let composed = super::write_request::compose_edit_clauses(request)?;
    let segments = quoted_segment_spans(request);
    let toks = tokens(request);
    let (from, end) = edit_region(request, composed.spans);
    let counted = |index: usize| {
        let token = [REDACTED]];
        token.start >= from
            && token.start < end
            && !segments
                .iter()
                .any(|segment| token.start < segment.end && token.end > segment.start)
    };
    let mut targets: Vec<(usize, String)> = cued_write_targets(&toks)
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(index, _)| counted(*index))
        .collect();
    // A file listed after a cued one shares its cue (PR #1188 G104):
    // `In a.mjs and b.mjs, replace ...` names b.mjs as much as a.mjs.
    let cued: Vec<usize> = targets.iter().map(|(index, _)| *index).collect();
    for (index, path) in coordinated_paths(&toks, &cued) {
        if counted(index) {
            targets.push((index, path));
        }
    }
    targets.sort_by_key(|(index, _)| *index);
    let mut paths: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    for (_, path) in targets {
        if !paths.contains(&path) {
            paths.push(path);
        }
    }
    (paths.len() > 1).then_some(paths)
}

/// Strip seeded qualifiers and content leads only before a clause separator.
fn strip_clause_lead(raw: &str) -> &str {
    let modifiers = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_CONTENT_QUALIFIER);
    let mut qualifiers = modifiers.clone();
    for role in [
        seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_CONTENT_LEAD,
        "file_write_authoritative_content_lead",
    ] {
        for form in seed::lexicon()
            .role_word_forms(role)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|form| form.slot() == Slot::Prefix)
        {
            let lead = form.before_slot().trim().to_lowercase();
            qualifiers.extend(modifiers.iter().filter_map(|modifier| {
                let (before, _) = lead.split_once(modifier.as_str())?;
                (before.is_empty() || before.chars().next_back().is_some_and(char::is_whitespace))
                    .then(|| lead[before.len()..].to_owned())
            }));
            qualifiers.push(lead);
        }
    }
    let mut led = raw.trim();
    loop {
        let separated = led.trim_start_matches([':', '-', '—', '–']).trim();
        let shortened = strip_leading_qualifier(separated, &qualifiers);
        if shortened.len() == led.len() {
            return led;
        }
        led = shortened;
    }
}

This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the

## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

/// Plan the next step of a "find this out and record it at PATH" request.
///
/// Three states, in the order they occur:
///
/// * the write has already been attempted — report what happened, truthfully;
/// * the router still wants tool calls for the residual — pass them through, so
///   the investigation runs under the ordinary routes;
/// * the router has an answer — write it to the named path, under the pinned
///   first line when the caller pinned one.
pub(super) fn plan_evidence_record_step(
    task: &str,
    messages: &[ChatMessage],
    tool_names: &[&str],
    result: &mut Option<FinalResult>,
) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
    let obligation = parse_obligation(task)?;
    // A later producer of the same target owns its bytes.
    if let Some(reason) = later_route_delivering(task, &obligation, tool_names) {
        trace_route("evidence_record", reason);
        return None;
    }
    let write_tool = tool_for(tool_names, Capability::Write)?;
    let progress = Progress::scan(messages);
    match super::task_obligations::observed_file_outcome(task, &obligation.target, messages) {
        ObligationOutcome::Satisfied { .. } => {
            let content = progress.successful_write_content_for(&obligation.target);
            if let Some(plan) = plan_record_readback_step(
                task,
                &obligation.target,
                content.as_deref(),
                &progress,
                tool_names,
                result,
            ) {
                return Some(plan);
            }
            if let Some(plan) = discovery_delivery::recorded_discovery_gap(
                &obligation,
                content.as_deref(),
                &progress,
                tool_names,
                task,
                result,
            ) {

/**
 * Mirrors `fn plan_chat_step` in rust/src/agentic_coding/planner.rs.
 * @param {Array<object>} messages parsed chat messages
 * @param {Array<string>} toolNames the grounded advertised tool names
 * @returns {Promise<object|null>} an `AgenticPlan` or null
 */
export async function planChatStep(messages, toolNames) {
  const observer = hasHost() ? host().planningObserver?.() : null;
  if (!observer) return projectPlan(await planChatStepResolved(messages, toolNames));
  const events = new EventLog();
  events.append('impulse', latestUserRequest(messages) ?? '');
  try {
    const resolved = await planChatStepResolved(messages, toolNames),
      projected = projectPlan(resolved);
    events.append('agentic:resolved', jsonText(resolved));
    events.append('render:emit', jsonText(projected));
    observer({
      schema: 'formal-ai-planner-observation-v1',
      messages,
      tools: toolNames,
      resolved,
      projected,
      eventLog: events.events,
      derivation: toLino(recordFor(events.events, answerDerivationId(jsonText(projected))))
    });
    return projected;
  } catch (error) {
    events.append('agentic:failed', String(error?.name ?? 'ThrownValue'));
    observer({
      schema: 'formal-ai-planner-failure-v1',
      messages,
      tools: toolNames,
      eventLog: events.events,
      error: {
        name: String(error?.name ?? 'ThrownValue'),
        message: String(error?.message ?? error)
      }
    });
    throw error;
  }
}

//!
//! The general planner and request inspection share this parse (issues #654, #1066).

use super::file_path_shape::{is_dotted_number, peel_sentence_punctuation};

    first_raw_content_lead_end, first_raw_prefix_lead_end, raw_content_lead_close,
    raw_lowercase_span,

/// One whitespace token together with its byte span in the original request.

    pub(super) text: &'a str,
    pub(super) start: usize,
    pub(super) end: usize,
    pub(super) request: &'a str,
}
/// Split whitespace and ideographic punctuation while retaining byte spans.
/// Without punctuation boundaries, an unspaced clause can become one path token.
pub(super) fn tokens(request: &str) -> Vec<Token<'_>> {
    let mut out = Vec::new();
    let mut start: Option<usize> = None;
    for (index, character) in request.char_indices() {
        if character.is_whitespace() || is_ideographic_punctuation(character) {
            if let Some(from) = start.take() {
                out.push(Token {
                    text: &request[from..index],
                    start: from,
                    end: index,
                    request,
                });
            }
            continue;
        }
        if start.is_none() {
            start = Some(index);
        }
    }
    if let Some(from) = start {
        out.push(Token {
            text: &request[from..],
            start: from,
            end: request.len(),
            request,
        });
    }
    out
}

function trailingCue(token, cues, fused) {
  const cleaned = cleanCueToken(token.text);
  for (const cue of cues) {
    if (cleaned === cue) return [token.start, token.end];
    if (fused && containsCjk(cue) && cleaned.endsWith(cue)) return [Math.max(0, token.end - cue.length), token.end];
  }
  return null;
}
function leadingCue(token, cues, fused) {
  const cleaned = cleanCueToken(token.text);
  for (const cue of cues) {
    if (cleaned === cue) return [token.start, token.end];
    if (fused && containsCjk(cue) && cleaned.startsWith(cue)) return [token.start, token.start + cue.length];
  }
  return null;
}
/** Mirrors `fn quoted_as_value`. */
function quotedAsValue(word) {
  const bare = peelSentencePunctuation(word, (token) => trimEndMatches(token, charIn(',:;')));
  return bare.length >= 2 && bare.startsWith('"') && bare.endsWith('"');
}
/** Mirrors `fn stated_write_target`. @param {string} request @returns {string|null} */
export function statedWriteTarget(request) {
  return cuedWriteTarget(tokens(request))?.[1] ?? null;
}
/** Mirrors `fn typed_write_target`. @param {string} request @param {string} extension */
export function typedWriteTarget(request, extension) {
  return cuedWriteTargets(tokens(request)).map(([, path]) => path).find((path) => pathExtension(path) === extension) ?? null;
}
/** `Path::extension` of a relative path, or null: Rust built-in `Path::extension`. */
export function pathExtension(path) {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-secrets.sh
#
# Scans the files a change touches for committed credentials, using secretlint
# with the recommended preset (CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 11 / issue #808).
#
# Usage:
#   BASE_REF=main bash scripts/check-secrets.sh     # scan the diff vs BASE_REF
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh --all             # scan every tracked file
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh path/to/file ...  # scan specific files
#
# Exit code 0 = no secrets found; non-zero = a finding or scanner failure.
#
# Why the diff and not the whole tree
# -----------------------------------
# The js template runs `secretlint "**/*"`. Measured on this repository that
# does not finish in a usable time: the glob walks the working tree (including
# `target/` and ~150 MB of committed case-study logs) and the scan was still
# running after 25 minutes locally. A gate that cannot be relied on to finish is
# a new CI failure mode, which is the opposite of what issue #808 asks for.
#
# Scanning what the change touches keeps the gate fast and catches the case that
# matters: a credential being *introduced*. Pre-existing files are not re-scanned
# on every pull request; run `--all` (no timeout) to audit the whole tree.
#
# FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG=[REDACTED] prints the resolved file list before scanning.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
debug() {
  if [ "${FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG:[REDACTED]}" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[check-secrets] %s\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}
# Captured third-party CI/agent logs kept verbatim as evidence. They are
# reviewed when added and consist of redacted GitHub Actions output.
exclude() {
  local status=0
  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}

export function ladderTestLogFilename(target, filter) {
  if (typeof target !== 'string' || !/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9-]*$/u.test(target)
    || typeof filter !== 'string' || !filter || /[\0\r\n]/u.test(filter)) {

  return 'cargo-test-' + digest + '.log';
}

        prompt: String,

/// Read the conversation the harness itself stored for this session.
fn harness_context(
    session: &str,
    db: Option<&Path>,
    log_dir: Option<&Path>,
) -> Result<Value, Box<dyn Error>> {
    if db.is_none()
        && let Some(harness) = harness::current()
    {
        return harness.export(session, log_dir);
    }
    opencode_context(session, db)
}
fn opencode_context(session: &str, db: Option<&Path>) -> Result<Value, Box<dyn Error>> {
    let output = run_extractor(&[session, "--format", "json"], db).map_err(|error| {
        config("context_harness_unavailable")
            .replace(SESSION_PLACEHOLDER, session)
            .replace(ERROR_PLACEHOLDER, &error.to_string())
    })?;
    Ok(serde_json::from_slice(&output)?)
}

/**

 * `FORMAL_AI_TRACE_REQUESTS` environment flag is set; the planner host has no
 * environment (the browser worker must load this module), so this is a no-op.

  void route;
  void value;

    printf '%s\tFAIL\tformal_ai_server_start\n' "$id" | tee -a "$RUN_LOG"
    tail -100 "$session_dir/formal-ai.log" >&2 || true
    return 1

  # and Formal AI counts one token per character, so a single read and write of

    2>/dev/null || true)"

/// A name the codec's key escape leaves alone, so the probe record's shape in
/// [`format_lino_value`] is known exactly.
const PROBE: &str = "v";
pub fn format_lino_record(id: &str, pairs: &[(&str, String)]) -> String {
    let sanitized = pairs
        .iter()
        .map(|(key, value)| (*key, sanitize_lino_value(value)))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();

        .iter()
        .map(|(key, value)| (*key, value.as_str()))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    format_indented_ordered(id, &borrowed, "  ")
        .expect("static Links Notation records should be valid")
}

/// Decode a double-quoted value, reading both escapes this repository writes:
/// Links Notation's own doubled delimiter, and the backslash dialect
/// [`crate::links_format::sanitize_lino_value`] emits for this line-based reader.
///
/// The `t` and `r` arms exist because that writer emits `\t` and `\r`. Without
/// them a tab was written and then read back as the two characters `\` and `t`,
/// which is silent corruption of exactly the content issue #715 is about: a
/// Makefile recipe line is *required* to begin with a tab, and Go is
/// conventionally tab-indented, so a substitution rule derived from such a
/// fragment round-tripped into one that no longer matched the code it came from.
///
/// The catch-all is load-bearing and stays: it passes an unknown escape through
/// with its backslash, which is what lets a value carrying prose or LaTeX
/// (`\ldots`) survive a reader that has no arm for it.
pub fn unescape_value(raw: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(raw.len());
    let mut iter = raw.chars().peekable();
    while let Some(c) = iter.next() {
        if take_doubled(&mut out, c, '"', &mut iter) {
            continue;
        }
        if c == '\\' {
            match iter.next() {
                Some('n') => out.push('\n'),
                Some('t') => out.push('\t'),
                Some('r') => out.push('\r'),
                Some('"') => out.push('"'),
                Some('\\') | None => out.push('\\'),
                Some(other) => {
                    out.push('\\');
                    out.push(other);
                }
            }
        } else {
            out.push(c);
        }
    }
    out
}

async function symbolicAnswer(residual) {
  const answer = await solve(residual);
  if (!answer) return null;
  const text = trim(answer.answer ?? '');
  if (text === '') return null;
  // Preserve symbolic decline behavior; only a conclusive answer certifies a finding.
  if (answer.intent.endsWith(GAP_INTENT_SUFFIX) || isInconclusive(answer)
    || defersToTheOpenWeb(answer) || announcesAListItDoesNotMake(answer)) return null;
  return resolvedFinalAnswer(text, FinalDisposition.Finding, answer.intent);
}
function withResidualRequest(messages, residual) {
  let index = -1;
  for (let at = messages.length - 1; at >= 0; at -= 1) {
    if (messages[at].role === 'user' && !isContinuationCue(plainText(messages[at].content))) {
      index = at;
      break;
    }
  }
  if (index < 0) return null;

  out[index].content = residual;

    if (message.role.toLowerCase() !== 'user') out.push({ ...message });
  }
  return out;
}

fn nested_node_values_round_trip_through_the_production_seed_reader() {

// The `SymbolicAnswer` readers of rust/src/engine_answer.rs the planner
// consults. An answer is the host solver's `{intent, answer, ...}` shape.
/** Mirrors `SymbolicAnswer::asks_for_clarification`. */
export function asksForClarification(answer) {
  return answer.intent.startsWith('clarify');
}
/** Mirrors `SymbolicAnswer::is_inconclusive`. */
export function isInconclusive(answer) {
  return ['unknown', 'ill_formed', 'punctuation_only_prompt', 'concept_lookup_unresolved', 'meta_reasoning_open', 'meta_reasoned_program_unverified'].includes(answer.intent)
    || asksForClarification(answer);
}
/** Mirrors `SymbolicAnswer::defers_to_the_open_web`. */
export function defersToTheOpenWeb(answer) {
  return answer.intent === 'web_search';
}
/** Mirrors `SymbolicAnswer::announces_a_list_it_does_not_make`. */
export function announcesAListItDoesNotMake(answer) {
  const text = answer.answer.replace(/\p{White_Space}+$/u, '');
  return text.endsWith(':') || text.endsWith('：');
}
  return wordCount <= Number(handlerRulesPolicy("response_language_followup", "terse-word-limit") || 0);
}

function isInconclusiveReplayIntent(intent) {
  const value = String(intent || "");
  return (
    value === "unknown" ||
    value === "ill_formed" ||
    value === "punctuation_only_prompt" ||
    value === "concept_lookup_unresolved" ||
    value.startsWith("clarify")
  );
}

js/agentic/host.mjs:121:export function solve(prompt, history = []) {
js/server/worker-host.mjs:24:export const REPO_ROOT = path.resolve(path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), "../..");
// The host the JavaScript agentic planner runs against (R1015).
//
// The planner (js/agentic/*.mjs) is a port of rust/src/agentic_coding/ and
// stays host-agnostic so the browser worker can load it later: it never
// touches `node:fs` or the network itself. Everything it needs from outside
// comes through one installed host:
//
// * `readText(relative)` - a repository file (seed and meta data) as text,
//   the twin of the Rust `include_str!` of `embedded/data/...`;
// * `parseLino(text)` - the shared Links Notation parser
//   (`js/seed_loader.js`, `FormalAiSeed.parse`), returning
//   `{name, id, value, children}` nodes;
// * `realm` - the booted browser worker's global scope, whose ports of
//   `crate::seed::lexicon()`, `crate::engine::normalize_prompt`,
//   `crate::language::detect` and the handler rules the planner calls instead
//   of porting them twice;
// * `solve(prompt, history)` - the host solver's answer, a Promise of the
//   Rust `SymbolicAnswer` shape (`{intent, answer, confidence,
//   evidence_links, thinking_steps, links_notation}`), for the few routes
//   that consult `crate::solve_with_history`;
// * `isDirectory(path)` / `isFile(path)` / `currentDirectory()` - the few
//   filesystem probes the Rust planner makes (`Path::is_dir`, the server's
//   own working directory). A browser host answers `false` / `null`;
// * `listDirectory(relative)` - the entries of a repository directory as
//   `[{name, isDirectory}]` (the twin of build.rs's `fs::read_dir` over
//   `rust/src` that embeds `OWNED_SOURCE_FILES`). A browser host answers `[]`.
//
// The JavaScript server installs a host once its worker has booted

 * @param {object} result the worker's `solve` value
 * @param {Array<{role: string, content: string}>} [history] the turns it was solved after
 * @returns {SymbolicAnswer}
 */
export function symbolicFromWorker(result, history = [], { readOnly = false } = {}) {
  const answer = nativeProgramAnswer(String(result?.content ?? ''), result?.programExecution);
  if (!readOnly) noteLearned(result?.memoryOperation);
  const log = solverLogFromWorker(result, history);
  return {
    ...(result?.outputProjection ? {output_projection:result.outputProjection} : {}),
    intent: String(result?.intent ?? 'unknown'),
    answer,
    confidence: Number(result?.confidence ?? 0),
    evidence_links: solverEvidenceLinks(result, history)
      ?? (Array.isArray(result?.evidence) ? result.evidence.map(String) : []),
    // The native solver's event log when the worker recorded one (it always
    // does on the finalize path); the browser trace otherwise.
    thinking_steps: Array.isArray(result?.solverEvents)
      ? thinkingStepsFromEvents(result.solverEvents, answer)
      : thinkingStepsFromWorker(result?.steps || []),
    links_notation: answerLinksFromLog(log, String(result?.intent ?? 'unknown'), answer),
    // Off the wire: the raw traces `learning_trace_from_symbolic_answer`
    // (js/server/self-improvement.mjs) rebuilds the solver log from.
    worker_steps: Array.isArray(result?.steps) ? result.steps : [],
    solver_events: log?.events,
    // Off the wire: a function the browser synthesized, which the agentic
    // reroute turns into an execution recipe (`attachExecutionRecipe`).
    synthesized_program: result?.synthesizedProgram ?? undefined,
  };
}

const NATIVE_PROMPT_LINK = /^prompt:prompt_[0-9a-f]{16}$/u;
/**
 * The worker's own evidence without what `finalize` appends after it: the
 * browser trace (`trace:<event>` per dispatch event) and the native links of
 * its log, which open with the prompt link. What is left is the handler's.
 */
function handlerEvidence(evidence) {
  const native = evidence.findIndex((link) => NATIVE_PROMPT_LINK.test(link));
  let end = native < 0 ? evidence.length : native;
  while (end > 0 && evidence[end - 1].startsWith(BROWSER_TRACE_PREFIX)) end -= 1;
  return evidence.slice(0, end);
}
/**
 * Mirrors rust/src/event_log.rs `build_evidence_links` over the native log
 * the worker recorded (`solverEvents`), after the `prior_turn:*` events
 * `solve_with_history` opens the log with; a meta-reasoner answer extends the
 * links with its own evidence (rust/src/meta_reasoner/integration.rs
 * `project`). Null when the worker recorded no native log.
 */
export function solverEvidenceLinks(result, history = []) {
  const events = Array.isArray(result?.solverEvents) ? result.solverEvents : null;
  if (!events) return null;
  const priorTurns = (history || []).map((turn) => ({
    kind: turn?.role === ASSISTANT_ROLE ? PRIOR_TURN_ASSISTANT : PRIOR_TURN_USER,
    payload: String(turn?.content ?? ''),
  }));
  const links = eventLogEvidenceLinks([...priorTurns, ...events], result?.intent);
  if (!links) return null;
  const response = events.findLast((event) => event.kind === RESPONSE_KIND);
  if (response?.payload === META_RESPONSE_LINK && Array.isArray(result?.evidence)) {
    links.push(...handlerEvidence(result.evidence.map(String)));
  }
  return links;
}

/** Kinds whose link is `{kind}:{payload with every space as '_'}` (issue #674). */
const SPACE_AS_UNDERSCORE_KINDS = new Set(['skill_gap', 'program_gap']);
/** Kinds whose link is the bare kind, the payload dropped. */
const BARE_KINDS = new Set([
  'fact_query:cache:miss', 'fact_query:cache:bypass', 'fact_query:force_fresh',
  'policy:chat_bounded_autonomy', 'policy:add_only_history',
  'policy:destructive_action_requires_confirmation', 'policy:cache_flush_requires_confirmation',
  'policy:offline', 'policy:inappropriate_content',
  'policy:guessed_under_ambiguity', 'policy:clarify_under_ambiguity',
]);
/** Kinds whose link is `source:{payload}`. */
const SOURCE_KINDS = new Set(['docs_method:source', 'source', 'release_timeline:source']);
const OFFLINE_SKIP = 'skipped:offline';
/** The typed evidence link for one event: one arm of `build_evidence_links`. */
export function evidenceLink(event) {
  const { kind, id } = event;
  const payload = String(event.payload);
  if (kind === 'response') return payload;
  if (PAYLOAD_KINDS.has(kind)) return `${kind}:${payload}`;
  if (SPACE_AS_COLON_KINDS.has(kind)) return `${kind}:${payload.split(' ').join(':')}`;
  if (SPACE_AS_UNDERSCORE_KINDS.has(kind)) return `${kind}:${payload.split(' ').join('_')}`;
  if (BARE_KINDS.has(kind)) return kind;
  if (SOURCE_KINDS.has(kind)) return `source:${payload}`;
  if (kind === 'release_timeline:hit') return `release_timeline:${payload}`;
  if (kind === 'spelling_correction') return `${kind}:${payload.split(' ').join('')}`;
  if (kind === 'program_parameters') return `${kind}:${payload.replace(/[ ,]/g, ':')}`;
  if (kind === 'search:external' && payload === OFFLINE_SKIP) return 'policy:offline';
  return `${kind}:${id}`;
}

// `candidate:`, `policy:*`, `response:*` ...). The worker's own links stay
// first, so the native block opens with the prompt link and holds only the
// links the answer does not carry yet.
function recordSolverEventLog(result, prompt, answer) {
  result.rawSolverEvents = solverEventLog(prompt, answer);
  result.solverEvents = crateModule(SOLVER_EVENT_PROJECTION_MODULE).nativeSolverLog(result);
  const links = crateModule(SOLVER_EVENT_LOG_MODULE).eventLogEvidenceLinks(result.solverEvents, answer.intent);
  if (!links) return;
  const present = new Set(result.evidence);
  result.evidence = [...result.evidence, ...links.filter((link) => !present.has(link))];
}

//! History-aware response-language retargeting.
//!
//! A follow-up such as "I do not understand English, write in Russian" is not a
//! new factual question. It asks the solver to preserve the previous user
//! request's semantic object and rerender that answer in the named response
//! language.
//!
//! Issue #556 generalizes this beyond a single hardcoded handler: rather than
//! re-running one project-lookup path, the follow-up replays the previous
//! request through the *whole* solver with the requested language forced onto
//! every localizable answer family (concept lookup, repository/project lookup,
//! …). This is the universal recursive-reasoning step — the solver re-derives
//! the prior answer, now constrained to speak the requested language — so the
//! retarget covers the entire class of answerable requests, not just one shape.
//!
//! Both the language marker and the "I cannot understand" trigger are grounded

//! the response-language marker role and [`detect_comprehension_failure`] reads

//! Issue #1138 B8 (plan 08, L9–L11): the program runs, and its stdout is the answer.
//!
//! What separates this route from a pattern table is that something is actually
//! executed: the composed program is run and what it printed is the answer. The
//! self-checks are observations, not adjectives — an answer that only *ran* is
//! reported as computed-but-uncorroborated, "verified" is reserved for agreement
//! or a round trip, and two disjoint derivations that disagree produce a gap
//! rather than a guess.
use formal_ai::FormalAiEngine;
use super::{LANGUAGES, case};
fn trailing_number(answer: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let digits: String = answer
        .chars()
        .rev()
        .skip_while(|c| !c.is_ascii_digit())
        .take_while(char::is_ascii_digit)
        .collect();
    if digits.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(digits.chars().rev().collect())
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# External verifier for one Agent CLI ladder node (issues #1028, #1066, #1085).
#
# The verdict never trusts the agent's own words: a leaf must have changed the
# one tracked file its task names, the file must still format, compile and pass
# the unit tests of its module; a depth-4 composite must compose both verified
# child effects and both children's diffs must apply to one tree and compile;
# a node at depth 3 or above is requirement-shaped, so every leaf marker under
# it must be present, only those files modified, and the tree must compile and
# pass the tests of every touched module (issue #1085 D4).
#
# Environment (all optional):
#   LADDER_CARGO_CHECK=0       skip `cargo check --lib`
#   LADDER_CARGO_TEST=0        skip `cargo test --test unit <module>`
#   LADDER_CARGO_TARGET_DIR    shared target directory (run.sh sets one per run)
#   LADDER_VERIFY_LOG_DIR     write receipt and Cargo logs here as they appear
#   LADDER_LEAVES              leaves.tsv (requirement-shaped nodes)
#   LADDER_LEAF_SPAN=start-end leaf numbers under a requirement-shaped node
#   LADDER_CHILD_DIFFS         two diff files a depth-4 composite must merge
set -uo pipefail

  exit 2

: > "$report" || exit 2
fail() {
  printf '%s\n' "$1"

}

//! Issue #1138 B8 (plan 08, L9–L11): the program runs, and its stdout is the answer.
//!
//! What separates this route from a pattern table is that something is actually
//! executed: the composed program is run and what it printed is the answer. The
//! self-checks are observations, not adjectives — an answer that only *ran* is
//! reported as computed-but-uncorroborated, "verified" is reserved for agreement
//! or a round trip, and two disjoint derivations that disagree produce a gap
//! rather than a guess.
use formal_ai::FormalAiEngine;
use super::{LANGUAGES, case};
fn trailing_number(answer: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let digits: String = answer
        .chars()
        .rev()
        .skip_while(|c| !c.is_ascii_digit())
        .take_while(char::is_ascii_digit)
        .collect();
    if digits.is_empty() {
        None
    } else {
        Some(digits.chars().rev().collect())
    }
}

This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the
