+#[test]
+fn the_result_and_proof_retain_each_verified_edit_in_a_sequence() {
+    let source = "settings/options.txt";
+    let prompt = "Insert the line «cobalt dawn» after the line «azure noon» in settings/options.txt, +        then delete the line «stale entry» from settings/options.txt. Create +        `agent-ladder-effects/node.lino` with these exact field lines: `kind=edit` and +        `result=<each verified edit>`. Leave supporting evidence in .agent-ladder/node-proof.md. +        The first line must be exactly `proof_for=edit`.";
+    let mut workspace = ToolWorkspace::new(prompt);
+    workspace
+        .write_initial(source, "azure noon\nstale entry\n")
+        .unwrap();
+    let mut messages = vec![ChatMessage::user(prompt)];
+    for turn in 0..14 {
+        let Some(AgenticPlan::ToolCalls(calls)) = plan_chat_step(&messages, &LADDER_TOOLS) else {
+            break;
+        };
+        for (index, call) in calls.iter().enumerate() {
+            let id = format!("sequence-delivery-{turn}-{index}");
+            messages.push(ChatMessage::assistant_tool_calls(vec![ToolCall::function(
+                &id,
+                &call.tool,
+                &call.arguments,
+            )]));
+            messages.push(workspace.execute(&id, call));
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(workspace.read(source).unwrap(), "azure noon\ncobalt dawn\n");
+    let effect = workspace.read("agent-ladder-effects/node.lino").unwrap();
+    let proof = workspace.read(".agent-ladder/node-proof.md").unwrap();
+    assert!(proof.starts_with("proof_for=edit\n"), "{proof}");
+    let result = effect
+        .lines()
+        .find_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("result="))
+        .expect("verified edits have a result");
+    for evidence in [result, &proof] {
+        assert!(evidence.contains("cobalt dawn"), "{evidence}");
+        assert!(evidence.contains("stale entry"), "{evidence}");
+    }
+}

// The host the JavaScript agentic planner runs against (R1015).
//
// The planner (js/agentic/*.mjs) is a port of rust/src/agentic_coding/ and
// stays host-agnostic so the browser worker can load it later: it never
// touches `node:fs` or the network itself. Everything it needs from outside
// comes through one installed host:
//
// * `readText(relative)` - a repository file (seed and meta data) as text,
//   the twin of the Rust `include_str!` of `embedded/data/...`;
// * `parseLino(text)` - the shared Links Notation parser
//   (`js/seed_loader.js`, `FormalAiSeed.parse`), returning
//   `{name, id, value, children}` nodes;
// * `realm` - the booted browser worker's global scope, whose ports of
//   `crate::seed::lexicon()`, `crate::engine::normalize_prompt`,
//   `crate::language::detect` and the handler rules the planner calls instead
//   of porting them twice;
// * `solve(prompt, history)` - the host solver's answer, a Promise of the
//   Rust `SymbolicAnswer` shape (`{intent, answer, confidence,
//   evidence_links, thinking_steps, links_notation}`), for the few routes
//   that consult `crate::solve_with_history`;
// * `isDirectory(path)` / `isFile(path)` / `currentDirectory()` - the few
//   filesystem probes the Rust planner makes (`Path::is_dir`, the server's
//   own working directory). A browser host answers `false` / `null`;
// * `listDirectory(relative)` - the entries of a repository directory as
//   `[{name, isDirectory}]` (the twin of build.rs's `fs::read_dir` over
//   `rust/src` that embeds `OWNED_SOURCE_FILES`). A browser host answers `[]`.
//
// The JavaScript server installs a host once its worker has booted
// (js/server/agentic.mjs); node:test suites install the same one through
// js/agentic/node-host.mjs.
let current = null;
const caches = new Map();

/** Mirrors `WorkspaceCensus::compile` over already-censused modules. */
export function workspaceCensus(modules) {
  return { modules: [...modules].sort((a, b) => (a.path < b.path ? -1 : a.path > b.path ? 1 : 0)) };
}
/** Mirrors `fn workspace`: navigation from the host's current owned sources. */
export function workspace() {
  return cached('self-ast-census', () => {
    const documents = hasHost() && typeof host().censusDocuments === 'function' ? host().censusDocuments() : [];
    return workspaceCensus(documents.map((document) => document.module ?? moduleFromDocument(document.text)).filter(Boolean));
  });
}
/** Mirrors `ModuleCensus::symbol`. */
export function moduleSymbol(module, name) {
  return module.symbols.find((symbol) => symbol.name === name) ?? null;
}
/** Mirrors `WorkspaceCensus::module`. */
export function censusModule(census, modulePath) {
  return census.modules.find((module) => module.path === modulePath) ?? null;
}
/** Mirrors `WorkspaceCensus::module_by_reference`. */
export function moduleByReference(census, reference) {
  const exact = censusModule(census, reference);
  if (exact) return exact;
  const matches = census.modules.filter((module) => module.path.endsWith(`/${reference}`));
  return matches.length === 1 ? matches[0] : null;
}
/** Mirrors `WorkspaceCensus::modules_declaring`. */
export function modulesDeclaring(census, name) {
  return census.modules.filter((module) => moduleSymbol(module, name) !== null);
}

/** Mirrors `fn failure_message`. */
export function failureMessage(raw, explicitlyFailed, inferFromProse) {
  const result = normalize(raw);
  if (result.error !== null) return result.error;
  if (explicitlyFailed || (inferFromProse && result.exit_code !== 0 && looksLikeError(result.payload))) {
    return trim(result.payload) ? result.payload : trim(raw);
  }
  return null;
}
/** Mirrors fn incomplete_receipt: declared partial observations cannot certify bytes. */
export function incompleteReceipt(raw) {
  const value = parseJson(trim(raw));
  return isObject(value) && (value.complete === false || value.stream_complete === false
    || value.truncated === true || value.timed_out === true || value.aborted === true
    || (typeof value.signal === 'string' && value.signal.length > 0));
}

}

/** Mirrors `fn failure_message`. */
export function failureMessage(raw, explicitlyFailed, inferFromProse) {
  const result = normalize(raw);
  if (result.error !== null) return result.error;
  if (explicitlyFailed || (inferFromProse && result.exit_code !== 0 && looksLikeError(result.payload))) {
    return trim(result.payload) ? result.payload : trim(raw);
  }
  return null;
}
/** Mirrors fn incomplete_receipt: declared partial observations cannot certify bytes. */
export function incompleteReceipt(raw) {
  const value = parseJson(trim(raw));
  return isObject(value) && (value.complete === false || value.stream_complete === false
    || value.truncated === true || value.timed_out === true || value.aborted === true
    || (typeof value.signal === 'string' && value.signal.length > 0));
}

    path: &str,
) -> Option<&'a ToolAttempt> {

        }
    }
    None

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) enum Binding {
    Exact,
    Unknown,
    Contradicted,
}
pub(super) struct QualifiedToolAttempt {
    capability: Capability,
    declared_tool: String,
    call_id: String,
    arguments_value: Value,
    declaration_arguments: String,
    pub(super) binding: Binding,
    duplicate: bool,
    receipt_present: bool,
    pub(super) succeeded: bool,
    pub(super) detail: String,
}
impl QualifiedToolAttempt {
    pub(super) fn declaration_arguments(&self) -> &str {
        &self.declaration_arguments
    }
    pub(super) fn declared_tool(&self) -> &str {
        &self.declared_tool
    }
    pub(super) const fn arguments_value(&self) -> &Value {
        &self.arguments_value
    }
    pub(super) const fn capability(&self) -> Capability {
        self.capability
    }
    pub(super) fn targets_path(&self, path: &str) -> bool {
        super::progress::source_read_path(&self.arguments_value.to_string()).as_deref()
            == Some(path)
    }
    pub(super) fn arguments_match(&self, arguments: &Value) -> bool {
        argument_values_equal(&self.arguments_value, arguments)
    }
    pub(super) const fn has_receipt(&self) -> bool {
        self.receipt_present
    }
    pub(super) fn matches_receipt(&self, tool: &str, raw: &str) -> bool {
        self.binding == Binding::Exact
            && self.receipt_present
            && self.declared_tool == tool
            && self.detail == raw
    }
}

//! Issue #1069: a *change-shaped* delegation must reach a real source edit.
//!
//! The issue #1028 ladder only ever asked the Agent CLI to inspect a tracked
//! file and record what it saw, so every rung was satisfiable by writing a
//! self-describing side file. `experiments/issue_1069_change_shaped_delegation`
//! asks instead for a diff to a tracked file and reads only that file back. The
//! first run of that probe failed: given
//!
//! > edit `src/orchestration/workspace.rs` … add `"node_modules"` to that same
//! > list
//!
//! the planner emitted **no tool calls at all** and answered with a dictionary
//! definition of Rust, because `structured_edit` only recognised one request
//! shape — a single quoted value inserted into a *named Rust array* whose kind
//! the request spelled with the word "array".
//!
//! Generalising that one shape into "apply the described member insertion to the
//! member list the file actually contains" is what these tests pin. The anchor,
//! the delimiters and the separator are all read out of the target's bytes
//! rather than out of the request's wording, so the same recipe covers a bracket
//! array, a `matches!` alternation and a parenthesised tuple without a new
//! branch per shape.
use formal_ai::agentic_coding::{
    AgenticPlan, PlannedToolCall, plan_chat_step, tool_result::complete_owned_source_read_frame,
};
use formal_ai::{ChatMessage, ToolCall};
const TOOLS: [&str; 3] = ["read_file", "write_file", "run_shell_command"];
fn next_call(messages: &[ChatMessage]) -> PlannedToolCall {
    match plan_chat_step(messages, &TOOLS) {
        Some(AgenticPlan::ToolCalls(mut calls)) if calls.len() == 1 => calls.remove(0),
        other => panic!("expected exactly one planned tool call, got {other:?}"),
    }
}

function insertMembers(source, edit) {
  if (edit.named.length) {
    const viaLinks = insertMembersViaLinks(source, edit.named[0], edit.values);
    if (viaLinks) return viaLinks;
  }
  const bytes = encoder.encode(source);
  const [regions, literals] = scan(bytes);
  const anchor = anchorByMembers(regions, literals, edit.values) ?? anchorByName(source, bytes, regions, literals, edit.named);
  if (!anchor) return null;
  const members = directMembers(literals, anchor.open);
  const absent = edit.values.filter((value) => !members.some((member) => member.value === value));

function exactFieldLines(sentence, target) {
  const fields = sentence.split('`')
    .filter((_, index) => index % 2 === 1)
    .map(trim)
    .flatMap((quoted) => {
      if (quoted === target) return [];
      const equals = quoted.indexOf('=');
      if (equals < 0 || !/^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/.test(quoted.slice(0, equals))) return [];
      if (!Array.from(quoted).some(isWhitespace)) return [quoted];
      // A prose description inside angle brackets declares an open field.
      const value = quoted.slice(equals + 1);
      return /^<[^<>\r\n]+>$/u.test(value) && trim(value.slice(1, -1)) !== '' ? [quoted.slice(0, equals + 1)] : [];
    });

}
function workBeforeDelivery(sentence) {
  const start = firstActionCueStart(tokens(sentence));
  if (start === null || start === undefined) return null;
  const work = withoutTrailingSeparator(trim(sentence.slice(0, start)));
  return Array.from(work).some(isAlphanumeric) ? work : null;
}
function withoutTrailingSeparator(work) {
  const lowered = work.toLowerCase();
  let best = null;
  for (const separator of bareSurfaces('skill_procedure_clause_separator')) {
    if (!lowered.endsWith(separator)) continue;
    const kept = work.slice(0, work.length - separator.length);
    const last = Array.from(kept).pop();
    if (last === undefined || !isWhitespace(last)) continue;
    const trimmedKept = trimEnd(kept);
    if (best === null || trimmedKept.length < best.length) best = trimmedKept;
  }
  return best ?? work;
}

/** Mirrors `fn preserved_first_user_turn`. */
export function preservedFirstUserTurn(summary) {
  const split = splitOnce(summary, '\n\nUser turns:\n');
  if (!split) return null;
  let rest = split[1];
  for (let number = 1; ; number += 1) {
    const body = stripPrefix(rest, `  ${number}. `);
    if (body === null) return null;
    const next = body.indexOf(`\n  ${number + 1}.`);
    const end = next < 0 ? body.length : next;
    const task = trim(body.slice(0, end));
    if (task && isStandingTask(task)) return task;
    if (next < 0) return null;
    rest = body.slice(end + 1);
  }
}

//! (issue #1085 D2.2).
//!
//! The self-AST census is the links network over the workspace's own source.
//! A requirement such as "add wikiquote as a web search provider" is resolved
//! by querying it for the `const` or `static` whose identifier words the
//! requirement contains, or for the identifier the requirement names, so the
//! prompt never has to name `src/web_search_core.rs`.
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use crate::self_ast_census::{ModuleCensus, SymbolSpan, WorkspaceCensus, workspace};
/// Where a requirement lands: the module and the declaration it changes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RequirementTarget {
    pub module_path: String,
    pub symbol: String,
    pub kind: String,
}
/// Resolve `requirement` against the live workspace census.
#[must_use]
pub fn resolve_requirement_target(requirement: &str) -> Option<RequirementTarget> {
    resolve_in(workspace(), requirement)
}
/// Resolve `requirement` against `census`.
///
/// An identifier the requirement names verbatim wins; otherwise the `const` or
/// `static` whose identifier words (singularised) all occur in the requirement
/// wins, longest identifier first. A tie between modules is broken by the
/// module path words the requirement mentions; a remaining tie is ambiguity and
/// resolves to nothing rather than to a guess. When identifier words do not bind,
/// an actual canonical seed surface and its semantic role can bind its declared owner.
#[must_use]

        resolve_scoped(census, requirement)
    } else {

// Numbered source requirements used as the work for a verified delivery.
import { renderSeededChange } from './code_task.mjs';
import { latestUserRequest } from './content.mjs';
import { quotedSegmentSpans } from './crate/normal_markov.mjs';
import { hasHost, host } from './host.mjs';
import { FinalDisposition, resolvedFinalAnswer } from './plan.mjs';
import { resolveRequirementTargets } from './requirement_resolution.mjs';
import { planBoundRequestSteps } from './request_sequence.mjs';
import { planDeclaredMemberChange, planSeedLiteralChange } from './structured_edit.mjs';
import { bareSurfaces, safeRelativePath } from './write_request.mjs';
const MAX_REQUIREMENTS = 64;
const MAX_PARAGRAPH_LENGTH = 8192;
const SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING = 'coding-source-authoring-contract-missing';
// Use only the opening instruction paragraph. A numbered list in a quoted
// payload, a declaration example or a later evidence field grants no edits.
function numberedClauses(task) {
  const head = task.trimStart().split(/\\r?\\n[^\\S\\r\\n]*\\r?\\n/u, 1)[0];
  if (head.length > MAX_PARAGRAPH_LENGTH) return null;
  const quotes = quotedSegmentSpans(head);
  const markers = [...head.matchAll(/(^|\\s)\\(([1-9][0-9]?)\\)(?=\\s)/gu)]
    .filter(match => !quotes.some(quote => match.index + match[1].length >= quote.start
      && match.index + match[1].length < quote.end));
  if (markers.length < 2 || markers.length > MAX_REQUIREMENTS) return null;
  const lead = head.slice(0, markers[0].index).trim();
  if (lead !== '' && !lead.endsWith(':')) return null;
  return markers.map((marker, index) => ({
    number: Number(marker[2]),
    text: head.slice(marker.index + marker[0].length, markers[index + 1]?.index).trim(),
  }));
}
function sourceClause(clause) {
  const words = clause.replace(/\\.$/u, '').split(/\\s+/u);
  const [action, value, relation] = words.map(word => word.toLowerCase());
  if (bareSurfaces('coding_member_add_action').includes(action)
    && bareSurfaces('file_write_action_cue').includes(action)
    && /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,96}$/u.test(value)
    && [...bareSurfaces('file_edit_new_lead_cue'), ...bareSurfaces('file_write_target_cue')].includes(relation)) {
    return { descriptor: words.slice(3).join(' '), member: words[1] };
  }
  if (!bareSurfaces('file_edit_action_cue').includes(action)) return null;
  const oldLeads = bareSurfaces('file_edit_old_lead_cue');
  const newLeads = bareSurfaces('file_edit_new_lead_cue');
  const from = words.findIndex((word, index) => index >= 2 && oldLeads.includes(word.toLowerCase()));
  const to = words.findLastIndex(word => newLeads.includes(word.toLowerCase()));
  if (from < 0 || to <= from + 1) return null;
  const old = words.slice(from + 1, to).join(' ');
  const next = words.slice(to + 1).join(' ');
  if (old === next || ![old, next].every(text => /^[A-Za-z0-9_ -]{1,96}$/u.test(text))) return null;
  return { descriptor: words.slice(1, from).join(' '), old, next };
}
function gap(task) {
  const answer = renderSeededChange(SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING, task, '');
  return answer === null ? null : resolvedFinalAnswer(answer, FinalDisposition.Gap, SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING);
}
function bindClauses(inputs, targets) {
  const owners = inputs.some(input => input.member === undefined) && hasHost()
    ? host().generatedSeedOwnerDeclarations?.() ?? [] : [];
  return inputs.map((input, index) => {
    const target = targets[index];
    if (target === null || !['const', 'static'].includes(target.kind)) return null;
    if (input.member !== undefined) {
      const path = 'rust/' + target.module_path;
      return path.startsWith('rust/src/') && path.endsWith('.rs') && safeRelativePath(path)
        ? { ...input, path, declaration: target.symbol } : null;
    }
    const seed = owners.filter(owner => owner.module_path === target.module_path && owner.symbol === target.symbol
      && owner.kind === target.kind && input.descriptor.split(/[^A-Za-z0-9_]+/u).includes(owner.symbol));
    return seed.length === 1 ? { ...input, path: seed[0].seed_path } : null;
  });
}
export async function planNumberedSourceRequirements(task, messages, toolNames) {
  const clauses = numberedClauses(task);
  if (clauses === null) return null;
  const inputs = clauses.map(clause => sourceClause(clause.text));
  if (inputs.every(input => input === null)) return null;
  if (inputs.some(input => input === null) || clauses.some((clause, index) => clause.number !== index + 1)) return gap(task);
  const targets = resolveRequirementTargets(inputs.map(input => input.descriptor));
  const bound = bindClauses(inputs, targets);
  if (bound.some(input => input === null)) return gap(task);
  const texts = clauses.map(clause => clause.text);
  if (new Set(texts).size !== texts.length) return gap(task);
  return await planBoundRequestSteps(texts, messages, toolNames, (own, tools) => {
    const part = latestUserRequest(own);
    const input = bound[texts.indexOf(part)];
    return (input.member !== undefined
      ? planDeclaredMemberChange(part, own, tools, input.path, input.declaration, input.member)
      : planSeedLiteralChange(part, own, tools, input.path, input.old, input.next)) ?? gap(part);
  });
}

function observeCensusDocuments(repository) {
  let complete = true;
  const incomplete = () => {
    complete = false;
    return [];
  };
  const visit = relative => {
    if (!censusRegularPath(repository, relative, 'directory')) return incomplete();
    let entries;
    try {
      entries = readdirSync(path.join(repository, relative), {
        withFileTypes: true
      });
    } catch {
      return incomplete();
    }
    return entries.sort((left, right) => Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(left.name), Buffer.from(right.name))).flatMap(entry => {
      const file = relative + '/' + entry.name;
      if (entry.isSymbolicLink()) return incomplete();
      if (entry.isDirectory()) return visit(file);
      if (!entry.name.endsWith('.rs')) return [];
      if (!censusRegularPath(repository, file, 'file')) return incomplete();
      let source, symbols;
      try {
        const status = lstatSync(path.join(repository, file));
        if (status.size > 4 * 1024 * 1024) return incomplete();
        source = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {
          fatal: true,
          ignoreBOM: true
        }).decode(readFileSync(path.join(repository, file)));
        symbols = scanSignatureSymbols(source).map(symbol => ({
          kind: symbol.kind,
          name: symbol.name,
          start_line: symbol.startLine,
          end_line: symbol.endLine
        }));
      } catch {
        return incomplete();
      }

function observeCensusDocuments(repository) {
  let complete = true;
  const incomplete = () => {
    complete = false;
    return [];
  };
  const visit = relative => {
    if (!censusRegularPath(repository, relative, 'directory')) return incomplete();
    let entries;
    try {
      entries = readdirSync(path.join(repository, relative), {
        withFileTypes: true
      });
    } catch {
      return incomplete();
    }
    return entries.sort((left, right) => Buffer.compare(Buffer.from(left.name), Buffer.from(right.name))).flatMap(entry => {
      const file = relative + '/' + entry.name;
      if (entry.isSymbolicLink()) return incomplete();
      if (entry.isDirectory()) return visit(file);
      if (!entry.name.endsWith('.rs')) return [];
      if (!censusRegularPath(repository, file, 'file')) return incomplete();
      let source, symbols;
      try {
        const status = lstatSync(path.join(repository, file));
        if (status.size > 4 * 1024 * 1024) return incomplete();
        source = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {
          fatal: true,
          ignoreBOM: true
        }).decode(readFileSync(path.join(repository, file)));
        symbols = scanSignatureSymbols(source).map(symbol => ({
          kind: symbol.kind,
          name: symbol.name,
          start_line: symbol.startLine,
          end_line: symbol.endLine
        }));
      } catch {
        return incomplete();
      }
      const target = file.slice('rust/'.length);
      return [{
        path: file,
        text: null,
        module: {
          path: target,
          fidelity: 'navigation',
          symbols
        },
        sourceIdentity: {
          path: target,
          content_id: stableId('source_module', source),
          byte_len: Buffer.byteLength(source)
        }
      }];
    });
  };
  const documents = visit('rust/src');
  return {
    documents,
    complete
  };
}

/// Plan the next agentic step from the conversation and advertised tools.
/// Returns [`None`] when neither a stored recipe nor a safe general plan applies.
#[must_use]
pub fn plan_chat_step(messages: &[ChatMessage], tool_names: &[&str]) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
    plan_chat_step_resolved(messages, tool_names).map(|resolved| resolved.plan)
}
pub(super) fn plan_chat_step_resolved(
    messages: &[ChatMessage],
    tool_names: &[&str],
) -> Option<ResolvedPlan> {
    let mut result = None;
    let plan = plan_chat_step_inner(messages, tool_names, &mut result);
    let plan = super::repetition_guard::guard_plan(messages, plan, &mut result)?;
    let plan = super::prerequisite_recovery::with_recovery_report(messages, plan, &mut result);
    Some(ResolvedPlan::new(plan, result))
}

fn plan_verified_source_change(
    task: &str,
    messages: &[ChatMessage],
    tool_names: &[&str],
    target: &str,
    result: &mut Option<FinalResult>,
    compute: impl FnOnce(&str) -> Option<SourceChange>,
) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {

    let preimage = if attempted_write {
        progress.source_read_before_latest_mutation_for(target, Capability::Write)
    } else {
        progress.fresh_source_read_for(target)
    };

            FinalDisposition::Finding,

        result,

fn declared_string_array<'a>(source: &str, regions: &'a [Region], name: &str) -> Option<&'a Region> {

//! Numbered source requirements used as the work for a verified delivery.
use std::sync::LazyLock;
use regex::Regex;
use super::code_task::render_seeded_change;
use super::final_result::{FinalDisposition, FinalResult, ResolvedPlan, record};
use super::planner::AgenticPlan;
use super::request_sequence::plan_bound_request_steps;
use super::requirement_resolution::resolve_requirement_target;
use super::structured_edit::{plan_declared_member_change, plan_seed_literal_change};
use super::write_request::{bare_surfaces, safe_relative_path};
use crate::normal_markov::quoted_segment_spans;
use crate::protocol::{ChatMessage, latest_user_request};
use crate::seed;
const MAX_REQUIREMENTS: usize = 64;
const MAX_PARAGRAPH_LENGTH: usize = 8192;
const SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING: &str = "coding-source-authoring-contract-missing";
static PARAGRAPH_END: LazyLock<Regex> =
    LazyLock::new(|| Regex::new(r"\\r?\\n[^\\S\\r\\n]*\\r?\\n").expect("valid paragraph pattern"));
static CLAUSE_MARKER: LazyLock<Regex> = LazyLock::new(|| {
    Regex::new(r"(?:^|\\s)\\(([1-9][0-9]?)\\)").expect("valid requirement marker pattern")
});
/// Read only the opening instruction paragraph, outside quoted payloads.
fn numbered_clauses(task: &str) -> Option<Vec<(usize, &str)>> {
    let task = task.trim_start();
    let head = PARAGRAPH_END.splitn(task, 2).next()?;
    if head.len() > MAX_PARAGRAPH_LENGTH {
        return None;
    }
    let quotes = quoted_segment_spans(head);
    let markers: Vec<_> = CLAUSE_MARKER
        .captures_iter(head)
        .filter_map(|captures| {
            let whole = captures.get(0)?;
            let number = captures.get(1)?;
            let opener = number.start() - 1;
            (head[whole.end()..].starts_with(char::is_whitespace)
                && !quotes.iter().any(|quote| (quote.start..quote.end).contains(&opener)))
                .then_some((whole.start(), whole.end(), number.as_str()))
        })
        .collect();
    let [(start, _, _), ..] = markers.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    let lead = head[..*start].trim();
    if !(2..=MAX_REQUIREMENTS).contains(&markers.len()) || (!lead.is_empty() && !lead.ends_with(':')) {
        return None;
    }
    markers.iter().enumerate().map(|(index, (_, end, number))| {
        let next = markers.get(index + 1).map_or(head.len(), |marker| marker.0);
        Some((number.parse().ok()?, head[*end..next].trim()))
    }).collect()
}
enum Change {
    Member(String),
    SeedLiteral { old: String, next: String },
}
fn literal(text: &str, spaces: bool) -> bool {
    (1..=96).contains(&text.len())
        && text.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"_-".contains(&byte)
            || (spaces && byte == b' '))
}
fn source_clause(clause: &str) -> Option<(String, Change)> {
    let words: Vec<_> = clause.strip_suffix('.').unwrap_or(clause).split_whitespace().collect();
    let [verb, value, relation, rest @ ..] = words.as_slice() else {
        return None;
    };
    let action = verb.to_lowercase();
    let relation = relation.to_lowercase();
    let new_leads = bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_NEW_LEAD_CUE);
    if bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_CODING_MEMBER_ADD_ACTION).contains(&action)
        && bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_ACTION_CUE).contains(&action)
        && literal(value, false)
        && (new_leads.contains(&relation) || bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_WRITE_TARGET_CUE).contains(&relation))
    {
        return Some((rest.join(" "), Change::Member((*value).to_owned())));
    }
    if !bare_surfaces(seed::ROLE_FILE_EDIT_ACTION_CUE).contains(&action) {
        return None;
    }
    let old_leads = bare_surfaces("file_edit_old_lead_cue");
    let from = words.iter().enumerate().skip(2).find(|(_, word)| old_leads.contains(&word.to_lowercase()))?.0;
    let to = words.iter().rposition(|word| new_leads.contains(&word.to_lowercase()))?;
    if to <= from + 1 {
        return None;
    }
    let old = words[from + 1..to].join(" ");
    let next = words[to + 1..].join(" ");
    if old == next || !literal(&old, true) || !literal(&next, true) {
        return None;
    }
    Some((words[1..from].join(" "), Change::SeedLiteral { old, next }))
}
fn bind_source_clause(descriptor: &str, change: &Change) -> Option<(String, String)> {
    let target = resolve_requirement_target(descriptor)?;
    if !matches!(target.kind.as_str(), "const" | "static") {
        return None;
    }
    let path = match change {
        Change::Member(_) => {
            let path = format!("rust/{}", target.module_path);
            (path.starts_with("rust/src/") && path.ends_with(".rs") && safe_relative_path(&path))
                .then_some(path)?
        }
        Change::SeedLiteral { .. } => {
            if target.module_path != "src/seed/embedded_registry.rs"
                || !descriptor.split(|character: char| !character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && character != '_')
                    .any(|token| token =[REDACTED] target.symbol)
            {
                return None;
            }
            let seeds = seed::seed_files();
            let mut matching = seeds.into_iter().filter_map(|(path, _)| {
                let stem = path.rsplit('/').next()?.strip_suffix(".lino")?;
                (format!("{}_LINO", stem.to_ascii_uppercase().replace('-', "_")) == target.symbol)
                    .then_some(path)
            });
            let path = matching.next()?;
            if matching.next().is_some() {
                return None;
            }
            path.to_owned()
        }
    };
    Some((path, target.symbol))
}
fn gap(task: &str, result: &mut Option<FinalResult>) -> Option<AgenticPlan> {
    Some(record(
        AgenticPlan::Final(render_seeded_change(SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING, task, "", &[])?),
        FinalDisposition::Gap,
        SOURCE_CONTRACT_MISSING,
        result,
    ))
}
pub(super) fn plan_numbered_source_requirements(
    task: &str,
    messages: &[ChatMessage],
    tool_names: &[&str],
) -> Option<ResolvedPlan> {
    let clauses = numbered_clauses(task)?;
    let inputs: Vec<_> = clauses.iter().map(|(_, clause)| source_clause(clause)).collect();
    if inputs.iter().all(Option::is_none) {
        return None;
    }
    let mut result = None;
    let mut texts = Vec::with_capacity(clauses.len());
    let mut bound = Vec::with_capacity(texts.capacity());
    for ((number, text), input) in clauses.into_iter().zip(inputs) {
        let target = input.and_then(|(descriptor, change)| {
            Some((bind_source_clause(&descriptor, &change)?, change))
        });

            return Some(ResolvedPlan::new(plan, result));
        };
        texts.push(text.to_owned());
        bound.push(target);
    }
    let plan = plan_bound_request_steps(&texts, messages, tool_names, |own, tools| {
        let part = latest_user_request(own)?;
        let index = texts.iter().position(|text| *text == part)?;
        let ((path, declaration), change) = &bound[index];
        let mut outcome = None;
        let plan = match change {
            Change::Member(value) => plan_declared_member_change(&part, own, tools, path, declaration, value, &mut outcome),
            Change::SeedLiteral { old, next } => plan_seed_literal_change(&part, own, tools, path, old, next, &mut outcome),
        }.or_else(|| gap(&part, &mut outcome))?;
        Some(ResolvedPlan::new(plan, outcome))
    }, &mut result)?;
    Some(ResolvedPlan::new(plan, result))
}

/// The parsed meaning lexicon. Cached — the embedded data is immutable at
/// runtime, so parsing happens at most once per process.
#[must_use]
pub fn lexicon() -> &'static Lexicon {
    static CACHE: OnceLock<Lexicon> = OnceLock::new();
    CACHE.get_or_init(|| parse_lexicon(&MEANING_FILES.join("\n")))
}

/// loader, and confirms the surfaces denote their meaning and carry their
/// facets before the batch is written to the seed.
#[must_use]
pub fn parse_lexicon_text(text: &str) -> Lexicon {
    parse_lexicon(text)
}

function within(dir, path) {
  const full = isAbsolute(path) ? path : join(dir, path);
  const resolved = resolve(full);
  if (resolved !== resolve(dir) && !resolved.startsWith(resolve(dir) + sep)) throw new Error(`path escapes the sandbox: ${path}`);
  // Run from the repository root, a plan event goes to a git-ignored sandbox,
  // never over the committed `.formal-ai/` plan log (PR #1188 G15).
  if (resolve(dir) === REPOSITORY_ROOT && (resolved === PLAN_EVENTS || resolved.startsWith(`${PLAN_EVENTS}${sep}`))) {
    return join(PLAN_EVENTS_SANDBOX, relative(PLAN_EVENTS, resolved));
  }
  return resolved;
}
/**
 * The Agent CLI's `grep` (ripgrep underneath): "Found N matches" then each
 * file's absolute path and its `  Line N: text` hits, or "No files found".
 */
function grep(dir, args) {
  const argv = ['--json', '--sort', 'path', '--regexp', args.pattern ?? args.query ?? ''];
  if (args.include) argv.push('--glob', args.include);
  argv.push('--', within(dir, args.path ?? '.'));

/**
 * The Agent CLI's `grep` (ripgrep underneath): "Found N matches" then each
 * file's absolute path and its `  Line N: text` hits, or "No files found".
 */
function grep(dir, args) {
  const argv = ['--json', '--sort', 'path', '--regexp', args.pattern ?? args.query ?? ''];
  if (args.include) argv.push('--glob', args.include);
  argv.push('--', within(dir, args.path ?? '.'));
  return grepCapture(argv);
}

/** Mirrors `fn parse_lexicon_text`: parse an explicit source without changing the cached lexicon. */
export function parseLexiconText(source) {
  const root = parseLino(source);
  const containers = (root.children || []).filter((child) => child.name === 'meanings');
  const sources = containers.length ? containers : [root];
  const meanings = [];
  for (const container of sources) {
    for (const node of container.children || []) {
      if (node.name === 'meaning' || node.name !== 'meanings') meanings.push(parseMeaning(node));
    }
  }
  return meanings;
}
/** Mirrors `fn lexicon` / `fn parse_lexicon`: every meaning in declaration order. */
export function lexicon() {
  return cached('meaning-lexicon', () => parseLexiconText(meaningFiles().map(readText).join('\n')));
}
/** Mirrors `crate::coding::contains_cjk`. @param {string} text */
export function containsCjk(text) {
  for (const character of text) {
    const cp = character.codePointAt(0);
    if ((cp >= 0x3400 && cp <= 0x4dbf) || (cp >= 0x4e00 && cp <= 0x9fff) || (cp >= 0xf900 && cp <= 0xfaff)
      || (cp >= 0x3040 && cp <= 0x30ff) || (cp >= 0x3100 && cp <= 0x312f)) return true;
  }
  return false;
}
/** Mirrors `fn surface_present` in rust/src/seed/meanings.rs. */
export function surfacePresent(normalized, expected) {
  if (!expected) return false;
  if (containsCjk(expected)) return normalized.includes(expected);

/// Render an answer under the constraints attached to its destination.
fn render_obligation(obligation: &DeliveryBinding, answer: &str) -> String {
    if !obligation.field_lines.is_empty() {
        let result = substantive_result_line(answer, &obligation.residual);
        let observed_results = exact_field_values(answer, "result");
        let mut next_observed = observed_results.iter();
        let mut rendered = String::new();
        for field in &obligation.field_lines {
            rendered.push_str(field);
            if field.ends_with('=') {
                if field == "result=" {
                    let combined = combined_observation(&observed_results, &obligation.residual)
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| result.to_owned());
                    rendered.push_str(&non_hollow_result(&combined, &obligation.residual));
                } else {
                    rendered.push_str(next_observed.next().map_or(result, String::as_str));
                }
            }
            rendered.push('\n');
        }
        return rendered;
    }
    let answer = non_hollow_result(answer, &obligation.residual);
    obligation.first_line.as_ref().map_or_else(
        || format!("{}\n", answer.trim_end()),
        |line| format!("{line}\n\n{}\n", answer.trim_end()),
    )
}

/// ignored; only a line whose prefix is exact participates.

    let prefix = format!("{key}=");
    answer

/// Render an answer under the constraints attached to its destination.
fn render_obligation(obligation: &DeliveryBinding, answer: &str) -> String {
    if !obligation.field_lines.is_empty() {
        let result = substantive_result_line(answer, &obligation.residual);
        let observed_results = exact_field_values(answer, "result");
        let mut next_observed = observed_results.iter();
        let mut rendered = String::new();
        for field in &obligation.field_lines {
            rendered.push_str(field);
            if field.ends_with('=') {
                if field == "result=" {
                    let combined = combined_observation(&observed_results, &obligation.residual)
                        .unwrap_or_else(|| result.to_owned());
                    rendered.push_str(&non_hollow_result(&combined, &obligation.residual));
                } else {
                    rendered.push_str(next_observed.next().map_or(result, String::as_str));
                }
            }
            rendered.push('\n');
        }
        return rendered;
    }
    let answer = non_hollow_result(answer, &obligation.residual);
    obligation.first_line.as_ref().map_or_else(
        || format!("{}\n", answer.trim_end()),
        |line| format!("{line}\n\n{}\n", answer.trim_end()),
    )
}

/**
 * Mirrors `fn compacted_agent_task`. Agent may compact an already compacted
 * conversation, and each compaction summarizes the previous summary turn, so
 * envelopes nest; every `Conversation summary:` envelope is read, the latest
 * first, until one names a standing task (PR #1188 dogfooding: the second
 * compaction listed "What did we do so far?" first and the task was lost).
 */
export function compactedAgentTask(earlier) {
  for (let index = earlier.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
    const message = earlier[index];
    if (!isRole(message, 'assistant')) continue;
    const envelopes = plainText(message.content).split('Conversation summary:').slice(1).reverse();
    for (const envelope of envelopes) {
      const summary = trimStart(envelope);
      let task = preservedFirstUserTurn(summary);
      if (task === null) {
        const titled = splitOnce(summary, '\n\nTitle:');
        task = titled ? standingSentences(trim(titled[0])) : null;
      }
      if (task !== null) return repairCompactedDotPaths(task);
    }
  }
  return null;
}

  isAlphanumeric, isWhitespace, rsplitOnce, splitOnce, stripPrefix, trim, trimEndMatches, trimMatches, trimStart,

const isRole = (message, role) => message.role.toLowerCase() === role;
/** Mirrors `fn is_continuation_cue`. */
export function isContinuationCue(text) {
  return handlerMatches('agentic_continuation', text);
}
/** Mirrors `fn evidence_window_start`. */
export function evidenceWindowStart(messages) {
  const users = messages.map(message => isRole(message, 'user'));
  // Native multipart input does not retain all image fields, so it never proves repeated-request identity.
  const cues = messages.map((message, index) => users[index] && typeof message.content === 'string'
    && isContinuationCue(message.content));
  const identities = messages.map((message, index) => !users[index] ? '' : typeof message.content === 'string'
    && message.content.length > 0 ? 'text:' + message.content : 'boundary:' + index);
  return continuationEvidenceWindowStart(users, cues, identities);
}

    if (isRole(messages[index], 'user')) {

  const head = task.trimStart().split(/\r?\n[^\S\r\n]*\r?\n/u, 1)[0];

//! Resolve a requirement that names behaviour or a declaration, not a file
//! (issue #1085 D2.2).
//!
//! The self-AST census is the links network over the workspace's own source.
//! A requirement such as "add wikiquote as a web search provider" is resolved
//! by querying it for the `const` or `static` whose identifier words the
//! requirement contains, or for the identifier the requirement names, so the
//! prompt never has to name `src/web_search_core.rs`.
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use crate::self_ast_census::{ModuleCensus, SymbolSpan, WorkspaceCensus, workspace};
/// Where a requirement lands: the module and the declaration it changes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RequirementTarget {
    pub module_path: String,
    pub symbol: String,
    pub kind: String,
}
/// Resolve `requirement` against the live workspace census.
#[must_use]
pub fn resolve_requirement_target(requirement: &str) -> Option<RequirementTarget> {
    resolve_in(workspace(), requirement)
}
/// Resolve `requirement` against `census`.
///
/// An identifier the requirement names verbatim wins; otherwise the `const` or
/// `static` whose identifier words (singularised) all occur in the requirement
/// wins, longest identifier first. A tie between modules is broken by the
/// module path words the requirement mentions; a remaining tie is ambiguity and
/// resolves to nothing rather than to a guess. When identifier words do not bind,
/// an actual canonical seed surface and its semantic role can bind its declared owner.
#[must_use]
pub fn resolve_in(census: &WorkspaceCensus, requirement: &str) -> Option<RequirementTarget> {
    let modules = explicit_module_scope(census, requirement)?;
    if modules.is_empty() {
        resolve_scoped(census, requirement)
    } else {
        let scoped = WorkspaceCensus { modules };

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Planner twin ratchet (R1188-U16).
//
// The agentic planner is JavaScript first: every function a module under
// js/agentic/ exports has a Rust twin in rust/src/, under the snake_case form
// of its name or under the name its doc comment cites as `Mirrors \`symbol\``
// (a `fn`, or the `const`, `static`, `struct` or `enum` it builds or returns),
// or stands for a Rust built-in or a dependency crate's item its doc comment
// names (`Rust built-in \`x\``, `Rust dependency \`crate::x\``).
// This script counts the exported functions with no such twin and holds the
// count to the ceiling in data/meta/planner-twin-ratchet.lino.
// Above the ceiling fails, so a planner function cannot land in JavaScript
// alone; below it fails too, naming the lower ceiling to commit, so the
// number only falls. Modules that exist only on the JavaScript side by design
// (the host port, the Rust `str` semantics shims) are listed in the ratchet
// file with their reason.
//
// Usage: node scripts/check-planner-twins.mjs [--list]

/// The members named the way the source spells them, for a sentence.
fn quoted_list(values: &[String]) -> String {
    values
        .iter()
        .map(|value| format!("\"{value}\""))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join(", ")
}
/// The list the request is about is the one that already holds the members the
/// request named. The smallest such region wins, so a `matches!(subject, Some(
/// "a" | "b"))` resolves to the alternation rather than to the macro call that
/// contains it.
/// A census-owned string array requires an actual, unique initializer in the observed bytes.
fn declared_string_array<'a>(
    source: &str,
    regions: &'a [Region],
    name: &str,
) -> Option<&'a Region> {
    if !valid_identifier(name) {
        return None;
    }
    let declaration = regex::Regex::new(&format!(
        r"(?:const|static)\s+{name}\s*:\s*&?\s*\[\s*&str\s*\]\s*=\s*&?\s*\["
    ))
    .ok()?;
    let mut anchors = declaration.find_iter(source).filter_map(|matched| {
        regions
            .iter()
            .find(|region| region.open == matched.end() - 1)
    });
    let anchor = anchors.next()?;
    anchors.next().is_none().then_some(anchor)
}

function rustFiles(directory, out) {
  let entries;
  try {
    entries = readDirEntries(directory);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new RustError(`${directory}: ${ioErrorMessage(error)}`);
  }
  for (const entry of entries) {
    if (isDir(entry.path)) rustFiles(entry.path, out);
    else if (extension(entry.path) === 'rs') out.push(entry.path);
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# External verifier for one Agent CLI ladder node (issues #1028, #1066, #1085).
#
# The verdict never trusts the agent's own words: a leaf must have changed the
# one tracked file its task names, the file must still format, compile and pass
# the unit tests of its module; a depth-4 composite must compose both verified
# child effects and both children's diffs must apply to one tree and compile;
# a node at depth 3 or above is requirement-shaped, so every leaf marker under
# it must be present, only those files modified, and the tree must compile and
# pass the tests of every touched module (issue #1085 D4).
#
# Environment (all optional):
#   LADDER_CARGO_CHECK=0       skip `cargo check --lib`

function storeReadShare(root) {
  const files = [];
  rustFiles(join(root, 'rust/src'), files);
  return files.reduce((total, file) => total + countMatches(readRustFile(root, file), 'from_store('), 0);

function countEntries(directory, label, keep) {
  let entries;
  try {
    entries = readDirEntries(directory);
  } catch (error) {
    throw new RustError(`${label}: ${ioErrorMessage(error)}`);
  }
  return entries.filter(keep).length;
}

# Only registered CST-derived tests can witness a changed source module.
module_filter() {
  node "$ROOT/scripts/lib/ladder-test-projection.mjs" "$workspace" "$1"
}
verify_source_tests() {
  local source="$1" filters filter target
  if [[ "${LADDER_CARGO_TEST:-1}" == 0 ]] || ! command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || [[ ! -f "$workspace/rust/Cargo.toml" ]]; then
    cargo_test source_projection_unavailable
    return $?
  fi
  if [[ "$source" =~ ^data/seed/[[:alnum:]][[:alnum:]_.-]*\.lino$ ]]; then
    LADDER_CHANGED_SEED="$source" cargo_test embedded_seed_matches_canonical_source data_files
    return $?
  fi
  filters=$(module_filter "$source") || { record "tests:$source" missing_source_projection; return 1; }
  [[ -n "$filters" ]] || { record "tests:$source" missing_source_projection; return 1; }
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r target filter; do
    cargo_test "$filter" "$target" || return 1
  done <<< "$filters"
}
cargo_check() {
  [[ "${LADDER_CARGO_CHECK:-1}" != 0 ]] || { record compile skipped; return 0; }
  command -v cargo >/dev/null 2>&1 || { record compile unavailable; return 0; }
  # A workspace that is not a Rust package has nothing to compile; the missing
  # package is not an uncompilable change (leaf criteria may name a README).
  [[ -f "$workspace/rust/Cargo.toml" ]] || { record compile unavailable; return 0; }
  local started=$SECONDS
  if (cd "$workspace/rust" && CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$(target_dir)" \
      cargo check --lib --quiet >"$verification_dir/cargo-check.log" 2>&1); then
    echo "verify $node: cargo check --lib took $((SECONDS - started))s" >&2
    record compile ok
    return 0
  fi
  tail -40 "$verification_dir/cargo-check.log" >&2 || true
  record compile failed
  return 1
}

Each push that only fixes part of the\nprevious run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188\nneeded 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.\nThe rules below make every push count:\n\n1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or\n   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.\n   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.\n2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to\n   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure\n   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same\n   batch.\n3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:\n\n   ```bash\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName\n   gh run list --branch \"$(git branch --show-current)\" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName\n   ```\n\n   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you\n   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run\n   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).\n4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check\n   apply:\n   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:\n     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;\n   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScript and never compile\n     Rust: `node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs --only <gate>`.\n\n   `--list` shows every gate. Run the whole set\n   (`node experiments/formal_ai_subagent/local-gates.mjs`) before a push that\n   touches shared data such as `data/meta`. The fast pull-request lane runs the\n   same twins, so a failure here would have failed there too.\n5. **No full local Rust build unless the change is Rust-only.** CI compiles\n   Rust: the focused `native-type-check` job on pull requests, and the full\n   matrix on main. Locally, run `rustfmt --check <file>` on the files you\n   changed. That command needs no build.\n6. **If a change is Rust-only and you must build locally, keep the build\n   bounded.** Use one shared target directory for every worktree and agent,\n   with no incremental cache, few jobs, and a prune afterwards:\n\n   ```bash\n   export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=\"$HOME/.cache/formal-ai-target\"  # one directory, shared by all worktrees\n   export CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0                               # no incremental cache to grow without bound\n   export CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2                                # a limited -j for plain cargo commands\n   CARGO_TEST_JOBS=2 scripts/cargo-test.sh --test unit <filter>  # one module, -j 2, then prunes\n   scripts/prune-build-cache.sh                             # prunes old artifacts after any other cargo command\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/prune-build-cache.sh` follows `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`. It keeps only\n   the latest build's artifacts, and by default it caps the tree at 4 GB\n   locally (`CARGO_TARGET_MAX_SIZE_MB`).\n\n## Where things live\n\n- Production-only failures are recorded in\n  [`data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino`](data/meta/main-only-regressions.lino).\n  These are failures that main recorded after a green pull request. /// Why a payload cannot be decoded in this environment, if anything.
#[must_use]
pub fn unavailable_reason(manifest: &SuiteManifest) -> Option<String> {
    if matches!(manifest.source, SuiteSource::ParquetRows { .. })
        && !python_module_available("pyarrow.parquet")
    {
        return Some(vocabulary::text(
            "external_benchmark_parquet_module_unavailable",
        ));
    }
    None
}
fn python_module_available(module: &str) -> bool {
    let import = vocabulary::render("external_benchmark_python_import", &[("module", module)]);
    crate::bounded_process::command_output(
        {
            let mut bounded_child_command = Command::new("python3");
            bounded_child_command.args(["-c", &import]);
            bounded_child_command
        },
        std::time::Duration::from_secs(30),
        64 * 1024 * 1024,
        16 * 1024 * 1024,
    )
    .map_err(|failure| std::io::Error::new(failure.kind(), failure))
    .is_ok_and(|output| output.status.success())
}
fn parquet_records(path: &Path, manifest: &SuiteManifest) -> Result<Vec<String>, String> {
    let script = concat!(
        "import json, sys\n",

# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai
This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the
hive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates
only the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI
time ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).
## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

//! Resolve a requirement that names behaviour or a declaration, not a file
//! (issue #1085 D2.2).
//!
//! The self-AST census is the links network over the workspace's own source.
//! A requirement such as "add wikiquote as a web search provider" is resolved
//! by querying it for the `const` or `static` whose identifier words the
//! requirement contains, or for the identifier the requirement names, so the
//! prompt never has to name `src/web_search_core.rs`.
use std::cmp::Ordering;
use crate::self_ast_census::{ModuleCensus, SymbolSpan, WorkspaceCensus, workspace};
/// Where a requirement lands: the module and the declaration it changes.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RequirementTarget {
    pub module_path: String,
    pub symbol: String,
    pub kind: String,
}
/// Resolve `requirement` against the live workspace census.
#[must_use]
pub fn resolve_requirement_target(requirement: &str) -> Option<RequirementTarget> {
    resolve_in(workspace(), requirement)
}
/// Resolve a group using the same workspace census.
pub(super) fn resolve_requirement_targets<'a>(
    requirements: impl IntoIterator<Item = Option<&'a str>>,
) -> Vec<Option<RequirementTarget>> {
    let census = workspace();
    requirements
        .into_iter()
        .map(|requirement| resolve_in(census, requirement?))
        .collect()
}

//! Test-only actual workspace adapter; process observations never come from canned text.
use formal_ai::agent::{AgentError, AgentWorkspace, AgentWorkspaceConfig};
use formal_ai::agentic_coding::PlannedToolCall;
use formal_ai::agentic_coding::planner::{Capability, tool_capability};
use formal_ai::protocol::ChatMessage;
use serde_json::{Value, json};
use std::process::{Command, Stdio};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
pub struct ToolWorkspace {
    workspace: AgentWorkspace,
    next_run: u64,
}
fn argument(args: &Value, names: &[&str]) -> Option<String> {
    names
        .iter()
        .find_map(|name| args[*name].as_str().map(str::to_owned))
}
impl ToolWorkspace {
    pub fn new(prompt: &str) -> Self {
        let config = AgentWorkspaceConfig {
            time_budget: Duration::from_secs(2),
            ..AgentWorkspaceConfig::default()
        };
        Self {
            workspace: AgentWorkspace::for_prompt(prompt, &config).expect("fixture workspace"),
            next_run: 0,
        }
    }
    pub fn write_initial(&self, path: &str, content: &str) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
        self.write(path, content)?;
        if self.read(path)? != content {
            return Err(std::io::Error::other("physical write bytes differ").into());
        }
        Ok(())
    }
    fn write(&self, path: &str, content: &str) -> Result<(), AgentError> {
        let target = std::path::Path::new(path);
        if target.as_os_str().is_empty()
            || target.is_absolute()
            || !target
                .components()
                .all(|part| matches!(part, std::path::Component::Normal(_)))
        {
            return Err(AgentError::PathEscapesWorkspace(path.to_owned()));
        }
        let target = self.workspace.root().join(target);
        std::fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().expect("workspace file parent"))?;
        std::fs::write(target, content)?;
        Ok(())
    }

    /// A content-addressed id over the whole census — one value that changes when
    /// any module's content id or fidelity changes.
    #[must_use]
    pub fn content_id(&self) -> String {
        let mut joined = String::new();
        for module in &self.modules {
            let _ = writeln!(
                joined,
                "{} {} {}",
                module.path,
                module.fidelity.slug(),
                module.content_id

    #[must_use]
    pub fn index_notation(&self) -> String {
        let mut out =

        for module in &self.modules {
            let _ = writeln!(out, "    {} {}", module.path, module.document_path());

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check-secrets.sh
#
# Scans the files a change touches for committed credentials, using secretlint
# with the recommended preset (CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md section 11 / issue #808).
#
# Usage:
#   BASE_REF=main bash scripts/check-secrets.sh     # scan the diff vs BASE_REF
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh --all             # scan every tracked file
#   bash scripts/check-secrets.sh path/to/file ...  # scan specific files
#
# Exit code 0 = no secrets found; non-zero = a finding or scanner failure.
#
# Why the diff and not the whole tree
# -----------------------------------
# The js template runs `secretlint "**/*"`. Measured on this repository that
# does not finish in a usable time: the glob walks the working tree (including
# `target/` and ~150 MB of committed case-study logs) and the scan was still
# running after 25 minutes locally. A gate that cannot be relied on to finish is
# a new CI failure mode, which is the opposite of what issue #808 asks for.
#
# Scanning what the change touches keeps the gate fast and catches the case that
# matters: a credential being *introduced*. Pre-existing files are not re-scanned
# on every pull request; run `--all` (no timeout) to audit the whole tree.
#
# FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG=[REDACTED] prints the resolved file list before scanning.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
debug() {
  if [ "${FORMAL_AI_SECRETS_DEBUG:[REDACTED]}" = "1" ]; then
    printf '[check-secrets] %s\n' "$1" >&2
  fi
}
# Captured third-party CI/agent logs kept verbatim as evidence. They are
# reviewed when added and consist of redacted GitHub Actions output.
exclude() {
  local status=0
  grep -zv -e '^docs/case-studies/.*\.log$' -e '^dev/log/.*ci-logs/.*\.log$' || status=$?
  # grep's no-match status means a valid empty selection; actual errors fail.
  [ "$status" -le 1 ]
}

fn singular(word: &str) -> String {
    if word.len() > 3 && word.ends_with('s') && !word.ends_with("ss") {
        word[..word.len() - 1].to_owned()
    } else {
        word.to_owned()
    }
}

fn unique(
    candidates: &[(&ModuleCensus, &SymbolSpan)],
    tokens: &[String],
) -> Option<RequirementTarget> {
    if let [(module, symbol)] = candidates {
        return Some(target(module, symbol));
    }
    let words: Vec<String> = tokens
        .iter()
        .map(|token| singular(&token.to_lowercase()))
        .collect();
    let scored: Vec<(usize, &ModuleCensus, &SymbolSpan)> = candidates
        .iter()
        .map(|(module, symbol)| {
            let score = path_words(&module.path)
                .iter()
                .filter(|word| words.contains(word))
                .count();
            (score, *module, *symbol)
        })
        .collect();
    let top = scored.iter().map(|(score, _, _)| *score).max()?;
    let mut winners = scored
        .iter()
        .filter(|(score, _, _)| *score == top)
        .map(|(_, module, symbol)| (*module, *symbol));
    let (module, symbol) = winners.next()?;
    if winners.next().is_some() {
        return None;
    }
    Some(target(module, symbol))
}
fn target(module: &ModuleCensus, symbol: &SymbolSpan) -> RequirementTarget {
    RequirementTarget {
        module_path: module.path.clone(),
        symbol: symbol.name.clone(),
        kind: symbol.kind.clone(),
    }
}
fn path_words(path: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    path.split(['/', '_', '.'])
        .filter(|part| !part.is_empty() && *part != "src" && *part != "rs" && *part != "mod")
        .map(|part| singular(&part.to_lowercase()))
        .collect()
}
fn tokens_of(text: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    text.split(|character: char| !character.is_alphanumeric() && character != '_')
        .filter(|token| !token.is_empty())
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .collect()
}

/// Emit `owned_source_files.rs` — the compile-time manifest of every owned Rust
/// source file under `src/`, embedded via `include_str!`.
///
/// Issue #558 asks for *"the entire source code of our system"* to be translatable
/// to the links/meta language and *"present in the seed data"*. `include_str!`
/// cannot iterate a directory, so this script writes a generated slice of
/// `(repo_relative_path, source_text)` pairs into `OUT_DIR`; the whole-repository
/// projection ([`crate::self_source_links`]) includes it via
/// `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/owned_source_files.rs"))` so every module's
/// source ships in the binary and the projection works with no filesystem access —
/// exactly as it must when the loop runs from an agent CLI's sandbox workdir.

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Read one producer-bound native test executable without downloading its sibling binaries."""
+
+import argparse
+import hashlib
+import io
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import subprocess
+import urllib.error
+import urllib.parse
+import urllib.request
+import zipfile
+
+
+class KeepRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
+    def redirect_request(self, request, response, code, message, headers, location):
+        return None
+
+
+class ArtifactRanges(io.RawIOBase):
+    """A seekable view over a GitHub Actions artifact via bounded HTTP ranges."""
+
+    def __init__(self, location, size):
+        self.location = location
+        self.size = size
+        self.offset = 0
+        self.bytes_received = 0
+
+    def tell(self):
+        return self.offset
+
+    def seek(self, offset, whence=io.SEEK_SET):
+        origin = {io.SEEK_SET: 0, io.SEEK_CUR: self.offset, io.SEEK_END: self.size}[whence]
+        self.offset = origin + offset
+        if self.offset < 0:
+            raise ValueError("negative artifact offset")
+        return self.offset
+
+    def read(self, size=-1):
+        count = self.size - self.offset if size < 0 else min(size, self.size - self.offset)
+        if count <= 0:
+            return b""
+        if count > 8 * 1024 * 1024:
+            raise ValueError("artifact read exceeds the 8 MiB range limit")
+        last = self.offset + count - 1
+        request = urllib.request.Request(self.location, headers={"Range": f"bytes={self.offset}-{last}"})
+        with urllib.request.urlopen(request) as response:
+            if response.status != 206 or response.headers.get("Content-Range") != f"bytes {self.offset}-{last}/{self.size}":
+                raise ValueError("artifact server did not confirm the requested byte range")
+            data = response.read(count + 1)
+        if len(data) != count:
+            raise ValueError("artifact range length differs from the requested length")
+        self.offset += count
+        self.bytes_received += count
+        return data
+
+    def seekable(self):
+        return True
+
+
+def signed_location(artifact_id):
+    credential = subprocess.check_output(["gh", "auth", "token"], text=True).strip()
+    url = f"https://api.github.com/repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/actions/artifacts/{artifact_id}/zip"
+    request = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": [REDACTED]"Bearer {credential}"})
+    try:
+        urllib.request.build_opener(KeepRedirect()).open(request).close()
+    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
+        location = error.headers.get("Location", "")
+        if error.code == 302 and urllib.parse.urlsplit(location).scheme == "https":
+            return location
+        if error.code != 302:
+            raise RuntimeError(f"GitHub artifact request failed with HTTP {error.code}") from None
+    raise RuntimeError("GitHub did not supply a signed HTTPS artifact location")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("metadata", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("compiled_commit")
+    parser.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
+    parser.add_argument("--inspect", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    metadata = json.loads(args.metadata.read_text())
+    artifact_id = metadata["id"]
+    ranges = ArtifactRanges(signed_location(artifact_id), metadata["size_in_bytes"])
+    with zipfile.ZipFile(ranges) as archive:
+        receipt = json.loads(archive.read("native-contract-receipt.json"))
+        identity = receipt["identity"]
+        if (receipt["schema"] != "native-contract-artifact/v1"
+            or identity["commit"] != args.compiled_commit
+            or str(identity["run"]) != str(metadata["workflow_run"]["id"])):
+            raise ValueError("native contract receipt does not identify the requested producer")
+        name = "coding_contracts"
+        member = archive.getinfo(name)
+        expected = receipt["files"][name]
+        if member.file_size != expected["bytes"] or member.file_size > 768 * 1024 * 1024:
+            raise ValueError("native contract member differs from the bounded producer receipt")
+        print(f"{name}: {member.file_size} executable bytes, {member.compress_size} transport bytes", flush=True)
+        if args.inspect:
+            return
+        digest = hashlib.sha256()
+        with archive.open(member) as source, args.destination.open("xb") as destination:
+            for block in iter(lambda: source.read(4 * 1024 * 1024), b""):
+                destination.write(block)
+                digest.update(block)
+        if digest.hexdigest() != expected["sha256"]:
+            raise ValueError("native contract bytes differ from the producer receipt")
+        args.destination.chmod(0o700)
+        print(f"verified {digest.hexdigest()} across {ranges.bytes_received} artifact bytes")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

//! Sentence scoping and command-policy classification for shell routing.
//!
//! A prompt that *mentions* a command is not a prompt that *asks for* one.
//! Hive Mind wraps every Codex request in caller policy — *"When running sudo
//! commands, run them in the background."* — and matching a run verb against a
//! command token message-wide planned a bare `sudo` for every such run
//! (issue #907). So routing reads one sentence at a time, and a sentence that
//! only governs commands never licenses the token it names.
//!
//! This is the classification half of [`super::shell_command`]; the routing
//! half calls [`sentence_spans`], [`states_a_command_policy`] and
//! [`named_shell_command_in_sentence`].

/// One sentence of a prompt: its trimmed text, and the byte range it occupies.
///
/// The ranges tile the prompt, so dropping a sentence and concatenating the rest
/// reproduces the original wording verbatim — which is what a route needs when
/// it consumes one clause of a request and hands the remainder on (issue #1066).
pub(super) struct Sentence<'a> {
    /// The sentence with its surrounding whitespace and terminator removed.
    pub(super) text: &'a str,
    /// Where the sentence sits in the prompt, terminator included.
    pub(super) span: std::ops::Range<usize>,
}

/// Resolve a workspace question into a subject and a fact-focused search.
///
/// A module name tells the agent *where* an answer is likely to live, but it is
/// rarely the answer. Searching only for `task_decomposition` can fill Agent's
/// result cap with release notes before reaching the `children` field the
/// caller asked about. The request's remaining content words therefore form
/// the grep expression, while a lowercase underscored subject narrows the file
/// set. Both are recovered structurally; no ladder wording is registered here.
pub(super) fn workspace_inspection_search_for_task(
    prompt: &str,
) -> Option<WorkspaceInspectionSearch> {
    for block in super::stated_request::request_blocks(prompt) {
        if !asks_about_the_workspace(block) {
            continue;
        }
        if let Some(query) = code_search_query_for_task(block) {
            return Some(WorkspaceInspectionSearch {
                pattern: query.clone(),
                query,
                include: None,
            });

        // checkout question and a machine-shaped worker contract. Prefer the
        // subject carried by the sentence that asks to inspect the workspace;
        // otherwise a later token such as `new_audit_effect` can outrank the
        // helper the caller asked about. Keep the historical whole-block
        // fallback for requests whose inspection cue and subject span two
        // sentences.
        if let Some(search) = sentence_spans(block)
            .into_iter()
            .filter(|sentence| asks_about_the_workspace(sentence))
            .find_map(workspace_inspection_search)
        {
            return Some(search);

/// Explicit terminal diagnostics; normal wrapper/server output stays clear.
pub fn configure_terminal(verbose: bool) {
    TERMINAL.store(verbose, Ordering::Relaxed);
}
fn rank(level: &str) -> u8 {
    match level {
        "error" => 1,
        "warn" => 2,
        "info" => 3,
        "trace" => 5,
        "silent" | "off" => 0,
        _ => 4,
    }
}
#[must_use]
pub fn enabled(level: &str) -> bool {
    !SILENT.load(Ordering::Relaxed)
        && !crate::solver_config::ephemeral_enabled()
        && !crate::solver_config::flag_enabled("FORMAL_AI_SILENT")
        && rank(level)
            <= rank(&std::env::var("FORMAL_AI_LOG_LEVEL").unwrap_or_else(|_| "debug".into()))
}
/// Passive native request timing; WASM has no standard-library monotonic clock.
pub(crate) fn request_phases(trace: bool) -> impl Fn(&str) {
    let started = (trace && !cfg!(target_arch = "wasm32")).then(std::time::Instant::now);
    move |name| {
        if let Some(started) = started {
            crate::diagnostic!("debug"; "[trace] agentic_phase={name} elapsed_ms={}", started.elapsed().as_millis());
        }
    }
}

/// The marks a step loses at its end.
const STEP_TAIL: &[char] = &[',', ';', '，', '；', '.', '。'];
/// The conversation with its latest user turn asking `part` alone.
fn with_request(messages: &[ChatMessage], part: &str) -> Vec<ChatMessage> {
    let latest = messages
        .iter()
        .rposition(|message| message.role.eq_ignore_ascii_case("user"));
    messages
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(index, message)| {
            let mut message = message.clone();
            if Some(index) == latest {
                message.content = MessageContent::Text(part.to_owned());
            }
            message
        })
        .collect()
}

/// A census-owned string array requires an actual, unique initializer in the observed bytes.
fn declared_string_array(source: &str, regions: &[Region], name: &str) -> Option<Region> {
    if !valid_identifier(name) {
        return None;
    }
    let declaration = regex::Regex::new(&format!(
        r"(?:const|static)\s+{name}\s*:\s*&?\s*\[\s*&str\s*\]\s*=\s*&?\s*\["
    ))
    .ok()?;
    let mut anchors = declaration.find_iter(source).filter_map(|matched| {
        regions
            .iter()
            .find(|region| region.open == matched.end() - 1)
    });
    let anchor = anchors.next()?;
    anchors.next().is_none().then_some(*anchor)
}
/// The smallest region holding the members wins. In `matches!(subject,
/// Some("a" | "b"))`, this selects the alternation inside the macro call.
fn anchor_by_members(
    regions: &[Region],
    literals: &[Literal],
    values: &[String],
) -> Option<Region> {
    let mut best: Option<(usize, usize, Region)> = None;
    for region in regions {
        let members = direct_members(literals, region.open);
        let held = values
            .iter()
            .filter(|value| members.iter().any(|member| &member.value == *value))
            .count();
        if held == 0 {
            continue;
        }
        best = better(best, held, *region);
    }
    best.map(|(_, _, region)| region)
}

//! Grounded structural edits over client-supplied workspace bytes.
//!
//! Unlike literal replacement, member insertion has no complete old value in the
//! request. The planner must read the target, derive the replacement from those
//! bytes, write the full updated source, and observe the result.
//!
//! Everything about *where* the insertion goes is discovered from the target's
//! own bytes rather than from the request's wording: which member list is meant,
//! which delimiters enclose it, which separator joins its members, and which of
//! the request's values are already there. The request only has to name a file,
//! say that a member list is involved, and quote the members. That is why one
//! recipe covers a bracketed array, a `matches!` alternation and a parenthesised
//! group without a branch per shape (#1069).

# Instructions for AI agents working on formal-ai
This file is for any automated contributor, such as Claude Code, Codex, the
hive-mind `solve` command or Formal AI itself. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) still applies in full. This file restates
only the rules an agent breaks most often, because each one has cost real CI
time ([issue #1191](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1191)).
## The single push gate
A push starts several workflows at once. Each push that only fixes part of the
previous run's failures pays for the whole matrix again. Pull request #1188
needed 100 commits and 11 `CI/CD Pipeline` runs, and none of them was green.
The rules below make every push count:
1. **Drafting sub-agents never push.** A sub-agent that drafts code, tests or
   documentation commits locally (or hands its diff back) and stops there.
   Only the coordinating agent touches the remote.
2. **One CI/CD agent pushes, once per round.** Exactly one agent owns pushes to
   the branch. It pushes only after it has collected every actionable failure
   of the latest run on the current head, and fixed all of them in the same
   batch.
3. **Never push while a run is in progress on the branch.** Check first:
   ```bash
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status in_progress --json databaseId,workflowName
   gh run list --branch "$(git branch --show-current)" --status queued --json databaseId,workflowName
   ```
   Both lists must be empty, or must hold only runs for an older head that you
   are deliberately superseding. Otherwise, keep drafting while the run
   finishes, then collect its failures (rule 2).
4. **Run the JavaScript checks locally before the push.** Two kinds of check
   apply:
   - the test files next to the change, run one at a time:
     `timeout 600 node --test --test-concurrency=1 <file>`;
   - the gates the change touches. These run in JavaScrip

impl Progress {
    pub(in crate::agentic_coding) fn fresh_source_read_for(
        &self,
        path: &str,
    ) -> Option<&crate::agentic_coding::tool_result::SourceReadObservation> {
        let attempt = fresh_source_read_attempt_for(self, path)?;
        if !attempt.succeeded {
            return None;
        }
        let arguments: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(attempt.arguments.as_deref()?).ok()?;
        let frame = self.latest_attempt_for(Capability::Read, &arguments)?;
        if !frame.matches_receipt(attempt.tool.as_deref()?, &attempt.detail) {
            return None;
        }
        let index = self
            .qualified_attempts
            .iter()
            .position(|candidate| std::ptr::eq(candidate, frame))?;
        if self.qualified_attempts[index + 1..]
            .iter()
            .any(|candidate| {
                !candidate.has_receipt() && !read_only_capability(candidate.capability())
            })
        {
            return None;
        }
        attempt.source_observation().filter(|observed| {
            observed.error.is_none() && observed.complete && observed.source.is_some()
        })
    }
